/**
 * @description       : The one GA4 event list and the one way to send an event.
 *                      A component cannot see the page's window.gtag: on the site it reads as
 *                      undefined inside the component sandbox. So trackEvent dispatches a
 *                      cancelable portfolio-analytics event on the document with the name and
 *                      params, and the site's head script, which can see gtag, sends it and
 *                      cancels the event to say so. When no listener takes it (no head script,
 *                      Jest), trackEvent calls window.gtag directly if one is there. It does
 *                      nothing when neither is present and never throws, so analytics can never
 *                      break a component. New events are appended to EVENTS.
 *                      Every call also leaves a record in a short in page list for this visit: the
 *                      name, a copy of the params, the local time and how it went ("head_script",
 *                      "gtag" or "not_sent"). The list holds the last 100 and is gone on reload.
 *                      recentEvents() returns copies of it, and onAnalyticsEvent(listener) tells a
 *                      listener about each new record and returns a function that stops it. A
 *                      listener that throws is ignored. c/analyticsEvents shows the list.
 * @author            : Ryan Bumstead
 * @githubRepo        : https://github.com/rdbumstead

# Executive Overview

**Table of Contents**

- [1. Strategic Summary (Read This First)](#1-strategic-summary-read-this-first)
- [2. Strategic Intent](#2-strategic-intent)
- [3. Business Value: Why Build This Complexity?](#3-business-value-why-build-this-complexity)
  - [3.1 The "5-Minute Tour" User Journey](#31-the-5-minute-tour-user-journey)
- [4. Terminology & Acronyms](#4-terminology--acronyms)
- [5. Success Criteria (Definition of Done)](#5-success-criteria-definition-of-done)

---

Project: Salesforce Platform Architect Portfolio

Version: 1.0

Owner: Ryan Bumstead

Status: live since October 2026, with the static front end live since 2026-11-09

## 1. Strategic Summary (Read This First)

**The Problem:** Enterprise Salesforce implementations often go wrong in three quiet ways: costs nobody watches (FinOps), slow pages, and guest users who can see more than they should.

**The Solution:** This portfolio is a **zero budget architecture** built to enterprise habits. Its records live in a free Salesforce Developer Edition org, which stays the system of record. The public pages are static files on Cloudflare Pages, built from those records. The site calls the Gemini API through a Named Credential for cover letters, keeps every guest grant in one permission set in source, and shows its own limits on every page.

**The Outcome:** I moved the public front end of a Salesforce portfolio to static pages on Cloudflare Pages, built from the same Lightning Web Components, with Salesforce kept as the system of record. Production Lighthouse mobile LCP went from 7.5 to 10.6 s on Experience Cloud to 2.2 to 2.9 s on Cloudflare across six routes. Accessibility is held at 100 by a pull request gate. These are lab results (the median of three runs a route, audited on 2026-11-12), not Core Web Vitals field data. The tool, emulation and environment are in the [Technical Guide §2.11](./04-Technical-Guide.md#211-mobile-performance).

**Why It Matters:**

> [!TIP]
> **For Non-Salesforce Readers:** It shows that a fixed budget can be respected without giving up capability.

- **For Architects:** It demonstrates "Glass Box Telemetry". The footer reports each visit's own CPU, heap and SOQL use against their limits, the org's daily API and async Apex quotas, and the state of the AI, GitHub and Jira circuit breakers.
- **For Recruiters:** It is a living proof of work, with its mobile load time measured and published rather than claimed.

If you only inspect one thing, look at the **[Systems Architecture Specification (SAS)](./03-SAS.md)** to see the "North Star" diagram.

## 2. Strategic Intent

This Executive Overview sums up why the Salesforce Platform Architect Portfolio exists, what it is worth to the people who read it, and how to judge it. It is the entry point to the other guides. The scope and the plan live in the [Program Charter](./02-Program-Charter.md).

## 3. Business Value: Why Build This Complexity?

The primary problem this portfolio solves is that Recruiters and Hiring Managers struggle to verify an architect's hands-on skills through static PDFs.

- **The Need:** A verified, interactive demonstration of complex capabilities like API design, LWC, and AI.
- **The Value:** This system intentionally mirrors a real enterprise architecture so evaluators can see architecture quality, integration patterns and DevOps discipline, all within a controlled, demonstrable environment. It shows that "Enterprise Grade" is a way of working, not a license tier.

### 3.1 The "5-Minute Tour" User Journey

How a recruiter or architect experiences this portfolio. The tour has one stop per pillar, and each pillar in `c/pillarData` sets its own minutes (`tourMinutes`), so its length is their sum (`TOUR_MINUTES`), which the hero's tour button shows. On the way, each showcase component has a View source button. It opens a dialog with the component's JavaScript, HTML and main Apex class, highlighted by the shared Prism module, with a link to each file on GitHub. The files are listed in the Source File custom metadata, so they can change without a deploy. A scheduled job reads them from GitHub at most once a day per file into an admin only cache. Visitors read only the cache, never GitHub ([ADR-004 amendment](../adr/004-static-resource-code-rendering.md)):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Recruiter
    participant H as Home page
    participant A as A. Business Architecture
    participant B as B. Solution Architecture
    participant C as C. API Lab
    participant D as D. AI Lab
    participant E as E. Delivery
    participant S as View source

    R->>H: Lands on Portfolio
    H-->>R: "Take the 10 minute tour"
    R->>A: A process mapped to its live data model
    R->>B: The reasoning behind a platform choice
    R->>C: A real API call with its headers
    R->>D: A cover letter grounded in portfolio data
    R->>E: The Jira roadmap and the commits that shipped the site
    R->>S: Clicks "View source" on any showcase component
    S-->>R: Its real JavaScript, HTML and Apex, with links to GitHub
    Note over R,S: "This isn't just a PDF."
```

## 4. Terminology & Acronyms

To clarify Salesforce-specific terms used throughout this portfolio:

| Term                  | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| :-------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **LWR**               | **Lightning Web Runtime**. A high-performance, standards-based framework for building fast Salesforce sites.                                                                                                      |
| **SAPI**              | **System API**. The interface that directly touches the database/backend (Salesforce Core).                                                                                                                       |
| **PAPI**              | **Process API**. The layer that combines several portfolio objects into one response for a client, such as the full profile or the resume as text. It runs its own queries. Only its health check calls the SAPI. |
| **FORM_FACTOR**       | A Salesforce constant that automatically detects the user's device type (Large, Medium, Small).                                                                                                                   |
| **Developer Edition** | The free, zero-cost Salesforce environment used to host this portfolio.                                                                                                                                           |

## 5. Success Criteria (Definition of Done)

This project holds itself to functional and technical acceptance criteria. Two of them: performance, where the target is a 2.5 s mobile LCP and the production Lighthouse audit of 2026-11-12 measured route medians of 2.2 to 2.9 s (lab data, mobile emulation, three runs a route, environment in the [Technical Guide §2.11](./04-Technical-Guide.md#211-mobile-performance)), and code quality, where org wide Apex coverage must be 90% or more on every pull request. The Experience Cloud site measured 7.5 to 10.6 s before the front end moved, and those figures stay in the Technical Guide as history.

For the authoritative definition of all success metrics, quality gates, and "Definition of Done", please refer to the **[Program Charter: Success Criteria](./02-Program-Charter.md#22-success-criteria-definition-of-done)**.

ProjectCardController.getPillarCards.solution: A working Employer Hub demo built on Salesforce. Every inquiry is captured once from a web form, matched to the partner's account and routed by the employer's industry. Service requests are fulfilled from the case, and monetary requests run through an opportunity to a contract. Operations and executive dashboards report from the same records.
ProjectCardController.getPillarCards.challenge: Several departments at an education provider worked with the same employer partners, each from its own inbox and spreadsheet. Partners repeated themselves, and nobody could see the whole relationship. Leadership had no shared numbers for engagement, investment or hiring.
ProjectCardController.getPillarCards.businessValue: Designed so that employer partners get one front door and a faster answer, departments stop duplicating outreach and see each other's work with a partner, and leadership can report on the employer relationship as a whole.

ProjectCardController.getPillarCards.solution: A minimalist model on NPSP with the Program Management Module, sized for a staff with no full-time admin. Classes, sessions and attendance use the native program objects, with three small custom objects for assessments, employment and partner referrals. Fundraising and state filing stay in the systems that already do them.
ProjectCardController.getPillarCards.challenge: An adult literacy nonprofit with a small staff needed one platform for its classes, attendance and learner outcomes. Instructors and learners hold no licences, so only staff enter data. Donations and state reporting already run in other systems, so the platform had to fit around them.
ProjectCardController.getPillarCards.businessValue: Built so staff record classes, sessions and attendance in one place, learner outcomes sit on the learner's record ready for the state report, and the platform runs on free nonprofit licences and a model a small team can keep running. In user acceptance testing, preparing for production.

If traffic exceeded limits, the **Phase 8** design (Designed, nothing built) moves the heavy lifting (Resume Generation, API Gateway) to AWS Serverless equivalents, allowing the Salesforce Core to remain a lightweight orchestration layer. This ensures the system could handle enterprise-scale traffic with minimal refactoring. **Architecture Implementation Status (live since October 2026)** Live MVP (Door 1) - `@AuraEnabled` Apex controllers, the main path for site components (resume and timeline, home case studies and pillar cards, footer, Delivery page, ERD, decision matrix, API Lab and cover letter) - Native Salesforce GraphQL through the `lightning/uiGraphQLApi` wire adapter, used by three components only: `c-skill-network`, `c-project-asset-gallery-data` (the lazy child of `c-project-asset-gallery`) and the footer's `c-graphql-probe` ([ADR-021 amendments](../adr/021-native-graphql-door-1-vs-apex-rest-for-ui.md#amendment-2026-10-30-the-galleries-read-moved-to-a-lazy-child)) - Apex REST services (the SAPI and PAPI), for outside callers and the API Lab - Direct integrations (GitHub, Jira via Named Credentials) Phase 8, 2027-2028 (Designed) | Phase | Status | Rationale | | :---------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Phase 8** | **Designed, 2027-2028** | Architected to prove "Scale Up" capability, and left out of the MVP. Nothing of it is built. | - AWS Lambda Polyglot Gateway (Function URL), "Door 2" - Enterprise API governance layer - Resume Engine offload ### 1.2 Architecture at a Glance > [!NOTE] > **Per host, as of 2026-11-12.** The public front end is the static build on Cloudflare Pages, live at `ryanbumstead.com` since the cutover on 2026-11-09. The diagrams and lists in sections 1 to 5 mostly describe the Salesforce (Experience Cloud) site, which the static build replaced and which stays up until 2026-11-23 as the rollback target. Salesforce stays the system of record for both. Section 6.3 draws the static build and [Technical Guide §2.25](./04-Technical-Guide.md#225-the-static-build-and-the-shims) lists the differences. Where a sentence below is true of only one host, it says so. 10-second overview for executive stakeholders. ```mermaid graph TD %%{init: {'flowchart': {'nodeSpacing': 50, 'rankSpacing': 50}}}%% %% ========= STYLES ========= classDef client fill:#E8F5E9,stroke:#2E7D32,stroke-width:3px,color:#1B5E20,font-weight:bold; classDef sfdc fill:#E3F2FD,stroke:#1976D2,stroke-width:3px,color:#0D47A1,font-weight:bold; classDef external fill:#FFF3E0,stroke:#FB8C00,stroke-width:3px,color:#E65100,font-weight:bold; classDef data fill:#F3E5F5,stroke:#8E24AA,stroke-width:2px,color:#4A148C; %% ========= LAYERS ========= Browser --> LWR LWR --> Apex Apex --> DB Apex --> AI Apex --> Jira Apex --> GitHub %% ========= APPLY STYLES ========= class Browser,LWR client; class Apex,AI sfdc; class DB data; class Jira,GitHub external; %% ========= CRITICAL PATH ========= linkStyle 0,1,2 stroke:#2E7D32,stroke-width:4px; ``` ### 1.3 Key Salesforce Features Used - **Experience Cloud (LWR):** High-performance, pixel-perfect frontend. - **Apex REST Services:** Custom API layer for external integrations. - **Custom Metadata Types:** Configuration management. - **Generative AI:** one Apex dispatch (`ContentGenerationController.dispatch`) over Agentforce (a Prompt Builder template), Gemini 2.5 Flash through the Gemini API and a local template. The site reaches Agentforce through `POST /papi/ai/generate` and runs Gemini and the template in process (section 5.4). - **Package directories:** the source is split into five package directories in `sfdx-project.json` and deployed as source. No email, phone or address reaches the site. - **Scalability:** Data model supports 10,000+ records via indexed Junction Objects. ### 2.2 Platform Constraints (Developer Edition) The architecture is designed to operate within the specific limits of the Salesforce Developer Edition. - **Storage Limits:** 5MB Data Storage / 20MB File Storage limit requires strict data hygiene. Images ship as static resources, and cleanup batches keep the cache and rate window objects small. Off-platform storage in AWS is Designed only. - **API Limits:** 15,000 API requests/24hr requires caching strategies for high-traffic external integrations. - **Guest User:** the guest gets no object permission on standard objects, so the portfolio data lives in a custom schema, and the few standard records a page needs are read by Apex in system mode (section 4.6). - **No Shield:** Lack of Event Monitoring requires custom telemetry implementation for analytics. - **Middleware Constraints:** Heroku and paid AWS resources are unavailable. The AWS Free Tier proxy and storage patterns are a Phase 8 design and are Designed only. Risk & Security Architecture ### 3.1 Threat Model Summary - **Injection Attacks:** Mitigated by strict SOQL bind variable usage. - **Data Exposure:** Mitigated by one guest permission set (`Portfolio_Guest`) with read on six portfolio objects and create and read on `Testimonial__c`, sharing rules for the guest on `Project__c`, `Experience__c`, `Skill__c` and `Testimonial__c`, and a restriction rule that hides unapproved testimonials. The guest has no Lead access: the contact form's Lead is saved by a platform event trigger as the Automated Process user ([ADR-031](../adr/031-native-contact-form.md)). No visitor IP is used, because Apex cannot read one in a guest request. Records the guest cannot read are reached only through `without sharing` Apex selectors with fixed field lists (section 4.6). - **API Abuse:** Mitigated by read-only endpoints and hardcoded query limits in the SAPI layer. - **Service Unavailability (AI):** Mitigated by the Strategy Pattern ([ADR-015](../adr/015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md)): a cover letter falls back from Agentforce to the Gemini API and then to a deterministic Local Template built from the records. Agentforce is held to an hourly budget under the Developer Edition's cap of 150 generations an hour ([ADR-015 amendment of 2026-10-26](../adr/015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md#amendment-2026-10-26-agentforce-is-built-and-the-deferral-is-lifted)). ### 3.2 How a guest reaches Apex > [!NOTE] > **Per host, as of 2026-11-02.** This section describes the Salesforce site. On the static site a visitor's browser never calls Apex as the guest. The pages carry data read at build time by the build user, and a request time feature goes through a Pages Function that calls Salesforce as the edge user (section 4.6.1). The guest permission set stays in force for the Salesforce site and is the baseline the build user's export is tested against. Nobody logs in to this site. Every visitor is the Experience Cloud site's guest user, so everything a visitor sees comes through five steps, each granted on purpose. 1. **A component calls a method.** A Lightning Web Component imports an `@AuraEnabled` method, for example `getResume` from `ResumeController`, and wires or calls it. Reads are marked `cacheable=true`. 2. **The guest may run only 16 classes.** The `Portfolio_Guest` permission set lists them, among them `ResumeController`, `ProjectCardController`, `SkillGraphController`, `FooterController`, `ContactFormController`, `TestimonialController` and `ApiLabController`. Any other class refuses a guest even if its method is `@AuraEnabled`. 3. **The controller is the boundary.** Each method returns a fixed shape built for the page, never a raw record. Its reads run through `QueryDefinitions` ([ADR-033](../adr/033-queries-in-custom-metadata.md)), and most of them run in system mode inside a small private `without sharing` selector, because the data sits on objects the guest has no access to (roles look up to Account, certifications and education are children of Contact). Each selector names its fields and selects no email, phone, address or owner field, so system mode widens what the controller can read, never what the visitor gets. `ResumeController.ResumeSelector` is the pattern. 4. **Where the guest reads records directly, the guest's own access applies.** The project gallery and the skills graph read through the UI API GraphQL adapter, so the guest needs its own permission and record access: `Portfolio_Guest` grants read on six portfolio objects and create and read on `Testimonial__c`, sharing rules for the guest open `Project__c`, `Experience__c`, `Skill__c` and `Testimonial__c` read only, and the restriction rule `Block_Unapproved_Testimonials` hides any testimonial that is not approved ([ADR-012](../adr/012-guest-user-security-restriction-rules.md)). The two testimonial reads run in user mode, so that rule applies to them too. 5. **Writes and shared state go through narrow stores.** Counters, rate windows, circuit breakers, caches and audit rows live in small `without sharing` classes that each touch one object and return only what the page shows, such as a count or a cached feed. The contact form's Lead is saved by a platform event trigger, never by the guest. The API Lab calls the REST API through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential as the integration user, whose `Integration_Access` permission set is read only ([ADR-027](../adr/027-platform-native-api-authentication.md)). So the guest can run 16 classes and read what sharing allows, and anything wider happens inside a class that decides exactly what leaves it. ## 4. The model is never asked to reveal its own prompt, because that is unreliable and invites prompt injection. #### 5.4.1 Feature Spotlight: Generative Cover Letter Engine > [!NOTE] > **Per host, as of 2026-11-02.** The sequence and the steps below are the Salesforce site's, where the page calls `ApiLabController` as the guest. On the static site the page posts to the `cover-letter` function, which calls the site actions endpoint as the edge user, and the same Apex chain runs from there. A `recorded` switch shows a labelled sample letter and calls nothing. > [!IMPORTANT] > **As built, the cover letter page is written by Agentforce through the API, or by Gemini 2.5 Flash through the Gemini API when Agentforce gives no letter, or by the local template when both fail.** A letter is attributed to the provider that wrote it ([ADR-015 amendment of 2026-10-26](../adr/015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md#amendment-2026-10-26-agentforce-is-built-and-the-deferral-is-lifted)). - **The Concept:** Instead of a static "About Me," recruiters enter a company name, a job title and, optionally, the job description. The system writes a cover letter explaining why this candidate fits that role. - **The Architecture as built:** - **Input Layer:** the LWC form `c-cover-letter-generator` calls `ApiLabController.generateCoverLetter`, which checks the AI tier limit on the key `papi-ai:site-cover-letter` (10 requests per minute, one bucket shared by every site visitor). While the Agentforce switch is on and its breaker is closed, it first posts the letter to `/papi/ai/generate` with `provider` set to `Agentforce` through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential, so the template runs as the integration user, because a guest may not run generative AI. A 200 is the letter. Anything else runs `ContentGenerationController.dispatch` in process as the site guest, from Gemini on, then the template, and the count is written afterwards. The guest holds the `Gemini_Auth-Gemini_Principal` principal for Gemini and no other AI grant. Gemini is never asked through the API, because a request that arrives as a callout from the same org may not call out again, so Gemini could never answer it ([ADR-015 amendment on the in process dispatch](../adr/015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md#amendment-2026-10-21-the-site-cover-letter-dispatches-in-process)). `/papi/ai/generate` also serves outside callers. - **Retrieval Layer:** `PortfolioGroundingService` reads featured `Project__c` records (name, challenge, solution, business value, skills) and `Experience_Highlight__c` text with its role and employer, ranks them by keywords from the job title and description, and adds them to the prompt as JSON. It never selects Email, Phone or an owner field, strips anything shaped like an email address or phone number, and stays under 8,000 characters. Its reads go through a `without sharing` selector with a fixed field list, because the site guest sees only rows shared to it. This is direct CRM retrieval in Apex. No Data 360 index exists (section 5.4). - **Prompt Layer:** `ContentGenerationController.coverLetterPrompt` builds the one cover letter prompt for both cover letter paths: the instruction from the `AI_Prompt__mdt` record `Cover_Letter` (the same text in code as the fallback), a word limit line, 250 to 350 words from two settings with 350 as a hard maximum, plus a fixed shape of five paragraphs (an opening of two sentences, three body paragraphs of three sentences each, a closing of two sentences), the job, the persona (Architect, Engineer, Consultant or Admin, where Admin stays internal) inferred from the job, and the grounding. Highlights tagged with that persona rank first. Email and phone shapes are removed from the visitor's text. The letter is never cut. - **Generation Layer:** `ContentGenerationController.dispatch`, described below. Agentforce runs a template that adds one line holding the letter to the prompt's word range, on the model `sfdc_ai__DefaultGPT41`. Every Gemini request sends a `generationConfig` with the output token limit and the temperature from two settings. - **Header:** every letter opens with my header and the profile links shared with the resume (LinkedIn, GitHub, Trailhead, Portfolio and Contact last). - **Show your work:** the page shows the whole letter with its word count beside the badge, which shows the provider and model from the response. A panel the visitor opens shows whether a fallback happened, the round trip and generation time, every attempt and the prompt that was sent. **Generation strategy as built.** Providers implement `IAIGenerationService` (`generateContent`, `isAvailable`). One dispatch method, `ContentGenerationController.dispatch`, serves both `PAPIAiGenerate.generate` and the page (in process, as the guest): | Order | Provider | Consulted when | Result today | | :---------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | First | Agentforce (`AgentforceService`) | The `Agentforce` record of `AI_Provider_Config__mdt` has `Enabled__c` set, the running user is not a site guest, its breaker is closed and the hourly budget is not used. The site reaches it through the API | The letter, within a 20 second timeout capped to fit the 120 seconds a transaction may spend on callouts. Past `Hourly_Budget__c` (120 per UTC hour) the attempt is `budget_exhausted` | | Second | Gemini 2.5 Flash (`gemini-2.5-flash`, the model on the `Gemini` record) through the Gemini API (`GeminiService`) | Unless the `gemini` circuit breaker is open | The letter, within a 60 second callout timeout. A reasoning model can use most of it, and Flash answered in about 11 seconds in a scratch org | | Last resort | Local Template (`LocalTemplateService`) | Cover letters only | A letter built in Apex from the records with no model, saying so in its last line. Other types answer 503 `ALL_PROVIDERS_UNAVAILABLE` | Every attempt is recorded with its outcome (`served`, `skipped_off`, `skipped_open_circuit`, `budget_exhausted`, `failed`), its time and, on a failure, a short `detail` (an HTTP status or the exception type, never a key), and the API returns them as `attempts` beside `provider`, `model`, `fallbackOccurred`, `latencyMs` and `promptShown`. Three failures in a row open that provider's circuit breaker (`CircuitBreaker`, keys `gemini` and `agentforce`) for 30 minutes, and the provider is skipped until the next try succeeds. A 429 or a 401 never counts as an Agentforce failure. Breaker state is written after every provider has been tried, never before a callout. `GeminiService.generateContent` reports a failure as text starting `Error: Unable to generate content.` or `Exception: `, which the dispatch treats as a failed attempt. **Sequence diagram** > _What This Diagram Shows: a cover letter from the site page as built. Agentforce is asked through the API, then Gemini and the template run in process._ ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Page as c-cover-letter-generator participant Lab as ApiLabController (guest) participant Limiter as RateWindowLimiter (papi-ai) participant Grounding as Grounding selector (without sharing) participant API as POST /papi/ai/generate (integration user) participant Agent as AgentforceService (Prompt Builder template) participant Dispatcher as ContentGenerationController participant Gemini as GeminiService (gemini-2.5-flash) participant Local as LocalTemplateService Page->>Lab: generateCoverLetter(company, title, description) Lab->>Limiter: checkKey(AI tier key) alt Over 10 a minute Limiter-->>Lab: refused Lab-->>Page: rate limit message else Allowed Lab->>Grounding: featured projects and highlights Grounding-->>Lab: PII-free JSON Lab->>API: provider Agentforce (20 s, one callout) API->>Agent: dispatch(request) alt Letter returned Agent-->>API: content API-->>Lab: 200 and the letter else Off, open breaker, budget used, error or timeout API-->>Lab: no letter Lab->>Dispatcher: dispatch(request) in process Dispatcher->>Gemini: generateContent() (one callout, 60 s) alt Usable text Gemini-->>Dispatcher: content else Error text, exception or timeout Gemini-->>Dispatcher: failure Dispatcher->>Local: generateContent() Local-->>Dispatcher: template text end Dispatcher-->>Lab: GenerationResult (provider, model, attempts, promptShown) end Lab->>Limiter: commitRateCounts() Lab-->>Page: CoverLetterResult (badge and panel read from it) end ``` - **Privacy:** Inputs are processed transiently and never stored in Salesforce. The prompt shown to the visitor holds only what they typed and public portfolio facts. #### 5.4.2 Optional Edge Layer Integration (Designed) Cloudflare Workers provides a fourth path for content generation. The trigger upserts `Pipeline_Run__c` by `Run_Key__c`, so a replayed event changes nothing. The component reads `GovernanceController.getPipelineStatus()` when the page is viewed and again when the tab becomes visible. There is no timer and no polling. Each item shows its evidence (the commit linking to the run, and the time), and an item with no data shows "No signal yet". A third workflow, the Live Smoke Test that runs after every deploy that changed production, publishes only on a failure, as workflow `smoke`. The checklist does not read those rows ([ADR-019 amendment](../adr/019-executable-governance-platform-events-for-documentation-logic.md#amendment-2026-10-23)). - **Page text:** the Delivery page's introduction describes this in the present tense: after every production deploy and every daily heartbeat the pipeline publishes the result, passed or failed, and the checklist says so when a run failed or is out of date (`sfdc_cms__view/Delivery/content.json`). - **Times:** each time shows in UTC and then in the visitor's own time and zone. - **What it claims:** the production deploy is green, the org heartbeat ran today (within 26 hours, the `Heartbeat_Stale_Hours` setting), and the integration caches are under 30 minutes old (`Governance_Cache_Minutes`). - **Why no browser subscription:** `lightning-emp-api` is unsupported in LWR sites, and each subscribed browser would count against the org's 20 concurrent streaming clients. The event-driven part is server-side: publish, an asynchronous subscriber and idempotent handling of a replayed event. - **Roadmap and changelog:** `c-roadmap-viewer` and `c-changelog` read cached Jira and GitHub data through `DeliveryController` (cacheable Apex). Scheduled Queueable jobs refresh the caches every 15 minutes, so a visitor never triggers a callout ([ADR-007 amendment of 2026-10-21](../adr/007-github-api-server-side-caching.md#amendment-2026-10-21-the-cache-objects-and-the-scheduled-refresh)). The roadmap shows only `SPAP` issues labelled `portfolio-roadmap`. The site's CDN caching of guest Apex stays off (my decision), so every visit reads the org. - **By the numbers:** the panel after the page's intro, with counts read from records: the deploys recorded with the newest deploy's Apex and Jest test counts and coverage, the evaluator tokens issued, the cover letters written and the API Lab requests sent, and the testimonials approved by vibe once one is approved. Only counts reach the guest ([Technical Guide §2.19](./04-Technical-Guide.md#219-by-the-numbers-c-by-the-numbers)). - **Architectural Signal:** event-driven architecture with a server-side subscriber, and external system integration through Named Credentials. #### 5.5.1 The Governance Model For the detailed "Three-Gate Approval Process" (Technical Feasibility, Security, DoR) governing these pillars, refer to **[Guardrails & Executable Governance: The Three-Gate Approval Process](./06-Guardrails-and-Executable-Governance.md#6-the-three-gate-approval-process)**. - Acceptance criteria defined (Gherkin syntax preferred). - Test data generation script written. - Rollback plan documented (Section 9.X). ## 6. Contingency & Rollback Plans ### 8.1 Deployment Failure - **Symptom:** GitHub Actions deploy.yml job fails or turns red. - **Detection:** Automated email notification from GitHub Actions, and the run's step summary ("Deployment Status" in `deploy.yml`) reports the failure. - **Mitigation:** 1. Check GitHub Action logs for the specific metadata error. The GlassOps validate, gate, deploy and verify steps each say which one stopped the run. 2. A failed validate, gate or deploy leaves the `glassops/deployed/prod` tag where it was, so the next merge or a hand run of Deploy to Production in delta mode plans the same change again. A deploy that verify then fails has moved the tag, because production changed, so the next run does not redeploy those components. Fix forward with a new commit or use full mode. The API reserve check can also stop a run before anything is sent, and then a hand run in delta mode later does it. 3. If GlassOps cannot run: use the hand run full or destructive mode, which deploys with raw `sf` commands ([Maintenance Guide §3.13](./05-Maintenance-Guide.md#313-operating-the-glassops-production-deploy)). - **Detection:** Automated email notification from GitHub Actions. - **Rollback:** See **[Maintenance & Operations Guide: Disaster Recovery](./05-Maintenance-Guide.md#4-disaster-recovery)** for the definitive rollback procedure. ### 8.2 Agentforce Unavailable > [!NOTE] > The Agentforce provider is a Prompt Builder template and its switch ships on ([ADR-015 amendment of 2026-10-26](../adr/015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md#amendment-2026-10-26-agentforce-is-built-and-the-deferral-is-lifted)). Document as "Platform Limit" in the footer. ### 8.3 API Rate Limit Exhaustion - **Symptom:** GitHub Commits or Portfolio API returns status 429. - **Mitigation (GitHub):** guests never call GitHub. The changelog serves the newest `Github_Cache__c` row (a custom object) with its age, and a failed refresh inserts nothing, so the last good list stays until the next refresh succeeds. - **Mitigation (Portfolio API):** the 429 comes from `RateWindowLimiter` (SAPI 120, PAPI 15, `/ai/*` 10 requests per minute per caller key). The platform rejects unauthenticated calls before Apex executes. See [ADR-027](../adr/027-platform-native-api-authentication.md) and [B.5](#b5-authentication--evaluator-access). **Key Design Principles:** - **Zero Trust Architecture:** All endpoints require a Bearer token minted by the External Client App; authorisation is bounded by the integration user's single read-only permission set. The guest user holds no execute access on any SAPI class - **Distributed Tracing:** Mandatory `X-Request-Id` header (UUID format) in all requests for correlation across log aggregation systems - **Contract-First Design:** OpenAPI 3.0 specification defines the interface before implementation - **Explicit Caching:** `Cache-Control` headers distinguish between cacheable configuration (`max-age=300`) and dynamic data (`no-store`) - **Rate Limiting:** `RateWindowLimiter` allows 120 requests per minute per caller key, with no burst allowance. Every evaluator token is the same session, so all evaluators share that one limit ([ADR-028 amendment on the shared token pool](../adr/028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md#amendment-2026-10-21-a-shared-token-pool-no-expiry-no-disposable-list)) - **Versioning:** `X-API-Version` is optional and selects the contract ([ADR-039](../adr/039-api-v2-and-the-v1-sunset.md)). A request without it is served as `v1`, which is deprecated. `v2` returns public keys only. The value is matched without regard to letter case, so `V2` works. Any other value gets 400 with a message that says to send v1 or v2, and every response Apex writes carries `X-API-Version` in lower case with the version served and `Vary: X-API-Version`. The version and sunset checks run before the rate limiter, so a request they refuse spends none of the rate limit quota (`ApiRequestContext.applyRequestRules`, `SUPPORTED_VERSION`, `VERSION_2`) - **Versionless URLs:** the URL names the resource and the header names the version ([ADR-040](../adr/040-versionless-api-urls.md)). `SAPIRouter` (`/sapi/*`) and `PAPIRouter` (`/papi/*`) read the first route segment and call the existing handler class for the verb. The 23 handler classes keep their `/v1/` mappings, and Apex REST picks the most specific `urlMapping`, so the old `/v1/` URLs are aliases that reach the same code. `ApiRequestContext.canonicalPath` turns either spelling into one versionless path for the exemptions, shaping, the rate tier and the log line. An unknown route is 404 and a verb a route lacks is 405, both in the error envelope. A caller with no token gets 401 with the site's token URL in the message. The `Api_Versionless_Urls` setting (shipped `On`) is the rollback switch: Off, the routers answer 404 naming the `/v1/` URL and every caller we own uses the `/v1/` URLs, with no deploy - **v2 shape:** on the record endpoints, no `id`, no `xId` that has an `xKey` beside it, and no `accomplishments` (`SAPITransformer.toV2`, which `PAPITransformer.toV2` calls). The token, health, AI generate, resume generate and portfolio config bodies are not shaped. The filters are `projectKey`, `experienceKey` and `certificationKey`, each a public key only. An Id there gets 400 " must be a public key.", and an old `*Id` name gets 400 "Use projectKey in v2.". The `/projects/{id}` path takes a key and answers 404 for anything else - **v1 deprecation and sunset:** every v1 response carries `Link` with `rel="successor-version"` to `https://ryanbumstead.com/api-lab/reference?version=v2`, `Deprecation` (RFC 9745) once `Api_V1_Deprecation_Date` is set and `Sunset` (RFC 8594) once `Api_V1_Sunset_Date` is set. From 00:00 UTC on the sunset date every v1 call, with or without the header, gets 410 with `errorCode` `GONE`, except `POST /papi/auth/token`, `/sapi/health` and `/papi/health`. They keep their deprecation headers and are answered normally, so a client can still get a token and check that the API is up. Run `POST /auth/token` first: it stores the token and instance URL for the other requests #### B.5 Authentication & Evaluator Access Authentication is platform-native on both sides of the API boundary ([ADR-027](../adr/027-platform-native-api-authentication.md)); external reviewers obtain short-lived tokens through a vending endpoint ([ADR-028](../adr/028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md)). | Side | Construct | Role | | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Provider (inbound)** | External Client App, OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow | Issues Bearer tokens; runs API calls as a dedicated integration user holding only `Integration_Access` (read-only) | | **Consumer (outbound)** | External Credential (Client Credentials principal) + `Portfolio_API` Named Credential | Holds the consumer key/secret in the platform vault; used by the API Lab proxy and the PAPI health check | | **Evaluator** | `POST /papi/auth/token` (`PAPIAuthToken`) + `Portfolio_API_Token` Named Credential | Only REST class the guest user may execute; `TokenExchangeService` performs the exchange server-side with the `Portfolio_API_Token_Auth` principal's `Client_Id` and `Client_Secret` and returns a short-lived token | > _What this diagram shows: the three ways a request reaches the APIs. The secret never leaves the org; the only thing that crosses the browser boundary is an expiring Bearer token._ ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Reviewer as External Reviewer (curl) participant LWC as c-api-tester (Guest) participant Proxy as ApiLabController / PAPIAuthToken participant NC as Portfolio_API or Portfolio_API_Token Named Credential participant ECA as External Client App (token endpoint) participant API as SAPI / PAPI (Apex REST, run-as Integration User) LWC->>Proxy: invoke(path) Proxy->>NC: callout NC->>ECA: client_credentials (secret from vault) ECA-->>NC: access_token NC->>API: GET /sapi/... Bearer token API-->>LWC: payload + X-Request-Id + X-RateLimit-* Reviewer->>Proxy: POST /auth/token {email, purpose} Proxy->>NC: client_credentials exchange NC-->>Reviewer: {access_token, instance_url} Reviewer->>API: GET /sapi/skills Bearer token API-->>Reviewer: payload ``` **Controls (in order of importance):** 1. **Least privilege:** a client-credentials token is valid for any REST API as the integration user, so the integration user's permission set is the real boundary: read-only on portfolio objects, execute on SAPI/PAPI classes, nothing else. 2. **Expiry:** every evaluator token is the integration user's one shared session, which ends after 30 minutes without use (the profile's idle timeout). The token response carries no `expires_in`, because the token endpoint reports no expiry. 3. **Kill switch:** deactivating the External Client App revokes every outstanding token. 4. **Quota protection:** rate limiting by `RateWindowLimiter` ([ADR-025](../adr/025-papi-fan-out-throttling-capacity-planning.md#amendment-2026-10-21)), shared by every evaluator because every vended token is the same session ([ADR-028 amendment on the shared token pool](../adr/028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md#amendment-2026-10-21-a-shared-token-pool-no-expiry-no-disposable-list)), 15 token requests per minute per email and source IP, and a daily cap on issued tokens (`Token_Daily_Cap__c`, default 50) guard the Developer Edition API request limit (15,000/day). 5. **Audit:** every token request writes an `API_Access_Request__c` record. **Evaluator flow:** The token request goes to the Experience Cloud site domain, where Apex REST is served to the guest user under `/portfoliovforcesite/services/apexrest/`. Every other call goes to My Domain, at the `instance_url` returned with the token. [`scripts/api-smoke.sh`](../../scripts/api-smoke.sh) runs the whole flow against every GET path in both specifications. ```bash # 1. Request a token (no credentials required) curl -s -X POST "https://ryan-bumstead-dev-ed.develop.my.site.com/portfoliovforcesite/services/apexrest/papi/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Request-Id: $(uuidgen)" \ -d '{"email":"","purpose":"Evaluating API design"}' # 2. Call any endpoint on the returned instance_url with the returned token curl -s "/services/apexrest/sapi/skills?limit=5" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " -H "X-API-Version: v2" -H "X-Request-Id: $(uuidgen)" ``` ```bash # Or run every GET path and print status and key headers per path EVALUATOR_EMAIL="" EVALUATOR_PURPOSE="Evaluating API design" ./scripts/api-smoke.sh ``` **Correlation id on live responses.** The platform echoes a caller-supplied `X-Request-Id` exactly once, on My Domain and on the site domain (site domain observed in an integration scratch org, including on an Apex 503), and Apex does not set it again (`ApiRequestContext.applyRequestRules`). With no `X-Request-Id`, the platform returns its own 32-character hex id (no dashes) on responses it generates before Apex runs, such as a 401. On My Domain the platform also injects that id into the request when the caller sends none. The first live smoke found PAPI then answered 400 with two ids. Since 2026-10-21, PAPI treats a 32-character hex id as missing, generates a UUID as its correlation id, and adds no header of its own (`ApiRequestContext.applyRequestRules`, my decision). The response should then carry one id, the platform's, while an error body's `correlationId` carries the UUID. I have not yet checked this against a live response, and the next live smoke will. SAPI still requires a UUID. Send your own UUID to get a single, predictable id back. ### Appendix C: MuleSoft Code, Governance, & Proxy Configuration (Reference) > [!NOTE] > This architecture represents the "Ideal Enterprise State" designed during the Anypoint Platform trial period (November 2025). On the skills page the graph's SVG is `aria-hidden` and a visually hidden list names every node and its connections, so its length equals the node count. On the Pillar A page the object list mirrors every node and edge, and on phones it is the visible view. The skills matrix itself is native buttons (`aria-pressed`) in rows by category. - **G.2 Motion Sensitivity:** the graphs never move on their own: the d3-force layout runs to completion before anything is drawn. The view eases for about 250 ms only after the visitor presses Fit, Reset layout, Zoom in or Zoom out, and moves at once under "reduce motion". The site has no motion button: the smooth scrolls, the menus, the count up on the numbers panel, the case study and tour openings and the timeline's reveal follow the visitor's system "reduce motion" setting alone (`c/motionPreference`). - **G.3 Keyboard Navigation:** the header's links, theme button and Back to top arrow, the footer's reading chips and Back to top, and the testimonial vibe switch are at least 44 px high (`--pf-control-height`, 2026-11-15), the target every control on the site is held to. The "Matrix | Graph" switch is two 44 px buttons in a labelled group. Skill chips, the ERD's object list, the scope toggle and the gallery links are reachable by keyboard. The site layout renders a "Skip to content" link as the first stop on every route, and it moves focus to the page's `main` landmark. - **G.4 Decision matrix:** a table with a caption, `scope` on every header, and a labelled range slider per criterion ("Weight for" and the criterion, 0 to 10). The ranking and the sensitivity line are text, not colour. - **G.5 Compliance Checklist:** WCAG 2.1 AA is the target. Lighthouse and axe cover the automated checks only, and a Lighthouse score of 100 does not establish conformance, so I do not claim it. G.6 lists what the manual audit found. - **G.6 Fixes of 2026-10-30, from the audit of 2026-10-29.** The audit ran axe on the 12 page routes at 1400 and 390 px, forty Tab stops each, and found these gaps. Each fix is built and covered by Jest tests. I reran the audit on a scratch copy of the fixed code on 2026-10-30. axe found no A or AA violations on the 24 route and width pairs, every page has one `main` landmark with the skip link as its first Tab stop, opening a document on `/docs` moves focus to its heading, and the API reference has one level 1 heading and no skipped level (31 before). The contrast of text over gradients and overlaps is still undecided (axe could not compute it), so I do not read zero axe violations as a pass. - **Landmark and skip link.** `c-portfolio-theme-layout` renders its content region as a `main` and puts a skip to content link before the header, so a keyboard visitor no longer passes eight header stops on every page (WCAG 1.3.1, 2.4.1). - **API reference.** `c-api-reference` rings the Redoc controls that had no visible focus (Expand all, Collapse all, Copy and the toggles), gives each permalink anchor the name of its heading in place of a URL fragment, and orders Redoc's headings under the page's `h1` by setting `aria-level` (WCAG 2.4.7, 2.4.6, 1.3.1). - **Docs.** `c-docs-viewer` moves focus to the document heading when a document opens or the list returns, and announces "{title} opened" or "Document list" in a live region (WCAG 2.4.3, 4.1.3). A deep link to a heading keeps focusing that heading. - **Live data marker.** The marker's button has `aria-controls` pointing at its panel. - **Checks for a person.** With NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on iPhone: the landmarks list on each page (expect banner, navigation, main, contentinfo), the headings list on `/api-lab/reference`, where the cursor lands and what is spoken when a document opens on `/docs`, the status read after Execute GET in the API Lab, the name of each image link on `/business-architecture`, and the contrast of the hero meta line and page eyebrows in both themes with the Colour Contrast Analyser. Apex → Named Credential → External APIs (Jira/GitHub). **Static front end ([Live](./cutover-runbook.md) since 2026-11-09, [ADR-041](../adr/041-headless-static-front-end-on-cloudflare-pages.md)).** Browser → Cloudflare Pages (static files) for the pages. GitHub Actions (`site.yml`) → My Domain `/services/apexrest/site/export` → Cloudflare Pages for the build. Section 6.3 draws the flow. ### Appendix I: Org & Package Structure A monorepo of five package directories, declared in `sfdx-project.json` and deployed as source (`sf project deploy start --source-dir packages`, or a delta manifest). They are not packaged as unlocked packages: the project has no `packageAliases`, and the declared dependencies form a cycle, because `portfolio-site` declares `integration-api` while `integration-api` calls `ContentGenerationController` in `portfolio-site` (`PAPIAiGenerate`, `ApiLabController`). Packaging them would first need that cycle broken. - `/packages/portfolio-site`: Configurations, declarative, and programmatic resources focused on adding features to the Salesforce Architect Portfolio. Every pillar component and class lives here too (`SchemaService`, `DecisionMatrixController`, `c-schema-visualizer`, `c-project-asset-gallery`, `c-decision-matrix`, `c-pillar-b-story`), because Jest runs only on this package. - `/packages/integration-api`: the OpenAPI specifications (`specs/`), the Apex REST classes for the SAPI and PAPI, and the integration user's profile. - `/packages/shared-modules`: a placeholder for modules shared across packages. Today it holds only `main/default/lwc/jsconfig.json`, and no component lives there. - `/packages/demos/employer-hub`: the inert Employer Hub data model of a demonstration built for an education provider: `EH_Partner_Engagement__c`, `EH_Job_Posting__c` (master-detail to Partner Engagement), `EH_Partner_Investment__c` and `EH_Endorsement_Request__c`, with lookups to Account, Contact, Case, Opportunity and Contract, and the Account picklist `EH_Industry_Sector__c`, which picks the queue a request goes to. No automation, tabs, layouts or records. Also the `EH_Demo_Read` permission set (read on the four objects, optional for administrators) and the `EH_Assets` static resource (two process flows and two dashboards, redrawn from the original demo with no names and sample values). - `/packages/demos/nonprofit-literacy`: the analysis of a platform choice for an adult literacy nonprofit: the three decision matrix Custom Metadata Types (`Decision_Option__mdt`, `Decision_Criterion__mdt`, `Decision_Score__mdt`), their 43 records, and the `NL_Assets` static resource with the redrawn object model. It references no managed package, so it deploys to production and to CI's scratch orgs unchanged. ### Appendix J: Cloud FinOps Strategy (Phase 8 - 2027-2028) - **FinOps Strategy:** Refer to **[Guardrails & Executable Governance: AWS FinOps & Serverless Guardrails](./06-Guardrails-and-Executable-Governance.md#3-aws-finops--serverless-guardrails-phase-8)** for the detailed cost governance model ($0.00 Forever architecture). ### Appendix K: Validation Rules & Logic - **K.1 `Experience__c`:** one validation rule, `End_Date_Validation`: a role cannot have an end date while `Is_Current_Role__c` is checked. Project: Salesforce Platform Architect Portfolio

Version: 1.0

Owner: Ryan Bumstead

Status: live since October 2026, with the static front end live since 2026-11-09

## 1. Executive Summary

### 1.1 Purpose of This Document

This Program Charter sets out the scope, the success criteria and the delivery plan for the Salesforce Platform Architect Portfolio. It is the reference for what is in scope, how success is judged and which milestones remain. Where it lists work still to come, it says so.

### 1.2 Strategic Intent: The Value: A Living Enterprise System

This is not a static website. It is a live, observable platform governed by production constraints. It demonstrates "Enterprise Grade" as a way of working through:

- **Glass Box Telemetry:** on every visit, the footer shows that request's governor limit use (heap, CPU, SOQL), the org's daily API request and async Apex quotas, and the AI, GitHub and Jira circuit breakers, which shows FinOps and multi-tenant awareness.
- **Dynamic Architecture:** an Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) drawn from the org's own schema when the page opens, not a static image.
- **Executable Governance:** a checklist on the Delivery page that ticks its own items from pipeline records (for example "production deploy green", with the commit and the run behind it).
- **Resilience Simulation:** a "Simulate an outage" switch on each Delivery page feed re-reads that feed as if GitHub or Jira were down, so a visitor sees the cached data come back marked as simulated ([ADR-022](../adr/022-resilience-engineering-resilience-simulation-toggle.md)).

### 1.3 Current vs. Target Architecture Scope

#### Current MVP State (live since October 2026)

- All data comes from the Salesforce org. The static pages are built from an allowlisted export of Apex controller methods and native Salesforce GraphQL queries, and the features that need a request at view time call Apex through Cloudflare Pages Functions. The Salesforce site reads it on the platform with Apex REST + native Salesforce GraphQL (lightning/uiGraphQLApi)
- Skill Graph and Project Gallery use the native GraphQL wire adapter. The Roadmap and Changelog read cached Jira and GitHub data through Apex (`DeliveryController`), because the cache is one JSON row per refresh, not one record per item (my decision, 2026-10-21)
- External services the site depends on: the Gemini API for cover letters (with a local template when it fails), GitHub and Jira for the Delivery page (read by scheduled jobs into caches, never by a visitor), Google Analytics 4 for events on the Salesforce site, and Cloudflare Web Analytics for field Core Web Vitals on the static site. Outside Salesforce the site runs on Cloudflare Pages and its Functions, with no database of its own

#### Target Enterprise State, Phase 8 (2027 to 2028): Designed

- Plan: an AWS Lambda Polyglot Gateway (Function URL), "Door 2", designed in SAS section 1.1 and Appendix M. The repository holds no AWS code.
- Left out of the launch, so the launch does not wait on it
- Because nothing of it is built, it adds no cost and no load to the live site

## 2. Governance Model & Scope

### 2.1 Scope Definition

**In Scope:**

- **Public-facing site** with "5-Minute Tour" guided navigation. It is a static build on Cloudflare Pages since 2026-11-09 ([ADR-041](../adr/041-headless-static-front-end-on-cloudflare-pages.md)), and the Experience Cloud (LWR) site it replaced stays up as the rollback target until 2026-11-23.
- **Custom LWC component framework** including a custom API Testing Harness.
- **Apex REST API implementation** in MuleSoft's API led layers (a System API and a Process API), matching the OpenAPI specifications in the repository (15 SAPI and 8 PAPI paths, version 1.3.0).
- **Generative AI** grounding and prompt engineering in Apex (`PortfolioGroundingService`, `ContentGenerationController.dispatch`). Agentforce, a Prompt Builder template, is the first provider and ships on.
- **Client-side document generation** (Resume).
- **Generative AI Utility:** A "Dynamic Cover Letter Engine" that uses Gemini 2.5 Flash through the Gemini API, with a local template as the last resort, to write personalized application letters based on the visitor's job description and the architect's matching project history (featured projects and experience highlights).
- **Gamified Social Proof engine** with "Vibe-Gated" submission logic.
- **Automated CI/CD Pipeline** with Static Analysis, Unit Testing gates, and a results step summary on every PR run ("PR Validation Results" in `pr.yml`).
- **External API Integration (GitHub):** the portfolio repository's recent commits on the site, read by a scheduled job into a cache.
- **External API Integration (Jira):** the portfolio roadmap's Epics and Stories, read by a scheduled job into a cache.
- **Phase 8 (2027 to 2028), Designed:** multi-cloud integration patterns on the AWS free tier (a Lambda Function URL, object storage and CloudFront). Nothing of it is built.
- **Advanced Visualization:** a skills matrix with "years used" from linked roles, and a D3.js force graph that loads only when a visitor opens it ([ADR-020 amendment](../adr/020-mobile-performance-static-svg-fallback-strategy.md)).
- **Dynamic ERD Visualizer:** an Entity Relationship Diagram drawn from the org's own schema through the Apex Schema class and the same D3.js engine, in place of a static architecture diagram.
- **Executable Governance:** LWC-based documentation that verifies its own success criteria from pipeline evidence. CI publishes a platform event, an Apex trigger persists it, and the checklist reads the result when viewed (for example, ticking "production deploy green" with the commit and the run behind it).
- **Enterprise Observability:** structured Apex logging through one seam (`PortfolioLog`) that writes to **Nebula Logger** (Open Source) when I have installed it, and to debug logs when not. Nebula is optional, so CI and scratch orgs run without it.

**Out of Scope:**

- Authenticated user profiles (Customer/Partner).
- Paid Middleware (Heroku/Enterprise AWS) implementation.
- Managed Package development.
- **Browser Compatibility:** Optimized strictly for Chromium/Webkit engines (Chrome, Safari, modern Edge). Support for legacy Internet Explorer or pre-Chromium Edge behavior is explicitly excluded to minimize QA overhead and testing time.

### 2.2 Success Criteria (Definition of Done)

To define the "Definition of Done" for this portfolio, the following metrics must be met:

**Portfolio Impact:**

- LinkedIn post regarding launch generates > 100 views.
- Interview requests received from 3+ companies within 30 days of launch.

**Functional Acceptance:**

- All 5 pillars accessible via guided navigation.
- API tester successfully calls at least 3 endpoints (Experience, Skills, Certifications).
- The resume downloads as one text based PDF, and a "Copy ATS text" button copies the plain text version (`c-resume-builder`).
- The skills page shows the matrix on every device, and its graph view opens on desktop and tablet only.
- Mobile responsive layout passes manual verification on iOS Safari and Android Chrome.

**Technical Acceptance:**
| Metric | Current Baseline (Est.) | Target (Hard Gate) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **LCP (Mobile)** | Route medians of 2.22 to 2.92 s on the six main routes, 2.52 s as the median of the six, production Lighthouse audit of 2026-11-12 (lab data, Lighthouse CI 0.15.1, mobile emulation, three runs a route, [Technical Guide §2.11](./04-Technical-Guide.md#211-mobile-performance)). The Experience Cloud site measured 7.57 to 10.62 s on production on 2026-10-29, kept in the same section as history | Target **2.5 s**. Reported by every Lighthouse audit and not a failing gate, since lab LCP moves with the machine. Field data (Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile) did not exist at the time of the audit |
| **Apex Coverage** | 98% org wide, 1000 of 1000 tests passing (production's post deploy test run of the 2026-10-24 deploy) | **90% or more**, enforced on every pull request |
| **Code Scanning** | N/A | **0 Critical or High violations** (`npm run scan`) |
| **Accessibility** | Cloudflare site: 100 on all 18 runs of the production audit of 2026-11-12, six routes. Salesforce site: 100 on every run on a scratch copy, a separate result ([Technical Guide §2.11](./04-Technical-Guide.md#211-mobile-performance)). The manual audit of 2026-10-29 found gaps Lighthouse does not score, fixed and re-audited on a scratch copy on 2026-10-30 (SAS Appendix G.6) | **100**, with a screen reader pass by me. A pull request fails when any audited route scores under 100. A score of 100 covers the automated checks only and does not establish WCAG conformance |

- LCP is measured with a Lighthouse mobile audit, three runs per route, medians. The target is 2.5 s. The production audit of 2026-11-12 gave route medians of 2.22 to 2.92 s. Two are under the target, three are within 0.03 s above it, and the home page is 2.92 s. These are lab results and not a Core Web Vitals assessment. On the Experience Cloud site most of the mobile LCP was render delay in the LWR framework's own script, 7.5 to 9.6 s on a scratch copy and 7.57 to 10.62 s on production, and that evidence is kept in the Technical Guide §2.11 as the reason the front end moved.
- Every Apex test passes and org wide coverage is 90% or more. `pr.yml` runs every local test in a scratch org and `scripts/coverage-gate.js --min 90` fails the pull request otherwise. It also validates the pull request check only against production through GlassOps with the relevant tests, the ones Salesforce picks from the change, so a relevant test that fails only in production fails the pull request too.
- CI/CD pipeline passing (Green build badge on Repo).
- No Critical or High violations from Salesforce Code Analyzer (`npm run scan`, `--severity-threshold 2`, run on every pull request).
- The network log shows no `D3_Library` request until a graph view is opened.
- Lighthouse Accessibility score remains 100 with the "Matrix | Graph" view switch present. Since the pull request gate was built, a preview that scores under 100 on any of the six routes fails.
- Skills graph: a D3.js force layout with pan, zoom and node drag (eleven d3 modules in an 81,482 byte static resource, where the AntV graph library it replaced was 1.57 MB), loaded only when a visitor opens the graph view on desktop or tablet. Phones show the skills matrix and request no graph engine, and the Pillar A ERD shows its object list. A drag or the arrow keys pan the graph at any zoom, and a plain wheel scrolls the page.

**Engagement:**

- Average Session Duration > 2 minutes (verified via GA4).
- **ai_live_model_rate:** % of generations served by a live model, Agentforce or Gemini (Target > 80%). Agentforce ships on, so a letter is served by a live model unless both providers fail.
- **ai_fallback_usage:** % of generations served by the Local Template (the fallback share).
- **ai_complete_failure_rate:** % of requests that end with no content at all, a 503 or an error message (Target < 1%).
- **finops_quota_visibility:** visitors who hover over or focus the footer's "AI requests today" line.
- All three AI rates are to come from one GA4 event, `ai_generation_completed`, with the parameters `provider`, `model`, `fallback`, `latency_ms` and `outcome`. GA4 computes the rates, so no counter is stored in Salesforce (my decision, 2026-10-21). Component events go to GA4 through the site's head script ([Technical Guide §2.8](./04-Technical-Guide.md#28-analytics-instrumentation-ga4)). Delivery was proven on a scratch copy of the site. I still have to do the check in production's GA4 DebugView. Before that change no component event reached GA4, so no earlier rate or conversion figure exists.

**Conversion:**

- Greater than 20% of visitors interact with "API Tester" or "Resume Builder" (verified via Custom Events).
  - **api_test_executed:** User successfully calls an endpoint in the API Tester.
  - **resume_downloaded** (`format` `pdf` or `ats`): User downloads the PDF or copies the ATS text.
  - **resilience_test_triggered:** User turns on a "Simulate an outage" switch.

**Reach:**

- Traffic originating from > 3 distinct geographic regions.

## 3. Program Delivery & Roadmap

This implementation is run as a program of parallel delivery tracks, so the dependencies between the schema, the API and the UI are planned and the critical path stays short.
