### 2.19 By the Numbers (`c-by-the-numbers`)

> [!NOTE]
> **Per host, as of 2026-11-02.** On the static site the counts are as of the last build. The Salesforce site reads them when the page loads.

The Delivery page shows a "By the numbers" panel right after its intro, above the checklist, the roadmap and Latest Updates, with its own `h2`.

- **What it shows.** The production deploy runs recorded (the `Pipeline_Run__c` rows of the deploy workflow, passed or failed), the newest deploy's Apex tests and Jest tests each with one plain line on what they prove, the API Lab evaluator tokens issued "since" the month the first was issued, the cover letters written and the API Lab requests sent "since" the month counting began, a closed "What the tests cover" disclosure, and a table of approved testimonials by vibe once one is approved. Every number is text in a list or a table, so none is carried by colour alone. It shows a loading line and an error line like the site's other cards. While the counts load, a hidden, unread copy of the loaded tiles holds their space (`.stats-pending`, `aria-hidden`), so the checklist and everything below it no longer jump when the counts arrive. Measured on the integration site on 2026-10-27 under 4x CPU and slow 4G, the tiles' block grew from 130 px to 947 px when their counts loaded, and that moved the checklist down about 817 px. With the placeholder, the checklist moves 233 px when the counts land, the rest being the "What the tests cover" line and the approved testimonials table (measured at 412 px wide with the same throttling).
- **What the tests cover.** The disclosure lists the Apex and Jest test groups with their counts. The counts are in `testGroups.js`, written by `scripts/count-test-groups.js` from the groups in `scripts/test-groups.json` on the date beside them (`COUNTED_ON`). Continuous integration fails when the file differs from the repository, and `npm run test:groups` rewrites it. The Jest line of the panel appears only once a deploy has published a Jest count.
- **Count up.** When the counts scroll into view after the visitor has scrolled, a copy hidden from assistive technology counts up from 0 over about 600 ms while the real number stays in the text, so a screen reader reads it once. Nothing counts at the top of the page or under reduced motion.
- **Read.** One cacheable call, `PortfolioStatsController.getStats()`, which returns counts only. Each count comes from a query definition read of an Id and at most one grouping field or date (the `PortfolioStatsController_*` records, section 1.7) and is counted in Apex. The issued token read also takes `CreatedDate`, and `tokensSince` is the UTC day of the earliest one. Tokens have their own month because their records start before the usage counters do (in production the first token is 2026-10-21 and the first counter row 2026-10-27). No row, name, email or free text leaves the class. The site guest needs only class access.
- **Waiting testimonials.** The number waiting for approval is not part of the answer. A visitor has no use for it, and I read it in the Testimonials Waiting Approval report. Approved testimonials are read in user mode with sharing, the rows the wall shows. `Pipeline_Run__c`, `API_Access_Request__c` and `Usage_Counter__c` have no guest grant, so their reads run in system mode inside a `without sharing` selector that returns counts.
- **Usage counters.** `UsageCounterWriter` keeps one `Usage_Counter__c` row per UTC day and kind (`Cover_Letter`, `Api_Lab_Request`), keyed "kind:yyyy-mm-dd" in `Key__c`. It reads the day's row with `FOR UPDATE`, adds one and writes it, and `ApiLabController` calls it last, after the callout and after the visitor's result is in hand. Every error is caught and logged, so counting can never fail the visitor's request. The row holds a kind, a day and a count, with no request content or personal data. Rows are never cleaned up. With no rows the panel shows 0 and no month.
- **Jest on each deploy.** `Governance_Event__e` and `Pipeline_Run__c` carry `Jest_Tests_Run__c` and `Jest_Tests_Passed__c`, twins of the Apex count fields, and `GovernanceEventHandler` copies them. The deploy workflow runs the Jest suite after the Apex tests and publishes the two counts on the same event. A Jest failure is reported and never undoes the deploy.
- **Private reports.** For me, not the site: the Portfolio Owner Reports folder holds Contact Form Leads by Month, Testimonials Waiting Approval, Evaluator Token Requests by Outcome and Usage by Month, and the Portfolio Owner Overview dashboard in the Portfolio Owner Dashboards folder charts them. The dashboard runs as the logged in user, so its metadata names no user.

### 2.20 The 10 Minute Tour (`c-tour-bar`)

The tour is a journey over the five pillar pages. It is opt in, and nothing tour related renders on any page unless a tour is running.

- **Start.** The hero's "Take the 10 minute tour" button and the first row of the header's "How it's built" menu both call `startTour`, which sets one session storage key, `portfolio-tour`, to "1" and sends a `portfolio-tour-start` document event, then the link goes to the first stop as a plain link. The key says a tour is running and holds nothing else. Nothing goes in the address. If storage throws, no tour starts, no bar shows and the site works as it did without one.
- **The stop** is worked out from the page path against the live pillars in `c/pillarData` (A `/business-architecture`, B `/nonprofit-solutions`, C `/api-lab`, D `/ai-lab`, E `/delivery`). On a page that is not a stop the bar shows nothing and the tour waits for the next stop page.
- **The bar.** `c-tour-bar` is placed by `portfolioThemeLayout`. It shows a progress row ("Stop 3 of 5, API Lab" with the stop's minutes, announced politely and nothing else is live), the stop's task line as a button, Back and Next as links to the stops either side, and End tour. The task line for each stop is `tour` in `c/pillarData`, at most 70 characters. Next on the last stop is Finish, which shows "That's the tour. Thanks for taking it." and a Close button, centred on one row at every width. It has no links of its own, because the header already links Resume, Contact and Docs. The ending goes away when it is closed or on the next page. End tour removes the bar for the rest of the visit.
- **Minutes.** `tourMinutes` on each pillar in `c/pillarData` is A 2, B 3, C 1, D 3 and E 1. `TOUR_MINUTES` is their sum over the live pillars, 10, and "10 minute tour" is computed from it, never typed. These are the minutes the plan asks of a careful reader. They are not a measurement. How long a careful reader takes on the live site is measured after the deploy and is not stated here. A run of the timing script on the integration site gave 4.7 minutes, but the API Lab could not reach the API there and no letter was asked for, so that is not the figure.
- **Show me.** The task line sends a `portfolio-tour-show-me` document event with the stop letter (`showMe` in `c/tourShowMe`). The one component that owns the stop's control listens (`onShowMe`), scrolls to its own element marked `data-tour-anchor` and focuses it (`revealAnchor`). A is the first image link in `c-project-asset-gallery`, B the first weight slider in `c-decision-matrix`, C the Execute button in `c-api-tester`, D the job description field in `c-cover-letter-generator` and E the In Progress tab or column in `c-roadmap-viewer`. No component reads another's DOM, and a press with no listener does nothing. On the integration site B to E focused their controls in both engines, and A found no anchor there because the gallery is hidden with no assets in the scratch data [unverified that this is the only cause].
- **Layout.** From 768 px up the bar sticks under the header. Below that it is pinned to the bottom of the screen and the layout pads the page by the bar's height (127 px at 390 px wide on the integration site, 2026-10-27). The header's brand, divider, arrow, theme button and menu button moved 0 px with the bar on, at the top and scrolled, in both engines (a header position probe, 2026-10-27).
- **Focus and motion.** The bar follows the header in the keyboard order. When the visitor moves by the bar, focus lands on the new page's `h1` on arrival and is never trapped in the bar. End tour and Close tell the layout so focus does not drop with the bar. The bar has no animation of its own, and Show me scrolls smoothly unless the system asks for reduced motion.
- **Analytics.** `tour_step_viewed` {`stop`, `pillar`}, `tour_exited` {`stop`} and `tour_finished` (section 2.8).
- **Smoke.** `scripts/live-smoke.js` walks all five stops and the ending, and `scripts/check-smoke-routes.js` and its test change with the views.

### 2.21 Native Form Controls (`c/nativeControls`)

Salesforce's base form components draw at 32 px in a site whose own controls are 44 px, so rows of mixed controls misaligned by up to 46 px (the alignment audit of 2026-10-27). [ADR-037](../adr/037-native-form-controls-site-wide.md) records the decision.

- **One CSS only module.** A component adds `@import "c/nativeControls";` at the top of its CSS and uses `nc-control`, `nc-button` (`nc-button_secondary` for a secondary action), `nc-field`, `nc-label`, `nc-hint`, `nc-error` and `nc-required`. The module sets height, fill, edge and focus from the `--pf-` tokens, and a component's own CSS sets layout only.
- **What a replaced control keeps.** A visible label tied by `for` and `id`, `required` with an `aria-hidden` asterisk, the email check announced to screen readers (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`), keyboard use and a focus ring. A native `select` follows the theme through `color-scheme`, set from the `--pf-color-scheme` token (light or dark) in the theme layout and the site stylesheet.
- **Moved.** 13 controls, counted from the base component tags in the four components before and after: the API Lab's endpoint combobox, Advanced query text, token Email and Purpose, the AI Lab's Company Name, Job Title and job description, the resume's "Tailor for" combobox with its Download PDF and Copy ATS text buttons, the code viewer's button, and since 2026-10-30 the resume's two include checkboxes ([ADR-037 amendment](../adr/037-native-form-controls-site-wide.md#amendment-2026-10-30-the-resumes-checkboxes-are-native)). Since 2026-11-15 the contact and testimonial forms' 13 fields use `nc-control` as well, which gives them the 8 px corner, the keyboard only ring and the disabled look a paused form needs ([ADR-037 amendment](../adr/037-native-form-controls-site-wide.md#amendment-2026-11-15-the-contact-and-testimonial-forms-use-the-shared-styles)).
- **Known.** WebKit draws a native select at 48 px against Chromium's 44. `config/jest.config.js` maps `c/nativeControls` to its CSS file by name. Every other `c/` module, `c/pill`, `c/panel` and `c/sectionHeading` among them, resolves through the catch all line under it, so a new CSS only module needs no line of its own (a probe component importing `c/panel` rendered under Jest, 2026-11-15).

#### Shared styles

The style audits of 2026-11-15 found the same role drawn several ways: five pressed looks for toggles, two tab looks, section headings at 32, 24, 22, 20, 18 and 16 px, panels at 4, 12 and 16 px with and without a shadow, and three pill shapes. The fix is one shared style per role. A component imports the module, uses its class and keeps only layout in its own CSS. Each module's own Jest test guards its values.

**Tokens.** Set in the site stylesheet (`sfdc_cms__styles/styles_css/styles.css`, the `:root` block) and mirrored in the `:host` block of `portfolioThemeLayout.css`. `portfolioThemeLayout/__tests__/themeTokens.test.js` fails when the two differ. They do not change with the theme, so the dark blocks leave them out. A size ending in `-sm` is the same role under 768 px, which a component sets in its own media query.

- `nc-button_ghost`, with `nc-button`. The quiet utility button, such as View source or Analytics events: no fill, a `--pf-border` edge, regular weight, and an accent edge on hover. A host that needs a smaller line sets `--nc-ghost-size` and `--nc-ghost-padding`.
- `nc-toggle`. Any button that carries `aria-pressed`, such as a filter or a view switch. Unpressed it looks like `nc-button_secondary`. Pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`) it has the solid `--pf-btn` fill with `--pf-btn-text`. The look is keyed on the attribute, never on a class such as `is-on`, so what is seen and what a screen reader hears cannot drift apart. While it is held down a toggle or tab sinks a little (an inset shadow, and a pressed toggle one step darker), so a click or tap shows at once. On a disabled form the chosen toggle or tab keeps its chosen look at 55% opacity, so a visitor can still see which option is set, and the others take the plain disabled look.
- `nc-toggle-group`. The row that holds related toggles, wrapping with an 8 px gap. Add `nc-toggle-group_tray` for the segmented switch the skills view uses, a tinted tray with borderless toggles where only the pressed one is filled.
- `nc-tablist` and `nc-tab`. One tab style, for a container with `role="tablist"` holding buttons with `role="tab"` and `aria-selected`. The selected tab is tinted with an accent edge and an accent bar along its foot, so a tab never looks like a pressed toggle.
- Hover, one rule per role: a primary button or a pressed toggle darkens to `--pf-btn-hover`, a secondary button, an unpressed toggle or a tab takes the `--pf-subtle` fill, a ghost button takes the accent edge, and a toggle on the tray lifts to the surface.

**Panel.** `c/panel` (`@import "c/panel";`) gives the class `pf-panel`: the `--pf-surface` fill, a 1 px `--pf-border` edge, the 12 px `--pf-radius` corner, 16 px of padding and no shadow. The class carries the `pf-` prefix because several components already have a `panel` class of their own. `pf-panel_subtle` swaps the fill for `--pf-subtle` and is kept for the home page's "Get in touch" panel alone, the one deliberate exception. On the static site the `lightning-card` stand in (`web/src/modules/lightning/card/card.css`) has the same look, so the four tool pages (Skills, Resume, API Lab and AI Lab) lift off the page in dark mode instead of showing an unfilled box.

**Panel heading.** `c/sectionHeading` adds `section-heading-panel` beside `section-heading-compact`, for a heading inside a panel: 20px, weight 700, at every width.

**Pill.** `c/pill` is the one pill, the class `pill`, with round ends (`--pf-radius-pill`), the chip colours and 12 px bold text. The round ends keep a tag from sharing the 8 px corner of a button, toggle or field, so it does not read as something to press. A component sets its own colours for a state, such as Passed or Now, and keeps the shape.

**Migrated components.** The tool and developer components use these classes: the skills view switch and the schema scope switch are `nc-toggle-group_tray`, the skills tier and persona filters, the skill chips, the API reference version and specification switches and the API Lab parameter values and body view are `nc-toggle`, the roadmap and View source tabs are `nc-tab`, View source, Analytics events and the live data marker are `nc-button_ghost`, and the roadmap, changelog, by the numbers, governance checklist, decision matrix, data model and resume settings boxes are `pf-panel`. An error message in any of them is a filled box: 12 px of padding, the `--pf-error` fill, `--pf-error-text` and the 8 px corner. View source and Analytics events still read `--view-source-size` and `--view-source-padding` from their host and pass them to `--nc-ghost-size` and `--nc-ghost-padding`.

### 2.23 Storage Snapshot and Site Usage

> [!NOTE]
> **Per host, as of 2026-11-02.** On the static site the footer's Storage row arrives through the `glass-box` function with the rest of the live reading (section 2.6).

- **The snapshot.** `StorageSnapshotJob` (a Queueable) reads `OrgLimits` for data and file storage, estimates the data by area from a record count per object times 2 KB (Salesforce shows storage by object only on its Setup page, so the figure is an estimate), sums `ContentVersion` sizes (latest versions, grouped by file extension into kinds) with `Document` and `Attachment` sizes, and reads the last 7 days of site usage from the saved report. The areas are Site content, API and rate limiting, Contact and testimonials and Delivery telemetry. No object, `Lead` included, gets a row of its own. A part that cannot be read is left out and the rest is saved. Every query runs in system mode, because the figures are org totals.
- **Storage.** `StorageSnapshot.save` overwrites one `Storage_Snapshot__c` row (`Key__c` "current", `Captured_At__c`, `Payload__c`). Only aggregates are kept.
- **When it runs.** `IntegrationCacheRefreshScheduler`, which already runs at :00, :15, :30 and :45, enqueues the job when `StorageSnapshot.isDue()` says the stored snapshot is older than the `Storage_Snapshot_Hours` setting (1, range 1 to 24). No new schedule or scheduled job slot is used.
- **How the footer reads it.** `FooterController.getSystemSnapshot()` calls `StorageSnapshot.read()`, which hands the aggregates to any caller, the site guest included. The guest has no access to the object, so a `without sharing` inner class reads the row, and only the payload's aggregates leave. No permission was added for the guest. `Portfolio_Admin` gets the object and its two fields.
- **Site traffic is off.** The 7 day site usage readings leave `read()` only when the `Footer_Site_Traffic_Visible` setting is 1, and it ships at 0.
- **The usage report.** The `Site_Usage_History` report type (the Site object joined through `UsageHistory`) and the "Site usage, last 30 days" report in the private Portfolio Owner Reports folder, grouped by site, limit type and day with usage summed. Usage history is report only, so it cannot be queried with SOQL.
- **What production showed.** Read on production on 2026-10-27, the Visualforce API site `Portfolio` showed Origin Bandwidth at most 625,486 in a day and Request Time at most 4,736, the LWR site `Portfolio1` that serves every page showed no rows at all in 30 days, and neither site had Cache Bandwidth or Cache Page Views rows. The units are bytes and milliseconds according to the help article [unverified for this report].
- **Open question.** Whether LWR traffic counts toward the Developer Edition's 500 MB a day per site, the separate 48 TB a year CDN allowance, both or neither is not known. No Salesforce source answers it, the limits articles never mention LWR, and the empty `Portfolio1` rows are the only evidence. Whether LWR usage reaches the usage history at all is also not known. If the limit is passed the site stays up with no service level and shows the Limit Exceeded page if the platform serves it for an LWR site, which I have not checked. I decide what to do with that risk.
- **Not claimed.** No storage figure from production is stated here, because the snapshot has not run there. The Storage line shows only once a stored snapshot exists.

### 2.24 Live Data Marker (`c-data-source`)

Every data driven section says plainly where its data comes from and when it was read. On the Salesforce site that is "rebuilt from Salesforce records each time the page loads, not a stored copy". On the static site (deployed at its `ryanbumstead.com` since the cutover on 2026-11-09) the marker reads "From Salesforce, built <time>" because the section was read when the site was built, not when the page loaded. Only a section that really calls Salesforce at view time says "Live from Salesforce". The bullets below describe the Salesforce site's marker unless they say otherwise.

- **The control.** `<c-data-source source-keys="ResumeController_Roles,ResumeController_Skills"></c-data-source>` sits in the section's title row, beside View source where there is one. `source-keys` names `Query_Definition__mdt` records. `objects` names objects instead, for a section that reads through GraphQL (the skills page passes `Skill__c`), and is served only when an active definition reads that object. `hide-counts` shows the sources without numbers, for a section where a row count would mislead: the numbers tiles, the GitHub and Jira caches (one row per refresh), and the cover letter's grounding (a ranked handful, not every record).
- **What it shows.** A button reading "Live from Salesforce" with up to three counts, such as "8 roles, 8 skills, 6 certifications". Opened, a panel says the section is not a stored copy, lists each source by name with its count, and links to the full data model. When any source reads an object the ERD draws, a "See this section's data model" button opens a modal dialog built like View source, holding `c-schema-visualizer` with the full data model and those objects highlighted. On a phone (under 768 px) the visualizer shows a text list, and with objects highlighted that list holds only those objects and the objects they link to directly (a platform self lookup does not count as a link), the section's own objects first. Its caption says the objects are "listed" and no longer "highlighted among" the full count, and it leaves out its own heading because the dialog already has one. The dialog ends with a "See the full data model" link, shown under 768 px only. Desktop, tablet and the full data model page are unchanged. The visualizer renders only while the dialog is open, Escape, Close or the backdrop close it and return focus to the marker, and on a phone the dialog fills the screen. Every visible string is in the `WORDING` block of `dataSource.js`. The button reports `aria-expanded`, Escape or Close returns focus to it, and on a phone it wraps and the panel opens in the flow under it. A panel that would run past the right edge of the window opens from the button's right edge instead. In every section the marker sits at the end of the heading row, and on a phone under the heading from the start of the line. On the roadmap and in the resume, cover letter and skills cards it follows View source. In those three cards, on narrower screens (under 1024 px for the resume, 768 px for the cover letter and skills cards), the pair opens the card body instead, through `c/mediaWatch`.
- **How it's built.** The panel's footer also holds a "How it's built" link that opens the Technical Guide on `/docs` in the same tab. The section is looked up by the first entry of `source-keys`, then by the first entry of `objects`, then falls back to this section, 2.24 (`GUIDE_SECTIONS` in `dataSource.js`).
- **Read.** `DataSourceController.getSources` and `getObjectSources` (`@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`) return, per active definition, a label, the object API name, whether the ERD draws that object (`SchemaService.modelObjectNames()`, read once per call) and a `COUNT()` built from the definition's own object and filter, at most 12 names a call. A definition whose filter uses a bind variable returns no count, because a plain count would not match what the section reads. System mode definitions are counted in a private `without sharing` selector, as `ResumeController` reads them, so the site guest sees the true count. The label is the definition's `Visitor_Label__c` when set ("roles" for experiences, so two sources on one object can read differently), else the object's plural label. For `objects`, the first active definition on that object with a visitor label supplies it. Descriptions, field lists and filters never leave the class.
- **Where it is placed.** The resume, the home timeline and case studies, the testimonials wall, by the numbers, the Delivery changelog and roadmap, the skills page and the cover letter.

### 2.25 The Static Build and the Shims

The static site in `web/` ([ADR-041](../adr/041-headless-static-front-end-on-cloudflare-pages.md)) compiles the same LWCs the Salesforce site runs. It is not a second copy.

- **The build.** `web/build/build.mjs` reads the org through the export (or the sample fixtures in `web/fixtures` when no build user secret exists), works out a read plan for each route from the bundler's module graph, compiles one bundle per route from the route's own view file with LWC OSS, and writes the pages to `web/dist`. A planned read with no data fails the build. `web/build/leak-scan.mjs` then scans the output for session ids, undeclared fields, email addresses and the terms in the `SITE_DENYLIST` secret. `npm test --prefix web` runs the build's `node --test` units, and `node web/build/check-export-coverage.mjs` checks that the allowlist in `SiteExportCalls` is exactly the set of build time calls the public pages import (`web/build/calls.mjs`).
- **The export.** `SiteExportResource` runs one allowlisted, read only controller method per call and returns its result with null fields left out. 27 calls, 83 reads, 15 pages (12 routes plus 404, 429 and 503). The parity tests `SiteExportResourceTest` and `SiteExportTestimonialParityTest` compare 26 of the calls as the guest and as the build user. The other call is the resume snapshot (section 2.26), which the guest must not read, so `ResumeSnapshotServiceTest` proves the refusal instead.
- **The shims.** Platform imports resolve to modules in `web/src/shims`. Apex methods answer from build time data. GraphQL wires answer from queries run at build time. `lightning-card`, `lightning-spinner` and `lightning-icon` are native stand ins, so a card has no header icon on the static site. The SLDS and `dxp` stylesheets are not loaded, because the components use native shadow and those sheets never reached inside them.
- **The request time seam.** A request time Apex call rejects in the browser until a handler is set. `setRequestHandler` in `web/src/shims/apex.js` is where the Pages Functions plug in, and it turns a function error into the `{ body: { message } }` shape the components already handle. `web/build/calls.mjs` lists the request time calls.
- **`c/siteHost`.** A small module tells a component which host serves it (`IS_STATIC`). On Salesforce nothing changes. On the static site the live data marker reads "From Salesforce, built <time>" with the time in UTC and in the visitor's zone, and the hero proof line and the footer say the same (`PROOF_STATIC` in `heroBanner.js`).
- **First section first.** Each page paints its first section before the rest of its components load, which is the rule of [ADR-014](../adr/014-deferred-telemetry-loading-performance.md#amendment-2026-11-02-the-static-front-end) applied to the static pages (section 2.11 has the local numbers).
- **Request time features.** Seven site actions go through Pages Functions with a kill switch each. Which features are `live` or `recorded` is read from `/api/features`. A production host reads an unset switch as `live`, and any other host is always `recorded` (`web/functions/_lib/features.js`). `PRODUCTION_HOSTS` in `web/wrangler.toml` names the production hosts as `ryanbumstead.com` and `www.ryanbumstead.com`, so `ryanbumstead.pages.dev` stays recorded. The five switches are set in `[vars]` in `web/wrangler.toml`, and a test in `web/test/functions.test.mjs` fails if one goes missing. The Maintenance Guide section 3.12 says how to flip a switch.
- **The person check and the failure log.** The contact form, the testimonial form, the cover letter and the evaluator token request each carry a Cloudflare Turnstile token, and `handlePost` in `web/functions/_lib/actions.js` checks it before the budget guard, before any Salesforce call and before the edge template letter, so a cover letter request with no good token gets a 400 and not a letter. The API Lab call itself (`lab/invoke`) has no check. The browser routes in `web/src/shims/api-client.js` mark the same four routes with `turnstile: true`. Every failure at the edge writes one JSON line through `web/functions/_lib/log.js` with the route, an error code, the status and the request id, and nothing about the visitor: no address, no hash, no user agent, no email, no body field, no token and no query string. Pages keeps no stored log for these lines, so they show only in a live tail (`wrangler pages deployment tail`).
- **Honest labels.** Only a section that really calls Salesforce at view time says "Live from Salesforce".
- **What is not carried over.** The sign in, register, password and news views have no static page.

### 2.26 Resume Selection Fields and the Snapshot

The tailored resume work needs to know, for every line the resume can show, what it is evidence of and whether I have checked it. That lives in the org, beside the resume data it describes ([ADR-009](../adr/009-granular-resume-data-model.md)).

- **Four fields on five objects.** `Experience_Highlight__c`, `Skill__c`, `Project__c`, `Certification__c` and `Resume_Variant__c` each carry Requirement Tags (a multi select on the `Requirement_Category` global value set, 16 categories), Selection Priority (1, 2 or 3, default 2), Verified (default false) and Visibility (Public is the only value, default Public). A picklist default applies to new records only, so records that existed before the fields are blank until `scripts/mark-existing-verified.apex` is run once.
- **The primary role.** `Experience__c.Is_Primary_Role__c` marks the one role a tailored resume treats as current. Exactly one role is ticked, and it must also be current. Two roles can be current at two employers, and this says which one leads.
- **Resume Variant.** `Resume_Variant__c` holds headline and summary wordings by title family (engineer, architect, consultant, admin). The resume page and PDF read the public, verified Summary and Headline variants through `ResumeController` (section 2.2), one summary and one headline per focus. The headline is the line under the name on the resume. Nothing else on the site reads it yet.
- **What the public site and API show.** Only verified records. Every Apex read that serves a public page, the public API (SAPI and PAPI), the API Lab options or the agent's grounding filters on `Is_Verified__c = TRUE`, and a skill reached through `Experience_Skill__c`, `Project_Skill__c` or `Certification_Skill__c` must be verified too. The filter sits in both the code default and its `Query_Definition__mdt` record. These reads run in system mode, so the guest needs no read on the field. `VerifiedPublicReadsTest` and `ApiVerifiedReadsTest` insert one verified and one unverified record of each kind and check only the verified one comes back. The snapshot is the one read that keeps unverified items, for the build only. The four GraphQL reads (`SkillNetworkGraph`, `SkillPersonaTags`, `SkillSelectionPriority` and `ProjectAssetGallery`) run as the guest in user mode, so sharing filters them instead. External access to `Skill__c` and `Project__c` is Private, and the guest sharing rules `Guest_Read_All_Skills` and `Guest_Read_All_Projects` share a row with the guest only when `Is_Verified__c` is true. The API names are older than the criteria and stay so a deploy updates the rules in place. `Project_Skill__c`, `Experience_Skill__c`, `Certification_Skill__c` and `Project_Asset__c` are master detail to a skill or a project, so a link or an asset that reaches an unverified record is hidden too. The guest needs no read on `Is_Verified__c`, because a sharing rule checks its criteria whatever the guest can see. The platform writes the guest shares after a record commits, so `GuestVerifiedSharingTest` can prove only that the guest never reads an unverified row and that internal users still read every row. The static build runs the same GraphQL queries as the build user, an internal user who reads every row, so `web/build/verified.mjs` filters the response after the query. The build sends each query exactly as the component does, so the read key still matches, then reads the Ids of unverified skills and projects with a SOQL query through the same connection and drops every row whose Id, or a skill or project it points at, is one of them. Assets nested in a dropped project go with it. The build user can read `Is_Verified__c` on both objects, and a failed Id read fails the build. `web/test/verified.test.mjs` covers the filter, and `SiteExportTestimonialParityTest.graphqlRowsMatchTheGuest` compares the guest's rows with the build user's rows after the same drop.
- **The snapshot.** `ResumeSnapshotService.getSnapshot` returns the owner, every role and every selectable item in one fixed shape. It is on the export allowlist as a build only call (`BUILD_ONLY_CALLS` in `web/build/calls.mjs`), so the coverage check fails if a public page ever imports it. It refuses to guess: a record that is not Public, a missing or repeated id, a missing priority or text, or anything but one current primary role stops the export with a plain message. Projects are included only in the statuses the site lists.
- **Item keys.** Every item has `id`, `type`, `text`, `tags`, `priority`, `verified` and `visibility`. A bullet also has `roleId`. A headline or summary also has `titleFamily`, from `Resume_Variant__c.Title_Family__c`. A project also has `value` and `solution`, from `Business_Value__c` and `Solution__c`, with the spacing collapsed to one line. A project's `text` is its name. Each of these keys is null when the field is blank, and no other type carries it. The project metric fields are not read, because they hold stale numbers and a placeholder. The contract check in `web/build/export.mjs` and the evaluation kit's builder both refuse an item that misses its type's keys or carries another type's. The tailoring grounding check counts a selected project's value and solution as evidence text, so a cover letter, the template one included, may quote them.
- **Who can read it.** Only a user holding `Site_Build_Export`. `Portfolio_Site_Build` grants the build user read access to the selection fields and `Title_Family__c`, and `Portfolio_Guest` grants only `Skill__c.Selection_Priority__c`, which the Skills page tiers read (section 2.1). The build user also holds `Portfolio_Guest`, which already grants `Business_Value__c` and `Solution__c`, because the public project pages show them. Certifications, employer names and the owner name are read in system mode after the permission check, because the build user has no Contact or Account access. `ResumeSnapshotServiceTest` proves the guest sees none of the new fields except that one and gets a refusal from both the class and the export.
- **The build side.** `web/build/export.mjs` checks the snapshot against the contract and writes it to `web/functions/_generated/resume-snapshot.json`, which git ignores. The writer refuses any path under `web/dist` or `web/public`, because the snapshot holds unverified items. `web/test/resume-snapshot.test.mjs` builds from fixtures and searches the output for unverified text. Every export build reads the snapshot after the page data and prints its counts, so a snapshot that breaks the contract fails the site build. A fixture build copies the seed snapshot in `web/fixtures` to the same ignored path.

## 3. Quality Assurance Checklist

> [!TIP]
> **One command.** `npm run pre-launch-check -- --target-org <alias>` runs the release checks in order and stops at the first failure: Prettier on the files changed against `origin/main`, the code analyzer (`npm run scan`), a delta dry run with `RunLocalTests` against the named org (`scripts/validate.js`), the Jest tests, and the Apex test and coverage gate (`scripts/coverage-gate.js`, 90%). A Lighthouse run follows and is optional. The org is required and never taken from the CLI default, because the main checkout's default is production (`scripts/pre-launch-check.js`). Name a scratch org, never production, since the coverage step runs every local test in the org it is given.

### 3.1 Key Verification Items

- **LCP:** Run a Lighthouse mobile audit (three runs per route, medians) and compare with the 2.5 s target and the recorded gate in §2.11.
- **Coverage:** every Apex test passes and org wide coverage is 90% or more (`npm run sf:coverage -- --target-org <alias>`). `pr.yml` enforces the same gate on every pull request.
- **Security:** no Critical or High violation from Salesforce Code Analyzer (`npm run scan`).
- **Internal references:** `npm run refs:check` (`scripts/check-internal-refs.js`) exits 0. It fails when a comment, a metadata description or a help text under `packages/`, or any text in `docs/`, `README.md` or `STATUS.md`, names a build process code instead of saying what the code does. It scans the same paths `pr.yml` does, and the pre-commit hook runs it on each staged file under those paths. It reads only prose (comments per language, `description` and `inlineHelpText` in XML, `description` values in JSON and YAML, the whole of a Markdown file), so a hex colour, an `h1` tag or an id in test data never counts, and it skips the vendored third party bundles it lists by name. An exception goes in `scripts/internal-refs-allowlist.json` with the path, the exact line and a reason, and the list is empty today. Its own tests are `node --test scripts/check-internal-refs.test.js`, and `pr.yml` runs both in `quality-check`.
- **CI parity:** `npm run ci:local` (`scripts/ci-local.js`) passes before a push. It runs the same commands as the `quality-check` job in `pr.yml`, for the files changed against `origin/main`, and `.husky/pre-push` runs it on every push. A SKIPPED step is not a pass, so read the summary. `scripts/ci-local.test.js` fails when `pr.yml` gains a command the runner lacks ([Maintenance Guide §3.1](./05-Maintenance-Guide.md#31-local-development-commands)).
- **Live smoke test:** after a production deploy, the Live Smoke Test passes (Maintenance Guide §3.2). By hand: `SITE_BASE=<site root> node scripts/live-smoke.js`, with Playwright and its Chromium and WebKit browsers installed.
- **Accessibility:** confirm nothing animates (the skills graph and the ERD are drawn once, after the layout finishes), so no pause control is needed (SAS Appendix G.2). Then confirm each route has a `main` landmark and a skip to content link as its first stop, and run the screen reader checks listed in SAS Appendix G.6, which are mine to do on NVDA and VoiceOver.
- **Degradation Test:** turn on "Simulate an outage" in the roadmap card (it drives Latest Updates too). Verify the cached data stays on screen with a "Simulated" badge (status `SIMULATED`) and no request leaves for GitHub or Jira.
- **Limit Visibility:** the footer shows CPU, heap and SOQL use against their limits. These are the figures of the `FooterController.getSystemSnapshot` call itself, so they cannot reflect another operation. Verify the line renders, and that it reads "status unavailable" when the call fails.
- **Analytics:** Verify api_test_executed event fires in GA4 Real-Time view when using the API Tester. Until the production check after the deploy, delivery is proven only on a scratch copy of the site (§2.8).
- Verify the Skill Graph uses `lightning/uiGraphQLApi` (the Network tab shows a `/graphql` call to the Salesforce domain). The Roadmap reads Apex over the cache (`DeliveryController.getRoadmap`), so it makes no GraphQL call
- **AI fallback:** with the Gemini API unavailable, `POST /papi/ai/generate` with `type: CoverLetter` returns `provider: Local` and `fallbackOccurred: true`, and the site page shows the template letter with the reason. After three Gemini failures the footer shows "Gemini: circuit open until HH:MM" and the next letter skips Gemini.

## 3.4 Concrete Testing Example

Here is a real test from the repository, `GitHubCacheRefreshJobTest.shouldInsertNothingWhenGitHubFails` (`packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/GitHubCacheRefreshJobTest.cls`). It mocks a GitHub outage and proves the degraded mode in section 1.1: the job makes one callout, stores nothing, the page keeps serving the last good commits, and the `github` circuit breaker counts the failure. `useRepo` and `newestRow` are helpers in the same class, and `CountingMock` is its `HttpCalloutMock`, which counts the calls it answers.

```apex
@IsTest
static void shouldInsertNothingWhenGitHubFails() {
  useRepo('o/r');
  CountingMock mock = new CountingMock(503, '{"message":"down"}');
  Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, mock);

  Test.startTest();
  String outcome = GitHubCacheRefreshJob.refresh();
  Test.stopTest();

  Assert.areEqual(GitHubCacheRefreshJob.OUTCOME_FAILED, outcome, 'Outcome');
  Assert.areEqual(1, mock.calls, 'The call was made');
  Assert.areEqual(
    1,
    [SELECT COUNT() FROM Github_Cache__c],
    'Nothing inserted'
  );
  Assert.isTrue(
    newestRow().JSON_Payload__c.contains(GOOD_SHA),
    'The newest good row is untouched'
  );
  Assert.areEqual(
    GOOD_SHA,
    DeliveryController.getRecentCommits(null).items[0].sha,
    'The page keeps serving the last good commits'
  );
  Assert.areEqual(
    1,
    CircuitBreaker.snapshot()[1].failures,
    'The github breaker counted the failure'
  );
}
```

# ADR-004: Static Resource Code Rendering

> Later built another way: the source is read from GitHub into an org cache, not from a static resource. See the [amendment](#amendment-2026-10-23-source-from-github-cached-in-the-org) below.

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/codeViewer), also [Source_Cache\_\_c](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/objects/Source_Cache__c)

Amended 2026-10-23 (see the amendment below): built, with the source read from GitHub into an org cache, not from a static resource. Originally Accepted.

## Context

Requirement to display raw source code without triggering GitHub API rate limits.

## Decision

Perform client-side fetches of code stored in Static Resources.

## Rationale

Decouples code visualization from external API availability and prevents 429 errors during high traffic.

## Implications

Code snippets must be packaged and deployed as part of the Salesforce metadata.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): source from GitHub, cached in the org

**As built.** The code is not packaged into static resources. Each showcase component (the API Lab, the skills graph, the Pillar A data model, the Pillar B decision matrix, the resume builder and the Delivery roadmap) has a View source button. It opens a dialog with the component's JavaScript, HTML and main Apex class, highlighted by the shared Prism module (`c/prismHighlighter`), with a link to each file on GitHub.

- **Files:** listed in `Source_File__mdt` records, so they can change without a code change.
- **Fetch:** `SourceCacheRefreshJob` reads each file from GitHub through the `GitHub_API` Named Credential at most once a day per file, into `Source_Cache__c`, an admin only object. `IntegrationCacheRefreshScheduler` enqueues it on its existing schedule only when a file is due. The documents on `/docs` are also read again after a push that changes them ([ADR-007 amendment of 2026-10-24](007-github-api-server-side-caching.md#amendment-2026-10-24-the-docs-refresh-after-a-push)).
- **Read:** visitors read only the cache, through `SourceController.getSourceFiles`. No visitor request calls GitHub, which keeps the original goal of this ADR: no GitHub rate limit or outage reaches a page view.
- **Why not static resources:** a packaged copy goes stale with every commit and would need a deploy to refresh. The cache always shows `main` as of the last daily read, with its fetch time.

Details are in the Technical Guide section 2.14.

# ADR-005: Gamified Testimonial UI

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/testimonialSubmit), also [TestimonialControllerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/TestimonialControllerTest.cls)

Accepted, amended 2026-10-23 (see the amendment below).

## Context

Need to balance professional verification with my personal brand personality.

## Decision

Implement a "Vibe-Gated" Sentence Builder (Mad-Libs style) UI.

## Rationale

Ensures structured data entry while providing a unique, engaging experience for visitors.

## Implications

Requires custom LWC logic to handle dynamic sentence fragments and "Vibe" toggles.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): the accessible sentence builder

An earlier version of the form had replaced the sentence with plain labelled fields, and the vibe toggle chose nothing. This amendment brings the sentence back in an accessible form.

- **The sentence.** "I'm a [relationship], and Ryan [strength]. The result? [outcome]" sits inside one `fieldset` whose `legend` reads the sentence. Each blank is a labelled select. A polite live region previews the finished sentence, and an optional note follows.
- **The vibe chooses the fragments.** Strengths and outcomes are `Testimonial_Fragment__mdt` records with a vibe (Professional or Casual), a slot (Strength or Outcome), a sort order and an audience (Worked together or Anyone), so I edit them without a code change. A Recruiter, or a Fan or visitor, sees only the Anyone outcomes.
- **Server rules.** `TestimonialController` accepts only a known fragment of the chosen vibe, stores the composed sentence in `Context__c` (so it stays exactly as approved even if a fragment's wording changes later) and keeps the fragment names and the note in fields of their own. `SubmissionGuard` drops spam silently and applies the rate limit of 5 a minute across all visitors. `Approved__c` is never set by the form.
- **The wall.** Approved testimonials show on `/testimonials` with a "Professional / All" filter that uses the API feed's rule: the Professional vibe from a Manager, Client or Peer.

## Amendment (2026-10-24): each new testimonial goes to the owner for approval

The site guest who saves a testimonial cannot submit it for approval, so `TestimonialController` publishes one `Testimonial_Submission__e` after the save. `TestimonialSubmissionTrigger` runs as the Automated Process user and `TestimonialApprovalSubmitter` submits the record to the Testimonial Approval process on its owner's behalf. I am the site's default owner for guest records. The process allows only the record owner as submitter and assigns the record owner as approver, so no user is named in metadata.

- The approval request email (`Portfolio_Testimonial_Approval_Request`) shows the author, title, relationship, vibe, the quote and the note, with links to the request and the record. I approve or reject by replying with one word, or in Salesforce. Email approval response is turned on in source (`EmailAdministrationSettings`, `enableEmailWorkflowApproval`).
- Final approval sets `Approved__c` (field update `Testimonial_Set_Approved`). Rejection leaves it false, so the restriction rule keeps the testimonial off the site.
- A record that cannot be submitted stays saved and unapproved, and the visitor is thanked as usual. A testimonial saved before this hand off existed is not submitted on its own. I submit or approve it by hand.

## Amendment (2026-10-28): a review in the reviewer's own words

The sentence builder stays the default, and a visitor can now choose "Write my own" instead.

- **Why.** A quote someone wrote reads as more convincing than a sentence assembled from approved phrases, and some reviewers have more to say than three blanks allow. The builder was chosen for engagement and structured data, not for safety: every review is already saved unapproved and goes to me for approval, and `SubmissionGuard` already drops spam and applies the rate limit. Those protections now cover free text too.
- **What stays structured.** The relationship is still a required choice in both modes, and the vibe still applies, because the wall's Professional filter reads those two fields.
- **Where the words go.** `TestimonialController.submitOwnTestimonial` stores the review in `Context__c`, the field a built sentence uses, so the wall, the API feed and the approval email need no change. It sets no fragment fields and no note. The review has the room `Context__c` has, 255 characters, and the guard scans it as it scans a note.
- **Limits on screen.** Every box on the form shows its count against its limit and warns once it is close.

# ADR-009: Granular Resume Data Model

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/objects/Experience__c), also [Experience_Highlight\_\_c](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/objects/Experience_Highlight__c)

## Context

The site must generate tailored content for different professional personas (e.g., Admin vs. Architect).

## Decision

Utilize a Master-Detail relationship (Experience**c → Experience_Highlight**c).

## Rationale

Enables persona-based filtering of granular bullet points rather than static text blocks.

## Implications

Requires parent-child query logic to assemble the final resume payload.

## Amendment (2026-10-23)

Skills now follow the persona too. For a chosen persona the resume keeps the skills whose `Skill__c.Persona_Tag__c` includes it, plus every skill with no tag, so a new skill nobody has tagged yet never disappears. With no persona it keeps every skill. The same rule runs in `ResumeController.getResume` (the resume page, its ATS text and its PDF) and in PAPI `GET /papi/v1/resume/generate` (`PAPIResume`).

## Amendment (2026-11-14)

The model now also says what each resume line is evidence of. `Experience_Highlight__c`, `Skill__c`, `Project__c`, `Certification__c` and the new `Resume_Variant__c` (headline and summary wordings by title family) each carry Requirement Tags, Selection Priority, Verified and Visibility. `Experience__c.Is_Primary_Role__c` marks the one current role a tailored resume leads with. `ResumeSnapshotService` reads all of it into one snapshot for the build user only. The site guest reads none of these fields, and no public page shows them. Verified still decides what a public page shows. Every public Apex read of highlights, skills, projects and certifications leaves out a record that is not verified, so a line I load unverified stays off the resume, the timeline and the public API until I verify it. That holds for the persona rule above too, so a new skill with no tag appears only once it is verified. The Technical Guide section 2.26 has the rules.

## Amendment (2026-11-14): the guest reads the skill priority

This replaces one sentence of the amendment above. The site guest now reads one of those fields, `Skill__c.Selection_Priority__c`, through `Portfolio_Guest`, and no other new field. The Skills page shows its skills in three tiers, "Core", "Extended" and "Full toolkit", and opens on Core. The tier comes from the priority and the links behind each skill, and the page reads the priority through GraphQL as the guest in user mode, so the guest needs field level read on it. Requirement Tags, Verified and Visibility stay hidden from the guest, and so does the priority on the other four objects. The build user already reads the field through `Portfolio_Site_Build`.

- **Why the guest and not Apex.** The skills page already reads skills through GraphQL as the guest. A separate Apex read for one picklist would add a call and a code path for a value that says only how strongly I lead with a skill, which the page shows anyway by where the skill appears.
- **What a visitor can learn.** Which tier a skill sits in, which the page shows by design. The raw value is in the GraphQL response, and it says no more than the tier does.
- **Proof.** `ResumeSnapshotServiceTest.shouldHideTheNewFieldsFromTheGuest` now expects exactly `Skill__c.Selection_Priority__c` among the new fields the guest can read, and `SiteExportTestimonialParityTest.graphqlRowsMatchTheGuest` compares the field as the guest and as the build user. The Technical Guide section 2.1 has the tier rules.

## Amendment (2026-11-18): the public focuses are Engineer, Architect and Consultant

The decision above stays as written, and the text of the context ("Admin vs. Architect") is the history of how this started. On 2026-11-14 I changed the focuses a visitor can pick. They were Architect, Developer and Admin. They are now **Engineer, Architect and Consultant**, shown as "Salesforce Engineer", "Platform Architect" and "Solution Consultant". The reason is that these three match the three title families of my summaries in `Resume_Variant__c` (engineer, architect and consultant), so each focus can lead with wording written for it. Architect stays the default focus.

- **What changed in the data model.** `Persona_Tag__c` on `Experience_Highlight__c` and on `Skill__c` gained two active values, Engineer and Consultant. `Experience_Highlight__c` gained `Engineer_Sort_Order__c` and `Consultant_Sort_Order__c`, beside the Admin, Developer and Architect sort fields, and the `Sync_Experience_Highlight_Sort_Orders` flow gained an Engineer branch and a Consultant branch. Both fields are restricted picklists, so a record can only carry a value the picklist lists as active.
- **Developer is replaced, in two steps.** A data step writes Engineer in place of Developer on every highlight and skill that carries it, and keeps every other tag. Developer is deactivated on both fields only after that, and only after the code that stopped asking for it has merged. A restricted picklist refuses an inactive value when a record is saved with it, so the order matters. Developer is now an inactive value on both fields, kept in the picklist so stored history stays valid, and the flow no longer has a Developer branch. `Developer_Sort_Order__c` stays on the object, unread. The Maintenance Guide section 3.14 has the steps.
- **Admin stays, as an internal value.** It is still an active value and still a title family for the cover letter and the agent, which tailor to jobs whatever the focus. It is no longer a focus a visitor can pick. `ResumeController.getResume` refuses Admin and Developer, and a highlight or skill tagged only Admin drops off the public resume until I retag it. A data step I approve record by record does that retag before the switch.
- **One summary per focus.** `ResumeController.getResume` now returns a top level `summary`. It is the Summary variant of `Resume_Variant__c` for the focus (the title family is the focus in lower case) that is Public and verified. When a focus has several, the lowest `Selection_Priority__c` wins and a blank priority comes last. When a focus has none, the summary is `Contact.Career_Objective__c`, and when that is blank the summary is null. The read is the query definition `ResumeController_Variants`, system mode like the other site reads. `header.careerObjective` is unchanged.
- **The sort fields.** `ResumeController` orders a focus's highlights by that focus's sort field, with blanks last, then by `Sort_Order__c`. A highlight with `Lock_Sort_Across_Personas__c` set, and every highlight when no focus is chosen, sorts by `Sort_Order__c` alone. Every highlight in production has the lock set, so the per focus fields do not change an order today and the new two needed no copied values.
- **The API.** v1 and v2 share one persona reader. Both accept Engineer, Architect and Consultant, and both still accept Developer (read as Engineer) and Admin, in any letter case, so a caller that sent Developer keeps working. The v2 specs document only the three focuses. The v1 specs document the three plus Developer and Admin as aliases. The API Lab offers the three focuses (`ApiLabOptionsController.ACCEPTED_PERSONAS`).
- **Analytics.** Reports read `developer` as `engineer`, with no backfill of past events.

# ADR-007: GitHub API Server-Side Caching

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/GitHubCacheRefreshJob.cls), also [DeliveryControllerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/DeliveryControllerTest.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

GitHub unauthenticated API limits (60 req/hr) are insufficient for public traffic.

## Decision

Implement Apex-based caching via Scheduled Jobs and Custom Metadata.

## Rationale

Prevents site failure by serving a GitHub_Cache\_\_c record when API limits are exhausted.

## Implications

Commits may appear with a "Last Updated" delay of up to 15 minutes.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): the cache objects and the scheduled refresh

The decision stands: guests read a server-side cache and never trigger a callout. The cache and the refresh are built as follows.

- **The cache is custom objects**, `Github_Cache__c` and `Jira_Cache__c`, not custom metadata or a custom setting. Each refresh inserts one row whose `JSON_Payload__c` holds the mapped item list (`{"schemaVersion":1,"items":[...]}`), not the raw API body. The newest row is the one served.
- **The refresh is Queueable.** Scheduled Apex cannot call out synchronously, so `IntegrationCacheRefreshScheduler`, scheduled at :00, :15, :30 and :45, enqueues `GitHubCacheRefreshJob` and `JiraCacheRefreshJob` (`Queueable`, `Database.AllowsCallouts`). They call out through the `GitHub_API` and `Jira_API` Named Credentials as the scheduling admin user, who holds the principal access through `Portfolio_Admin`. A failed refresh inserts nothing, so the last good row stays.
- **The read side** is `DeliveryController.getRecentCommits()` and `getRoadmap()` (cacheable Apex). Each returns the items with their age and a status: `FRESH` under 30 minutes, `STALE` older, `EMPTY` with no usable row, and `SIMULATED` or `DEGRADED` for the resilience toggle and an open breaker (ADR-022).
- **Cleanup keeps the newest row** per cache object and deletes only older rows past the age limit, so an outage never empties the page.
- **The roadmap** shows only `SPAP` issues labelled `portfolio-roadmap` (my decision, 2026-10-21), so nothing private reaches the public page.
- **The authenticated GitHub limit** is 5,000 requests an hour, so the 60 an hour unauthenticated limit in the context no longer binds. Four refreshes an hour are far inside it.

## Amendment (2026-10-24): the docs refresh after a push

The documents on `/docs` no longer wait up to a day for the scheduled read. `SourceCacheRefreshJob.forceRefresh` reads the given paths, or every path of one source key, whatever their age, with the same upsert on `Path__c`, parts, stale row delete, circuit breaker and file cap as the scheduled run. When a push to `main` changes `docs/**`, the Deploy to Production workflow's `docs-cache` job runs after the deploy job, waits 60 seconds because the GitHub contents API caches for 60, runs `scripts/refresh-docs-cache.apex` in production as the workflow's signed in admin, and fails unless every docs record reads 200 since it started. The page still reads only the cache, never GitHub.

# ADR-010: Visualization Engine (Vis.js vs. the AntV Graph Library)

## Status

- **Decision:** Superseded by the d3-force engine ([ADR-020 amendment](020-mobile-performance-static-svg-fallback-strategy.md#amendment-2026-10-22-matrix-first-the-graph-on-open-d3-force-as-the-engine)).
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/graphEngine) through the d3-force engine that replaced it. The AntV engine named here was used for a while and then removed. Also [D3_Library](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/staticresources/D3_Library.js)

Superseded by the d3-force engine (2026-10-22, [ADR-020 amendment](020-mobile-performance-static-svg-fallback-strategy.md#amendment-2026-10-22-matrix-first-the-graph-on-open-d3-force-as-the-engine)). Originally Accepted. The Decision below records the original choice of the AntV graph library, which no longer holds: see the note at the end.

## Context

Requirement for animated, "IcePanel-style" flow lines in the skill network.

## Decision

Select the AntV graph library over Vis.js as the visualization engine. (Superseded: the site uses d3-force, and the AntV library was removed on 2026-10-22.)

## Rationale

The AntV library supports native "running line" animations that would require complex canvas hacks in Vis.js.

## Implications

Requires Lightning Web Security (LWS) to be enabled in the org.

## Note (2026-10-22): the engine is now d3-force

The engine choice was revisited on 2026-10-22. Neither Vis.js nor the AntV library is used: the site draws its graphs with `d3-force` and its three dependencies in the `D3_Library` static resource, and the AntV library is removed. The reasons were the size (1.57 MB for the AntV library against about 18.5 KB for the four d3 modules), the tangle the AntV force layout made of the 59 skills production held in October 2026, and the wish for one engine for two diagrams, the skills graph and the Pillar A ERD. The animated "running line" that motivated the AntV library is no longer a goal: the graph is drawn once as SVG and nothing animates. The decision and the mobile rule are in the [ADR-020 amendment (2026-10-22)](020-mobile-performance-static-svg-fallback-strategy.md#amendment-2026-10-22-matrix-first-the-graph-on-open-d3-force-as-the-engine).

# ADR-011: Context Grounding Strategy (Direct CRM vs. Data 360)

## Status

- **Decision:** Deferred (2026-10-22, see the amendment below).
- **Build:** Designed. Grounding stays in Apex and nothing reads Data 360.

Deferred (2026-10-22, see the amendment below). Originally Accepted.

## Context

Need for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) source for Agentforce that avoids tight coupling with transactional data.

## Decision

Utilize Data 360 as the Trusted Context Layer.

## Rationale

Establishes separation of concerns and supports hybrid search (Vector + Semantic) across structured and unstructured data.

## Implications

Requires a provisioned Data 360 instance and manual configuration of data streams.

## Amendment (2026-10-22): deferred

I deferred this decision on 2026-10-22 (in the Pillar D design). The decision above is the target design. None of it is built, and nothing in the site or the API reads Data 360.

**What is built.** Grounding stays in Apex and reads the CRM directly. `PortfolioGroundingService.build(jobTitle, jobDescription)` selects featured `Project__c` rows and `Experience_Highlight__c` text through a `without sharing` selector with a fixed field list, ranks them by keywords from the job title and description, strips anything shaped like an email address or phone number, and returns at most 8,000 characters of JSON for the prompt. The cover letter page (`ApiLabController`) and `/papi/v1/ai/generate` (`PAPIAiGenerate`) both reach it through `ContentGenerationController.groundingSection` (SAS section 5.4.1).

**What exists in Data 360.** The production org has 14 data streams in the `default` data space, one per portfolio object, fed by the CRM connector. It has no search index and no retriever. Checked read-only on 2026-10-22: `SELECT COUNT() FROM DataStream` returns 14 and `SELECT COUNT() FROM DataSemanticSearch` returns 0.

**Why it is deferred.**

- Agentforce is deferred (decision 2026-10-02), so there is no Agentforce provider for a Data 360 retriever to ground.
- The data set is small: a handful of projects and about ten roles. Keyword ranking in Apex finds the same records an index would, so an index would not improve the letter.
- Index builds and queries are metered, and a Developer Edition caps Data 360 at 1,000 queries a day. Whether the edition carries any credit allowance is not documented.

**What would reopen it.** A real Agentforce provider (deferred, see [ADR-015](015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md)) and a reason to search text that keyword ranking cannot reach. Until then no document in this repository claims Data 360 grounding.

## Amendment (2026-10-26): the Agentforce provider now exists

The first reason above no longer holds. Agentforce is built as a Prompt Builder template and ships on ([ADR-015 amendment of 2026-10-26](015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md#amendment-2026-10-26-agentforce-is-built-and-the-deferral-is-lifted)). Data 360 grounding stays deferred for the other two reasons: the data set is small, and index builds and queries are metered. What would reopen it is now a reason to search text that keyword ranking cannot reach, and nothing else.

# ADR-013: Structured Logging Framework (Nebula Logger)

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/PortfolioLog.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

Requirement for persistent logs even during Apex transaction rollbacks.

## Decision

Adopt the Nebula Logger open-source framework.

## Rationale

Uses Platform Events for decoupled log persistence and provides a unified adapter for LWC and Apex.

## Implications

Requires a strict 2-day retention policy to manage storage limits in Developer Edition.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): an optional install behind a seam

**Nebula Logger is an optional dependency I install, reached through a seam** (my decision, 2026-10-21).

- I install Nebula Logger's unlocked, no-namespace package in production by hand. It is not in source, CI and scratch orgs run without it, and no source file names a Nebula type.
- `PortfolioLog` is the seam. It looks up Nebula's `System.Callable` entry point, `CallableLogger`, at run time with `Type.forName` (with or without the `Nebula` namespace) and sends each line through its `newEntry` action with the tag `portfolio`. When Nebula is absent, or the call fails, the line goes to `System.debug`, and a logging failure never reaches the caller.
- Every API request writes one line, `api request path=<path> status=<status> correlationId=<id> elapsedMs=<ms>`, through `RequestUtil.logRequest`, after the response is written (`ApiRequestContext`). The path loses its query string, and no body, header value or token is logged. The site cover letter writes the same line with the path `aura:ApiLabController.generateCoverLetter`.
- Retention stays 2 days, as my setting in Nebula once it is installed.

# ADR-012: Guest User Security (Restriction Rules)

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/restrictionRules/Block_Unapproved_Testimonials.rule-meta.xml), also [TestimonialGuestAccessTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/TestimonialGuestAccessTest.cls)

Accepted, made real on 2026-10-23 (see the amendment below).

## Context

Standard sharing rules are additive and prone to accidental over-exposure.

## Decision

Implement Restriction Rules on the Testimonial\_\_c object.

## Rationale

Enforces a "Block First" policy for unapproved content at the kernel level, adhering to Zero Trust principles.

## Implications

Operates as a hard filter on record visibility specifically for the Guest User profile.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): the rule now does the filtering

Until 2026-10-23 the guest could not read any testimonial, so `Block_Unapproved_Testimonials` filtered nothing. The testimonial wall needs the guest to read approved rows, so a guest sharing rule, `Guest_Read_Testimonials`, shares every testimonial read only with the guest, and the restriction rule alone hides the unapproved ones.

That this holds is proven, not assumed: `TestimonialGuestAccessTest.theGuestNeverReadsAnUnapprovedTestimonial` runs as the real site guest over the seeded rows. With the restriction rule deployed inactive it fails, because the guest reads the pending row, and with the rule active it passes. `TestimonialController.getApprovedTestimonials` also filters on `Approved__c = true`, so the wall would stay correct even without the rule, and the rule protects every other path a guest could take to the object.

## Amendment (2026-11-14): skills and projects are filtered at the sharing layer

The skill network and the project gallery read `Skill__c` and `Project__c` through GraphQL as the guest in user mode, so the Apex filter on `Is_Verified__c` does not reach them. For these two objects I chose a criteria based guest sharing rule over a restriction rule. External access to both is Private, and `Guest_Read_All_Skills` and `Guest_Read_All_Projects` share a row with the guest only when `Is_Verified__c` is true. The rules keep their older API names so a deploy updates them in place. The join objects and `Project_Asset__c` are master detail to a skill or a project, so they follow their parents. The guest gets no read on `Is_Verified__c`. The guest shares are written after a record commits, so `GuestVerifiedSharingTest` proves the guest never reads an unverified row, and a check against committed records in a scratch org showed a verified row is shared and an unverified one is not. The static build reads the same GraphQL as the build user, who sees every row, so the build drops the rows that reach an unverified skill or project after each query (`web/build/verified.mjs`), and the static pages match what the guest reads.
