# ADR-015: Strategy Pattern for Generative AI

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/ContentGenerationController.cls), also [ContentGenerationControllerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/ContentGenerationControllerTest.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-20, three times on 2026-10-21, and twice on 2026-10-26 (see below). The deferral of Agentforce was lifted on 2026-10-26.

## Context

Agentforce in Developer Edition environments has transactional limits and a call cap of 150 LLM generations an hour. It was first judged prone to cold-start timeouts. That was measured on 2026-10-26 and 27 in a scratch org: a cover letter called directly took 2.7 to 3.5 seconds (333 to 340 words), and the first call through the API after a quiet period took 13.7 seconds, then 2.9 to 3.2 seconds. Production is not measured yet.

## Decision

Implement the Strategy Pattern via the IAIGenerationService Apex interface.

## Rationale

Decouples the UI from the AI provider, allowing seamless failover between Agentforce, Gemini, and Local Templates to ensure zero user "dead ends".

## Implications

Requires maintaining standardized response wrappers across AgentforceService, GeminiService, and LocalTemplateService.

## Amendment (2026-10-20)

**Agentforce is deferred.** `AgentforceService` is a mock: `AgentforceService.generateContent` returns the fixed string `Agentforce response for: <prompt>` and `isAvailable` always returns true. No Agentforce agent, topic or Models API call is built in source, and none is built while the deferral stands. No document may present Agentforce as the primary ("Gold") path, because the only thing that path can return is the mock's string. The Strategy Pattern and the `IAIGenerationService` interface stand; the providers that can serve real content are Gemini (`GeminiService`) and the deterministic Local Template (`LocalTemplateService`).

## Amendment (2026-10-21)

**Two dispatch paths now exist.**

- `ContentGenerationController.generateCoverLetter` (the `@AuraEnabled` entry point for the site's cover-letter page) keeps its original chain, Agentforce first, by decision (2026-10-20). Because `AgentforceService.isAvailable` always returns true and `AgentforceService.generateContent` returns the mock string, this method always returns `Agentforce response for: <prompt>`; Gemini and the Local Template are never reached from it. No document may present that page as live AI content until Agentforce is built.
- `ContentGenerationController.generateWithoutAgentforce`, used by `PAPIAiGenerate.generate` (`POST /papi/v1/ai/generate`), tries Gemini and then, for cover letters only, the Local Template. It never consults Agentforce. It is the path that reaches a real model.

**Model.** `GeminiService.MODEL` is `gemma-4-31b-it`, the code default used only when the `Gemini` record names no model (Gemma 4 31B through the Gemini API, `Gemini_API` Named Credential, decision of 2026-10-20). The model in use is set on the `Gemini` record, `gemini-2.5-flash` since 2026-10-26 (see the amendment below). `gemini-2.0-flash`, the model before, was shut down by Google on 2026-06-01. The key's free tier allowed Gemma 4 31B 30 requests per minute, 16,000 tokens per minute and 14,400 requests per day when read on 2026-10-20. `GeminiService.generateContent` reports a failure as text starting `Error: Unable to generate content.` or `Exception: ` instead of throwing, and `generateWithoutAgentforce` treats such text as a failed attempt.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): one dispatch and the provider switch

**One dispatch replaces both paths.** This supersedes the two-path description in the amendment above.

- `ContentGenerationController.dispatch` is the only provider chain. It tries Agentforce, then Gemini, then the Local Template (cover letters only), and records every attempt with its outcome (`served`, `skipped_off`, `failed`) and elapsed time.
- **Agentforce is a switch, and the switch is off.** `AgentforceService.isAvailable` reads the `Agentforce` record of the new `AI_Provider_Config__mdt`, which ships with `Enabled__c` false. It is also false when no record exists and for a site guest. Agentforce itself is still not implemented: `AgentforceService.generateContent` throws. So even with the switch on, the dispatch records a failed attempt and Gemini serves. No response names Agentforce unless a real Agentforce call wrote the content.
- **Gemini** is `gemini-2.5-flash` through the Gemini API (the model on the `Gemini` record, see the amendment of 2026-10-26), with a 60 second callout timeout read from the `Gemini` record (my decision 2026-10-21, replacing the 20 seconds first planned). The first choice, Gemma 4 31B (`gemma-4-31b-it`), always reasons before it answers, and I measured 28.7 seconds for a trivial prompt.
- **Local Template** serves cover letters when Gemini fails. Other content types answer 503 `ALL_PROVIDERS_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `PAPIAiGenerate` (`POST /papi/v1/ai/generate`) calls the dispatch, and its response adds `latencyMs`, `attempts` and `promptShown`.
- **The cover letter page proxies through the API.** `coverLetterGenerator` calls `ApiLabController.generateCoverLetter`, which posts to `/papi/v1/ai/generate` through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential with a 90 second timeout, longer than the Gemini timeout plus the API overhead, so a slow model falls through to the Local Template inside the API instead of the page call failing first. The letter is written by the integration user under the API's validation and its 10 per minute `ai` rate tier, and the site guest needs no AI grant. `generateWithoutAgentforce` is removed, and `generateCoverLetter` on the controller now returns the same result object as the dispatch.
- **Grounding.** A cover letter prompt carries featured projects and experience highlights from `PortfolioGroundingService`, chosen by keywords from the job. It never includes an email address, a phone number or an owner field, and stays under 8,000 characters.
- **Show your work.** The page shows the provider and model on a badge read from the response, and a panel the visitor opens to see the fallback flag, latency, the attempts and the prompt that was sent.
- The metal names for the providers are dropped. The order is first, second and last resort.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): the site cover letter dispatches in process

**The site cover letter dispatches in process.** This supersedes the "cover letter page proxies through the API" bullet of the amendment above, for the page only (my decision, 2026-10-21).

- **Why.** The page as first built reached Gemini by calling the org's own `/papi/v1/ai/generate` through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential. A request that arrives as a callout from the same org may not call out again, so `GeminiService` failed at once with `System.CalloutException: Callout loop not allowed` and every live letter came from the Local Template. Apex tests mocked both callouts, so they could not see it.
- **What changed.** `ApiLabController.generateCoverLetter` keeps its signature and its `CoverLetterResult`, drops the `Portfolio_API` callout, and calls `ContentGenerationController.dispatch` in process, as the site guest. One callout leaves the org (to Gemini), so there is no loop.
- **The guest's grant.** `Portfolio_Guest` gains the `Gemini_Auth-Gemini_Principal` principal and nothing else for this. Agentforce is never consulted for a guest (`AgentforceService.isAvailable` is false for a site guest).
- **The limit still applies.** Before the dispatch the page path checks the key `papi-ai:site-cover-letter` (`ApiLabController.AI_RATE_KEY`) with `ApiRequestContext.rateLimiter().checkKey` at the AI tier's 10 requests a minute, and writes the count after the dispatch with `ApiRequestContext.commitRateCounts()`, never before the Gemini callout. It is one bucket shared by every site visitor, separate from the API's session keys. It carries the `papi-ai` prefix that `/papi/v1/ai/` uses, so the footer's "AI requests today" counts both paths.
- **Grounding as the guest.** The guest sees only rows shared to it, so the page's grounding reads featured projects and experience highlights through a `without sharing` selector that returns a fixed shape with no email, phone or owner field.
- **`/papi/v1/ai/generate` stays** for outside callers with a Bearer token, unchanged.

## Amendment (2026-10-26): the model on the Gemini record is gemini-2.5-flash

The `Gemini` record of `AI_Provider_Config__mdt` now names `gemini-2.5-flash`. Gemma 4 31B did not answer a full cover letter prompt within the 60 second callout timeout, so every live letter fell back to the local template. Gemini 2.5 Flash answered one grounded letter in about 11 seconds in a scratch org. `GeminiService.MODEL` stays `gemma-4-31b-it` as the code default, used only when the record names no model, and the badge and the "Show your work" panel report whichever model answered.

The key's free tier allowed Gemini 2.5 Flash 5 requests per minute and 20 requests per day when it was read from the AI Studio rate limit page on 2026-10-20. That is a recorded reading, not a live one, and the template serves a cover letter once Google refuses. In the same scratch org test the second Flash call was refused with HTTP 503 and the template served. A live letter is therefore a best effort, and the template is the guaranteed answer.

## Amendment (2026-10-26): Agentforce is built and the deferral is lifted

This supersedes the 2026-10-20 deferral and the "switch ships off" description in the 2026-10-21 amendments.

- **What runs.** `AgentforceService` runs the Prompt Builder template `Portfolio_Cover_Letter` through `ConnectApi.EinsteinLLM.generateMessagesForPromptTemplate`, behind the `PromptTemplateClient` interface (the real client is `EinsteinPromptTemplateClient`, with the application name `PromptTemplateGenerationsInvocable`, without which the call fails). The platform documents no test hook for this API, so the interface exists to take a stub. The template has one input, `Input:Prompt` (`primitive://String`), and its content is `{!$Input:Prompt}` plus one line that holds the letter to the word range the prompt asks for. Its model is `sfdc_ai__DefaultGPT41`. The prompt the dispatch builds is the prompt the model reads.
- **The switch ships on.** The `Agentforce` record of `AI_Provider_Config__mdt` has `Enabled__c` true, `Timeout_Ms__c` 20000 and `Model_Or_Template__c` `Portfolio_Cover_Letter`. `AgentforceService.isAvailable` is still false for a site guest, because a guest may not run generative AI.
- **How a visitor's letter reaches it.** The AI Lab runs as the site guest. `ApiLabController.generateCoverLetter` first posts to `/papi/v1/ai/generate` with `provider` set to `Agentforce` through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential, so the template runs as the integration user. A 200 is the letter. Anything else runs the dispatch in process from Gemini on, then the template, with the Agentforce attempt first in the attempts list. Gemini is never asked through the API, for the callout loop reason in the amendment of 2026-10-21. Connect worked inside a request that arrived as a same org callout in a scratch org (a Remote Site Setting stood in for the Named Credential, so the production proof call settles that exact path).
- **The worst case fits.** Apex allows 120 seconds of callouts in a transaction. The Agentforce timeout is the record's 20 seconds, capped to what Gemini's timeout leaves of the 120 seconds less a 2 second margin (`ApiLabController.CALLOUT_BUDGET_MS`).
- **A budget under the cap.** Agentforce is held to `Hourly_Budget__c` (120) calls per UTC hour, under the Developer Edition's 150. The count is one `API_Rate_Window__c` row per hour, key `agentforce-hour|yyyyMMddHH`, read before the template runs. Past it the attempt is `budget_exhausted` and the chain moves on. The read takes no lock, so calls in flight together can pass the budget by a few, inside the 30 left under 150.
- **The breaker.** A 429 or an answer from the limiter never counts as a breaker failure, and neither does a 401. Only no answer, or a 200 with no letter, does.
- **The last fallback is a real letter.** `LocalTemplateService` builds the letter in Apex from the records with no model: company and role, the current title, years on Salesforce, current certifications and up to three ranked highlights or projects. Its last line says no model wrote it.
- **A Published template cannot be changed by deploy.** A deploy that changes one reports Succeeded and changes nothing. A later wording change is a new version made in Prompt Builder.
- **API.** `POST /papi/v1/ai/generate` accepts `provider` with the one value `Agentforce`. With it only Agentforce is tried, and a failure is 503 `ALL_PROVIDERS_UNAVAILABLE`. The attempts outcome gains `skipped_open_circuit` and `budget_exhausted`.
- **Measured.** In a scratch org on 2026-10-26 and 27, three cover letters called directly took 2.7 to 3.5 seconds and came back at 333 to 340 words. Production is not measured yet and is my proof call after the merge.

## Amendment (2026-10-27): the production proof call, and the letter length

This answers the "Measured" line of the amendment of 2026-10-26. The rest of that amendment stands.

- **Production proof call.** On 2026-10-27, after the deploy, one letter was requested on the live AI Lab as a site guest. It was written by Agentforce (`Portfolio_Cover_Letter`) in 418 words, 10 seconds from page load to letter, grounded on the real records, with no client name, email or phone. The route through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential as the integration user works end to end. A second walk of the live journey the same day wrote two letters of 439 and 398 words.
- **The length.** Those letters ran over `Cover_Letter_Max_Words` (350), because production's records are fuller than a scratch org's. The Published template adds its own sentence for a `Length` line (write toward the upper number, in three body paragraphs of five sentences), which pushed letters past the maximum. The prompt's length line is now a word limit line that does not start with "Length", states 350 as a hard maximum and fixes a five paragraph shape, so the template needs no new version.
- **Measured after the change.** In a scratch org loaded with production's grounding records, six letters in a row came back at 277 to 322 words (nine Agentforce calls, 2026-10-27). Production lengths after the deploy that carries the line are not measured yet.

# ADR-019: Executable Governance – Platform Events for Documentation Logic

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/GovernanceController.cls), also [GovernanceControllerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/GovernanceControllerTest.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

Requirement to prove that documentation is a "living" asset rather than static text.

## Decision

Implement Executable Governance via the Governance_Notification\_\_e Platform Event and the c-smart-docs component.

## Rationale

Allows the UI to react in real-time to system state changes (e.g., CI/CD deployment completion), proving the candidate understands event-driven architecture.

## Implications

Requires the implementation of a subscription model in LWC using lightning/empApi.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): the event, the subscriber and the page

The decision stands: executable governance through a platform event. The names, the subscriber and the browser side change (my decisions, 2026-10-21).

- **One event name, one component name.** The event is `Governance_Event__e`, as the SAS and the existing component have it. The component is `smartChecklist` (`c-smart-checklist`). `Governance_Notification__e` and `c-smart-docs` are retired names.
- **The subscriber is on the server.** CI publishes the event after a production deploy (`deploy.yml`) and after the daily heartbeat (`keep-alive.yml`), each as that workflow's existing JWT user. An Apex trigger on the event persists it as a `Pipeline_Run__c` record, upserted by the `Run_Key__c` external id, so a replayed event changes nothing. The trigger runs asynchronously in its own transaction.
- **Why `lightning/empApi` is out.** Salesforce lists `lightning-emp-api` as unsupported in LWR sites, and even where it is supported each subscribed browser counts as one of the org's 20 concurrent streaming clients, which a public site would exhaust. A guest has no session or OAuth token for Pub/Sub API either. So no visitor's browser subscribes to anything.
- **How the page reads it.** `smartChecklist` reads `GovernanceController.getPipelineStatus()` (cacheable Apex: the latest run per workflow plus the age of the integration caches) when the page is viewed, and again with `refreshApex` when the tab becomes visible (`visibilitychange`). There is no timer and no polling loop.
- **What the checklist claims.** Three items, each from evidence, never from code: the production deploy is green (from `deploy.yml`), the org heartbeat ran in the last 26 hours (from `keep-alive.yml`), and the integration caches are under 30 minutes old (computed in the org). An item with no data shows "No signal yet", never a tick. Test coverage on production is not claimed.
- **When.** It was built before launch, not after.
- The workflow publish steps are my edits to `.github/workflows/**`, made after the event exists in production.

## Amendment (2026-10-23)

A third workflow publishes the event. After a production deploy that changed something, the Live Smoke Test (`smoke.yml`, run by `scripts/live-smoke.js`) checks the live site read only, and on a failure publishes `Governance_Event__e` with `Workflow__c` set to `smoke` and status Failure. `GovernanceEventHandler` accepts `smoke` beside `deploy` and `heartbeat`, so the row lands as `smoke:<run id>`. A pass writes no row. The Delivery checklist and the Pillar E card read only deploy and heartbeat rows, so neither changes.

# ADR-017: System API Security & Dual-Sided Auth Pattern

## Status

- **Decision:** Superseded by [ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md) on 2026-10-01.
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/externalCredentials/Portfolio_API_Auth.externalCredential-meta.xml) through ADR-027, which replaced the custom metadata header check. Also [Integration_Access](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/permissionsets/Integration_Access.permissionset-meta.xml)

Superseded by [ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md) on 2026-10-01. The custom-metadata header validation described below was a stand-in for a MuleSoft policy enforcement point; with MuleSoft removed from the architecture, authentication moved to platform-native OAuth 2.0 (External Client App + Named Credential). The read-only constraint is carried forward unchanged. Amended 2026-10-20 (see below).

## Context

The architecture requires secure, stateless authentication between the Process Layer (PAPI) and System Layer (SAPI), mirroring an enterprise Mutual TLS or Client Credential flow.

## Decision

Implement a **Dual-Sided Client Credential** pattern using explicit header validation.

## Rationale

Establishes a clear separation of concerns between the "Consumer" (PAPI) and the "Provider" (SAPI), allowing for independent credential rotation and policy enforcement.

## Implications

- **Outbound (PAPI Layer):** The orchestration layer (simulated on AWS/MuleSoft) acts as the secure client. It retrieves the `client_id` and `client_secret` from a **Secure Vault** (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) to sign the outbound request.
- **Inbound (SAPI Layer):** The Salesforce runtime acts as the API Gateway. It validates the incoming headers against `Portfolio_Config__mdt` (Custom Metadata) to simulate an API Policy enforcement point.
- **Constraints:** Write access is strictly prohibited; non-GET methods return 405 Method Not Allowed.

## Amendment (2026-10-20)

Nothing described above is in force. Inbound authentication is the **Portfolio API** External Client App (Client Credentials flow, run as the integration user); outbound calls use the `Portfolio_API_Auth` External Credential and the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential ([ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md)). No custom metadata takes part in authentication: `Portfolio_Config__mdt` holds no credential fields, and no Apex class reads a `client_id` or `client_secret` header.

# ADR-018: FinOps Constraint – AWS Lambda Function URLs vs. API Gateway

## Status

- **Decision:** Deferred (2026-10-23), like [ADR-016](016-cloudflare-worker-as-edge-ai-proxy.md).
- **Build:** Designed. No AWS code exists in the repository.

Deferred (2026-10-23), like [ADR-016](016-cloudflare-worker-as-edge-ai-proxy.md). Originally Accepted. No AWS code exists in the repository and no Lambda function serves the portfolio. The decision stands as the Phase 8 design and takes effect only if Phase 8 is built.

## Context

Phase 8 requires an external polyglot gateway while maintaining a "$0.00 forever" guarantee.

## Decision

Utilize AWS Lambda Function URLs instead of Amazon API Gateway.

## Rationale

Standard AWS API Gateway free tiers expire after 12 months, whereas Function URLs are a permanent feature of the Lambda service.

## Implications

Requires moving security logic (API Key validation, rate limiting) inside the Lambda function code.

# ADR-020: Mobile Performance – Static SVG Fallback Strategy

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/skillNetwork), also [graphEngine](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/graphEngine)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-22, see the amendment below. Note added 2026-10-22 on the Lighthouse claim, and a second note on 2026-10-30.

## Context

The animated skill graph, drawn with the AntV graph library, violates performance budgets (LCP < 2.5s) on low-power mobile devices.

## Decision

Implement a Static SVG Fallback for small viewports.

## Rationale

Prevents heavy canvas rendering on mobile, ensuring the site passes Lighthouse performance audits on 4G networks.

> **Note, 2026-10-22.** The site does not pass the 2.5 s mobile LCP target. Removing the graph from phones took the graph engine off the mobile critical path, but most of the mobile LCP is render delay in the LWR framework's own script, which the site's files do not control, and it stays above 2.5 s. The gate is now the best the LWR shell allows, measured: mobile LCP medians of 7.5 to 9.6 s (Lighthouse 11 mobile, measured 2026-10-22) on the six main routes ([Technical Guide §2.11](../guides/04-Technical-Guide.md#211-mobile-performance)).

> **Note, 2026-10-30.** The production baseline of 2026-10-29 is wider, 7.57 to 10.62 s. A throttled trace shows the first site component rendering at about 5 s, after about 850 KB of framework scripts and styles, so the 2.5 s target is not reachable by site changes alone. I keep it as the target and it is not met. The October 2026 changes (lazy data model dialog, lazy gallery read, reserved space on home) proved one gain, home layout shift from 0.33 to 0. Removing the platform stylesheets was tried and not shipped because it broke the card styling on four pages (Technical Guide §2.11).

## Implications

Requires FORM_FACTOR detection in the c-skill-network LWC.

## Amendment (2026-10-22): matrix first, the graph on open, d3-force as the engine

I replaced the static SVG fallback and the AntV graph on 2026-10-22. The ERD on the Pillar A page follows the same rule.

**Decision.**

- **The skills page shows a matrix by default.** One row per category, the skills as chips with their proficiency and "years used". Years used is worked out from the dates of the roles linked to the skill through `Experience_Skill__c`, with overlapping roles merged and a current role counted to today. A skill with no linked role shows no years.
- **The graph is a second view, loaded only when it is opened.** A "Matrix | Graph" switch sits above the matrix on desktop and tablet. The engine is requested the first time the graph view opens and never before.
- **Phones never request the engine.** On `FORM_FACTOR` `Small` or a viewport under 768 px the switch is hidden and the page shows the matrix only. The ERD on the Pillar A page shows its accessible list of objects and relationships as the visible view.
- **The engine is d3-force.** `d3-force` with its three dependencies (`d3-dispatch`, `d3-quadtree`, `d3-timer`), the official UMD builds concatenated into the `D3_Library` static resource, loaded through the shared module `c/graphEngine`. The simulation runs to completion and the components draw the positioned nodes and edges as SVG from their own templates, so nothing animates and reduced motion is honoured by construction.
- **The AntV library leaves the site.** The `G6_Library` static resource (1.57 MB) and the `c/g6Loader` module are removed, with their entry in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

**Why.**

- With the 59 skills production held in October 2026, the AntV force layout packed every skill into one tangle (my feedback, 2026-10-21). A matrix reads at a glance on any screen, and the graph clusters skills by category with the roles and projects on a ring, drawing edges only for the hovered or selected node.
- Size. `D3_Library` was 18,544 bytes on 2026-10-22 against 1.57 MB for the AntV library (81,502 bytes since 2026-10-23, see the amendment below).
- One engine draws both diagrams, the skills graph and the ERD.
- A build-time SVG of live data goes stale, which the ERD must not do, and the matrix already serves phones from live data.

**Implications.** Planned on 2026-10-22 and reconciled with the engine branch at merge. The engine contract is `loadGraphEngine(component)` and `layoutGraph(d3, nodes, edges, options)` in `c/graphEngine` (Technical Guide section 2.1). The earlier inline SVG for small screens is replaced by the matrix.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): pan, zoom and node drag

The graph view gains pan, zoom and node drag. `D3_Library` appends the official UMD builds of d3-selection, d3-color, d3-interpolate, d3-ease, d3-transition, d3-drag and d3-zoom, unchanged, so the resource grows from 18,544 to 81,502 bytes. The mobile rule stands: the resource still loads only when the graph view opens, and phones never request it. Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset view are buttons for keyboard users, and the zoom level is announced politely. Nothing animates on its own, so reduced motion still needs no special case (Technical Guide §2.1).

## Amendment (2026-10-23): the wheel scrolls the page, and the graph pans at every zoom

A plain mouse wheel over the graph now scrolls the page at every zoom level, and only Ctrl with the wheel, or a trackpad pinch, zooms, one step at a time. Before, a wheel up at 100% zoomed in. I chose that the wheel keeps scrolling the page at rest. A background drag or the arrow keys on the focused graph pan it at any zoom, 100% included, up to 120 units past the graph's edge, with a visible hint while it has focus. The buttons stay, and Reset view also returns dragged nodes. The mobile rule is unchanged: phones never request `D3_Library` (Technical Guide §2.1).

## Amendment (2026-10-26): evidence, a fitted view and an eased zoom on a button press

The skills graph gains three things, and the rule that nothing animates on its own stays as written.

- **Evidence.** Certifications join roles and projects as nodes, served by `SkillGraphController` because the guest cannot read them through GraphQL. Each skill's ring weighs the kinds of evidence behind it (a role, a project, a certification, never the number of rows), its lines step up the same way when shown, and a legend says what the weights mean.
- **A fitted view.** The graph opens fitted to its content. The ring radii follow the node counts, a label placement pass puts each label right, left, above or below its node where it covers nothing, and a Fit button and a Reset layout button join the zoom buttons. Dragged nodes stay where they were put for the visit, kept in `sessionStorage`. `c/graphEngine` gains an opt in `fitTo` and takes a minimum zoom from its caller, so the engine's defaults, and the ERD's pinned numbers that depend on them, do not move. The ERD opts in to the same fit.
- **Motion.** The view eases for about 250 ms, and only after the visitor presses Fit, Reset layout, Zoom in or Zoom out. Under the system "reduce motion" setting it moves at once. The layout still runs to completion before anything is drawn, and nothing moves on its own.

## Amendment (2026-11-12): the notes above describe the Salesforce site

The two notes in the Rationale, with their 7.5 to 9.6 s and 7.57 to 10.62 s figures, measured the Experience Cloud site, and they stay as that history. The public front end is now the static site ([ADR-041](041-headless-static-front-end-on-cloudflare-pages.md)). Its production Lighthouse audit of 2026-11-12 measured mobile LCP medians of 2.2 to 2.9 s on the six main routes, which is lab data and not a Core Web Vitals result ([Technical Guide §2.11](../guides/04-Technical-Guide.md#211-mobile-performance)). The original decision is unchanged: phones get the matrix and the graph engine loads only on demand.

# ADR-022: Resilience Engineering – Resilience Simulation Toggle

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/outageSimulation), also [CircuitBreakerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/CircuitBreakerTest.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-21, 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30 (see below).

## Context

Need to reduce recruiter "Time-to-Trust" by proving the system's resilience under failure.

## Decision

Implement a "Resilience Simulation" toggle (formerly Chaos Mode) within the Glass Box footer.

## Rationale

Allows evaluators to manually force integrations into failure states to observe the "Indefinite Degraded Mode" and circuit breakers in real-time.

## Implications

Requires state management (Session Cache) to track simulation status and mock 500 errors in service classes.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): the breaker state and the toggle

The decision stands. The state and the toggle are built differently from the implications above.

- **No Session Cache.** The org has no Platform Cache partition, and the project decided against Platform Cache. Breaker state lives in the list custom setting `Circuit_Breaker_State__c` (one row per dependency, with `Consecutive_Failures__c`, `Open_Until__c` and `Last_Failure_At__c`), read and written by the `CircuitBreaker` class.
- **The breaker.** `CircuitBreaker` (`isOpen`, `openUntil`, `recordSuccess`, `recordFailure`, `snapshot`), keys `github`, `jira`, `gemini` and `agentforce`. Three consecutive failures open the circuit for 30 minutes. After that the next call is tried: a success closes it, a failure opens it for 30 more minutes. A skipped provider is recorded as `skipped_open_circuit`. The GitHub and Jira refresh jobs skip their callout while their circuit is open, and `ContentGenerationController.dispatch` skips Gemini (or Agentforce) while theirs is open and serves the next provider. State is written only after the callouts in a transaction, never before one.
- **The toggle is a visible switch, "Simulate an outage", in the roadmap card, driving the roadmap and Latest Updates together**, off by default, not in the footer. It passes `simulate` to `DeliveryController.getRecentCommits(Boolean simulate)` and `getRoadmap(Boolean simulate)`, which return the cached data marked `SIMULATED` and make no callout. No service class mocks a 500, and nothing the visitor does changes stored state.
- **What the visitor sees:** `SIMULATED` while the switch is on, `DEGRADED` while the real breaker for that source is open, and in both cases the last good data with its age.

## Amendment (2026-10-29): the before and after for the outage switch

The decision stands. The switch now shows a before and after beside the panel it affects.

- While the "Simulate an outage" switch is on and a panel's feed is `SIMULATED`, the roadmap and Latest Updates show `c-outage-compare` above their content.
- It sets a static, labelled illustration of a panel with no saved copy and no breaker beside a three step trace of what the panel really does. Step one says no call was made to the source. Step two says the breaker counts a failed refresh and opens at 3 in a row for 30 minutes. Step three says the panel shows the last saved copy with its age.
- `DEGRADED`, a real open breaker, does not show it.
- **The numbers are text, not settings.** The 3 and the 30 are the `CircuitBreaker` defaults and the values of the `Circuit_Failure_Threshold` and `Circuit_Open_Minutes` settings, but they are written into the component's wording. If I change either setting, I change the wording too.

## Amendment (2026-10-30): the outage text reads the settings

This replaces the last bullet of the 2026-10-29 amendment. The decision and the rest stand.

- **The numbers come from the settings.** `DeliveryController.getRoadmap` and `getChangelog` return `failureThreshold` and `openMinutes` on the feed, read from `CircuitBreaker.failureThreshold()` and `openMinutes()`. Those read the `Circuit_Failure_Threshold` and `Circuit_Open_Minutes` settings and fall back to the code defaults of 3 and 30.
- **The components pass them on.** `c-roadmap-viewer` and `c-changelog` hand both numbers to `c-outage-compare`. The component holds no default of its own.
- **A missing number is left out.** When the threshold is missing the step reads "After repeated failures in a row it opens". When the open minutes are missing it leaves out the "for N minutes" part. It never shows a made up number.
- **Why.** The 2026-10-29 wording typed the 3 and the 30, so a change to either setting left the page telling visitors something untrue. Now the page changes with the setting and I edit nothing.

# ADR-021: Native GraphQL (Door 1) vs. Apex REST for UI

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/graphqlProbe), also [skillNetwork](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/lwc/skillNetwork)

Accepted, with its scope narrowed (2026-10-23, see the amendment below). GraphQL is used by three components, not for core frontend orchestration. Amended 2026-10-30: the gallery's read moved into a lazy child.

## Context

LWR components require efficient, multi-object data fetching without multiple REST round-trips.

## Decision

Utilize native Salesforce GraphQL (lightning/uiGraphQLApi) for core frontend orchestration.

## Rationale

Provides automatic caching via Lightning Data Service (LDS) and reduces payload size by fetching only essential fields.

## Implications

Requires components to be built with wire adapters.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): scope

**As built, GraphQL is one path among two, not the main one.** Three components read through `lightning/uiGraphQLApi`:

- `c-skill-network`: skills, their junctions and the linked roles' dates for the skills matrix and graph.
- `c-project-asset-gallery`: a pillar's `Project__c` with its `Project_Assets__r`.
- `c-graphql-probe`: one small `Skill__c` read the footer times and reports as "GraphQL: live, N ms" or "unavailable".

Every other component reads through `@AuraEnabled` Apex: the resume and its timeline (`ResumeController`), the pillar cards (`ProjectCardController`), the Delivery page (`DeliveryController`, `GovernanceController`), the footer (`FooterController`), the ERD (`SchemaService`), the decision matrix (`DecisionMatrixController`), testimonials (`TestimonialController`) and the API Lab and cover letter (`ApiLabController`).

**Why Apex for those.** GraphQL reads only what the guest has object and field permission for. Much of what the site shows sits on records the guest cannot read: my Contact, experience highlights, the integration caches, custom metadata, and data that is computed rather than stored (the schema describe, the decision matrix ranking inputs, the governor limits). Those go through Apex controllers that read in system mode and return a fixed shape (SAS section 4.6). The Delivery page reads Apex because each cache is one JSON row per refresh, not one record per item (my decision, 2026-10-21). The hero and cards read Apex because the Apex adapter is already on the home page and the GraphQL adapter stack is kept off it until the page is idle (Technical Guide §2.11).

**What stays true.** Where a component reads plain records the guest may see, GraphQL is the default, and the footer measures that path on every visit.

## Amendment (2026-10-30): the gallery's read moved to a lazy child

The count stays at three components, but one of them changed. `c-project-asset-gallery` no longer imports `lightning/uiGraphQLApi`. Its read moved to a child, `c-project-asset-gallery-data`, which renders nothing and hands the result to the gallery in a `galleryread` event. The gallery loads the child with a literal `import()` after the page has loaded and gone idle, renders it through `lwc:component`, and shows a skeleton that holds the gallery's space until the read settles. A failed load or read renders the same empty state as before.

The three components that read through the adapter are now `c-skill-network`, `c-project-asset-gallery-data` and `c-graphql-probe`. The query, the fields and the guest's permissions are the same, so the scope argument above is unchanged.

**Why.** The adapter stack was about 1,165 KB uncompressed in each of the `/skills`, `/business-architecture` and `/nonprofit-solutions` view bundles (performance audit, 2026-10-29). The static import pulled it into the two pillar views before first render. The footer's probe had already been moved out for the same reason (Technical Guide §2.11). `/skills` still imports it statically, because the matrix is that page's content. I did not measure a load time gain for the gallery change, since run to run noise was about 1.5 s. The reason is the bytes removed from the first load.

## Amendment (2026-11-02): the static site reads GraphQL at build time

On the static site ([ADR-041](041-headless-static-front-end-on-cloudflare-pages.md)) the skills page and the gallery do not call the GraphQL endpoint in the visitor's browser. Their queries run at build time, as the build user, and the static pages carry the rows. The test method `graphqlRowsMatchTheGuest` in `SiteExportTestimonialParityTest` proves the build user's rows equal the guest's for the same objects and fields, with sharing applied and unreadable fields stripped. A test cannot call the UI API GraphQL endpoint, so the check reads the same objects and fields through the equivalent queries. The Salesforce site keeps reading through the adapter until cutover, and the argument above about scope is unchanged.

# ADR-024: Twin API Pattern – Contract-First Parity

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/integration-api/specs/salesforce-sapi.yaml), also [portfolio-papi.yaml](../../packages/integration-api/specs/portfolio-papi.yaml)

Accepted, amended 2026-10-23 (see the amendment below): the MuleSoft parity rationale is gone. Contract first stays.

## Context

To prove enterprise maturity, the Salesforce implementation must match the MuleSoft design artifacts.

## Decision

Enforce the Twin API Pattern using OpenAPI 3.0 as the source of truth.

## Rationale

Ensures the Apex implementation (SAPI) and MuleSoft proxy remain interchangeable, demonstrating "API-Led Connectivity".

## Implications

Schema changes require a corresponding YAML update before implementation.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): the MuleSoft twin is gone

**The MuleSoft twin no longer exists.** The Anypoint trial ended, its live deployment expired, and the Anypoint Studio project was removed from the repository on 2026-10-20 (SAS Appendix C). Authentication moved on platform with [ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md). So the rationale above, keeping Apex and a MuleSoft proxy interchangeable, no longer applies: the Apex REST classes are the only runtime.

**What the decision still means.** The OpenAPI 3.0 files in `packages/integration-api/specs/` remain the contract for the Apex SAPI and PAPI. A change to a path, parameter or schema is made in the YAML first, then in Apex. The same files feed the rendered docs in `docs/api/oas/` (`npm run docs:api`, checked in CI by `npm run docs:verify`) and `scripts/api-smoke.sh`, which calls every GET path in both files. The site's API reference page reads identical copies in the `SAPI_Spec` and `PAPI_Spec` static resources. "Twin" now names the two API layers described by one pair of contracts, the System API and the Process API, not two runtimes.

# ADR-025: PAPI Fan-Out Throttling (Capacity Planning)

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/RateWindowLimiter.cls), also [RateWindowLimiterTest](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/RateWindowLimiterTest.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-01, 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-28 (see below). The 2026-10-28 amendment corrects the Context and Rationale: PAPI was never built to call SAPI over HTTP, so the "~8 upstream calls" below are eight data reads in one transaction, not eight requests.

## Context

The Process API (PAPI) `/profile/full` endpoint aggregates data from ~8 upstream System API (SAPI) calls. SAPI has a hard limit of 120 req/min.

## Decision

Enforce a strict rate limit of **15 requests/minute** on the PAPI layer.

## Rationale

Implementing "Backpressure" at the edge prevents the "Fan-Out Effect" (1 request becoming 8) from cascading and exhausting downstream SAPI quotas (15 \* 8 = 120).

## Implications

Clients requesting full profile hydration faster than every 4 seconds will receive HTTP 429; this is acceptable for a Portfolio use case.

## Amendment (2026-10-01)

The limits above stand. The **enforcement point** changes: the original text assumed MuleSoft API Manager would apply the policy. With MuleSoft removed ([ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md)), limits are enforced on-platform in a shared `ApiRequestContext`, keyed by the calling External Client App, emitting `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `Retry-After`.

Tiers: SAPI 120 req/min (burst 20); PAPI standard 15 req/min; PAPI `ai` tier 10 req/min; token vending per [ADR-028](028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md).

**Constraint:** the Developer Edition org has no Platform Cache allocation, so the counter cannot assume `Cache.Org`. Implementation must either (a) request the Platform Cache trial, (b) fall back to a lightweight custom-object counter purged by the existing cache-cleanup scheduler, or (c) ship the headers with enforcement documented as deferred. The choice is recorded in the implementation PR, not here.

## Amendment (2026-10-21)

The open constraint above is closed: option (b), a custom-object counter, was chosen (decision 2026-10-02), and the 2026-10-01 wording "keyed by the calling External Client App" is replaced by the keying below. Every vended token runs as the same integration user through the same External Client App, so keying by app or user would put every caller in one bucket.

Rate limits are enforced in Apex by `RateWindowLimiter`, a custom-object counter: one `API_Rate_Window__c` row per caller key per minute. `Key__c` is `{callerKey}|{yyyyMMddHHmm}` (UTC minute, unique external id, at most 255 characters; a caller key longer than 242 characters is replaced by `sha256:{hex}`). For SAPI and PAPI requests the caller key is `{tier}:{SHA-256 hex of the session id}`, or `{tier}:{user id}` when the session id is null. Each vended token is expected to be its own session (unverified until the live smoke). The token endpoint keys by `papi-token:{SHA-256 of lowercase email|source IP}`. Tiers: `sapi` 120, `papi` 15, `papi-ai` (`/papi/v1/ai/*`) 10 requests per minute. The window is a fixed calendar minute. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. Request limit + 1 within a minute gets `429` with `Retry-After` set to the seconds left in the minute, and the Error body `{httpStatus: 429, errorCode: "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", message: "Rate limit exceeded. Retry after N seconds.", correlationId, retryable: true}`. The rate check runs before any data query; a rejected request runs only the counter's own read and write. Rejected requests count. The check reads and locks the row and writes nothing. The incremented count is written when the response is written (`ok()`/`error()`), or by `ApiRequestContext.commitRateCounts()` for non-REST callers, so a resource may make callouts after `begin()`. If the row stays locked past the platform wait, the request gets 429 with `Retry-After: 1`. The daily `CacheCleanupScheduler` job deletes rows whose `Window_Start__c` is older than `Cache_Cleanup_Settings__mdt.Rate_Window_Retention_Days__c` (default 1 day). Platform Cache is not used. `HeadersOnlyRateLimiter` (never rejects) remains for tests.

Sources: `RateWindowLimiter.check`, `RateWindowLimiter.checkKey` and `RateWindowLimiter.commitPending`; `ApiRequestContext.applyRequestRules`, `ApiRequestContext.ok`, `ApiRequestContext.error` and `ApiRequestContext.commitRateCounts`; `TokenExchangeService.rateKey`; `CacheCleanupOrchestrator.runRateWindowCleanup` and `CacheCleanupRateWindowBatch.start`. The "burst 20" in the tier list above is not implemented: the window is a fixed calendar minute with no burst allowance.

## Note (2026-10-23)

The tier limits above (120, 15 and 10 a minute) and the API page sizes are now read from `Portfolio_Setting__mdt` records, with these numbers as the code defaults ([ADR-032](032-operational-settings-in-custom-metadata.md)). The decision is unchanged. A record outside its range is ignored, so a typo cannot set a tier to 0.

## Note (2026-10-24)

The SAPI list reads now come from `Query_Definition__mdt` records ([ADR-033](033-queries-in-custom-metadata.md)). The rate check is unchanged and still runs before any data query: the records load only when a read runs, so a rejected request loads none. The counter's own read stays in code, because a row read `FOR UPDATE` must not be editable as data. `/sapi/v1/projects` and `/sapi/v1/experience-highlights` spend one more SOQL query per request, to read their long filters in full.

## Amendment (2026-10-28): PAPI composes in process, and HTTP fan out was rejected

This corrects the Rationale above. The 15 a minute limit stands. The reason given for it does not, because PAPI never fans out to SAPI over HTTP.

**What is built.** PAPI and SAPI remain distinct logical API layers. PAPI composes the shared data access engine and request framework in process: it reads the same records through the query engine (`QueryDefinitions`, [ADR-033](033-queries-in-custom-metadata.md)) and the request framework (`ApiRequestContext`) SAPI also uses, with its own query definitions and its own transformer (`PAPITransformer`). One `/profile/full` request runs nine data reads in one Apex transaction. Those are data reads, not HTTP requests: nine SOQL queries cost the transaction nine of its query limit and nothing outside it.

**What was rejected, and why.** Turning those reads into HTTP requests from PAPI to SAPI through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential:

- **The same org callout constraint.** The site's API Lab reaches PAPI through `Portfolio_API`, which is a callout into this same org. A request that arrived as a same org callout may not call out again ([ADR-015](015-strategy-pattern-for-generative-ai.md)), so an HTTP fan out would fail on the site's own path, the one visitors use.
- **Latency.** Callouts in one synchronous Apex transaction run one after another, and together they must finish inside the 120 seconds of callout time a transaction allows. Eight loopback calls would add each call's round trip to every PAPI response. The "parallel groups" the specification once described could not have run in parallel.
- **Shared capacity.** Each loopback request would arrive as an inbound REST request and count against the org's daily API request allocation (15,000 on this Developer Edition, `DailyApiRequests`), where the in process reads count nothing. Each would also run as the integration user's one shared session, so one PAPI call would spend about eight of the SAPI tier's 120 requests a minute that every evaluator shares ([ADR-028](028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md)).

**Why 15 a minute still holds.** One PAPI request still does the data work of about eight SAPI reads in one transaction. The lower limit keeps one caller's PAPI load in step with what the same data costs through SAPI's 120 a minute. The arithmetic 15 \* 8 = 120 is a sizing ratio, not a count of HTTP calls.

**The deliberate exception.** `/papi/v1/health` calls SAPI's `/sapi/v1/health` through `Portfolio_API`, once, so the health check proves the credential works. It is the only PAPI callout.

**Not decided here.** An opt in HTTP fan out for outside callers, kept off the site's path, would be a separate experiment with its own decision record.

# ADR-026: Header-Based API Versioning Strategy

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/ApiVersionTest.cls), also [ApiRequestContext](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/ApiRequestContext.cls)

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-01; header rules corrected to the implementation 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

The API contract will evolve (v1.1, v1.2) and requires a strategy to manage breaking changes without disrupting existing consumers.

## Decision

Utilize the `X-API-Version` header (e.g., `X-API-Version: 1.2`) rather than URL path versioning (e.g., `/v1/profile`).

## Rationale

Decouples the **Resource Identity** (URL) from the **Representation Version** (Schema). Allows for cleaner URLs and easier routing logic in the future AWS Lambda layer (Door 2).

## Implications

Clients must be configured to send this header; default behavior (missing header) will resolve to the latest stable version.

## Amendment (2026-10-01)

As implemented in January 2026 the services only _emitted_ `X-API-Version`; they never read it from the request, so the strategy was described but not enforced. From the API foundation work onward ([ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md)) the shared `ApiRequestContext` reads `X-API-Version` and `X-Request-Id` on every request. On `/sapi/` paths a missing or non-UUID `X-Request-Id` returns `400 BAD_REQUEST`. On `/papi/` paths a missing `X-Request-Id` is replaced by a generated UUID and a present but non-UUID value returns `400`. A missing `X-API-Version` resolves to `v1`; any other value returns `400 BAD_REQUEST` with message `Unsupported X-API-Version` (the Error enum has no code for 406). Both headers are echoed on every response.

Source: `ApiRequestContext.applyRequestRules`, which every SAPI and PAPI REST class calls through `ApiRequestContext.begin()`.

## Amendment (2026-10-21)

The platform echoes a caller-supplied `X-Request-Id` on every response, including responses it generates before Apex runs, such as a 401. Apex therefore sets `X-Request-Id` only when it generated the value: on `/papi/` when the caller sent none, and on either API when the supplied value is not a UUID (the 400 response then carries a generated UUID in `correlationId`). A valid caller value is never set again by Apex, which would duplicate it (`id;id`). `correlationId` in error bodies always equals the id the caller sees.

Source: `ApiRequestContext.applyRequestRules`. The echo was observed on My Domain responses (a 401 from production and a 401 from a scratch org) and, once, on the site domain in an integration scratch org (guest requests, including an Apex 503). With no `X-Request-Id`, the platform returns its own 32-character hex id on responses it generates before Apex runs. Whether an authenticated PAPI response to a request without an id carries one id or two (the platform's and the UUID Apex generates) is unverified until the live smoke.

## Amendment (2026-10-31)

The URLs still carried a `/v1/` segment from before the header was read, so the decision above was only half carried out. [ADR-040](040-versionless-api-urls.md) removes the segment. The API is called at versionless URLs, the old `/v1/` URLs stay as aliases until a date I set, and the `X-API-Version` header is the only version switch.

# ADR-027: Platform-Native API Authentication (External Client App + Named Credential)

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/externalCredentials/Portfolio_API_Auth.externalCredential-meta.xml), also [Integration_Access](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/permissionsets/Integration_Access.permissionset-meta.xml)

Accepted (2026-10-01). Supersedes [ADR-017](017-system-api-security-and-dual-sided-auth-pattern.md). Amended 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

ADR-017 secured the System API (SAPI) by validating `client_id` / `client_secret` headers inside Apex against `Portfolio_Config__mdt`. That design existed to _simulate_ a MuleSoft API Manager policy enforcement point while the real gateway was expected to live in MuleSoft. The zero-cost operating model ([ADR-003](003-apex-rest-vs-external-service.md), [ADR-018](018-finops-constraint-aws-lambda-function-urls-vs-api-gateway.md)) removed MuleSoft from the architecture, so the simulation became the only gate.

A header check in Apex has three structural weaknesses:

1. The secret must be readable by the runtime, so it lives in metadata visible to every admin and in source control unless hashed.
2. The Experience Cloud guest user must hold execute access on every REST class for the check to run at all, which widens the guest attack surface that [ADR-012](012-guest-user-security-restriction-rules.md) deliberately narrows.
3. Rejection happens inside the transaction, after the platform has already spent governor budget on the request.

Salesforce provides a first-class answer to machine-to-machine authentication, and the portfolio should demonstrate it rather than re-implement it.

## Decision

Authenticate the SAPI and Process API (PAPI) with platform-native OAuth 2.0 on both sides of the boundary:

- **Inbound (provider side):** an **External Client App** enabled for the **Client Credentials flow**, configured to _run as_ a dedicated integration user. Callers present `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. The guest user holds no execute access on any SAPI or PAPI class except the token-vending endpoint defined in [ADR-028](028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md).
- **Outbound (consumer side):** an **External Credential** using the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials protocol against this org's own token endpoint, holding the External Client App consumer key and secret as its principal, wrapped by a `Portfolio_API` **Named Credential**. Any on-platform consumer (the site's API Lab proxy, the PAPI health check) calls the APIs through that Named Credential.
- **Authorisation:** the integration user holds a single permission set (`Integration_Access`) granting read-only access to the portfolio objects, execute access on the SAPI and PAPI classes, and nothing else.
- **Contract:** both OpenAPI specifications replace the two `apiKey` header schemes with one `oauth2` `clientCredentials` security scheme.

## Alternatives Considered

| Option                                               | Rejected because                                                                                                                                  |
| :--------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Keep the custom-metadata header check (ADR-017)      | Simulates a gateway that no longer exists; secret in metadata; guest user needs REST class access; rejection costs governor budget.               |
| Publish a shared demo secret in the documentation    | A published secret is not a secret. Reviewers would read it as a security defect, not a convenience.                                              |
| Legacy Connected App instead of External Client App  | Functionally equivalent for client credentials, but External Client Apps are the current packaging-friendly model and deploy cleanly from source. |
| Named / External Credentials alone                   | These are outbound-only constructs. They hold credentials Salesforce presents to others and cannot authenticate an inbound caller.                |
| Experience Cloud guest access with no authentication | Portfolio data is public, but an unauthenticated REST surface demonstrates nothing and exposes the org's API request quota to anyone.             |

## Rationale

- **Real controls instead of simulated ones.** The platform rejects an invalid or missing token before Apex executes. "No SOQL before authentication" is guaranteed by the runtime, not by code review.
- **Least privilege is explicit.** Everything a token can do is bounded by one permission set on one user, which is auditable in Setup and in source.
- **Secrets stay in the vault.** The consumer secret exists only in the External Credential principal. Rotation is a Setup action (regenerate in the External Client App, update the principal) with no code change and no deploy.
- **The dual-sided pattern survives.** ADR-017's separation between consumer and provider is preserved: the Named Credential is the consumer, the External Client App is the provider. The portfolio now demonstrates both constructs in a working loop rather than describing them.

## Implications

- **Guest user:** loses execute access on all SAPI and PAPI classes. Site components reach data through `@AuraEnabled` controllers or the API Lab proxy, never the REST surface directly.
- **API Lab (`c-api-tester`):** cannot hold a secret in the browser, so it calls an Apex proxy (`ApiLabController`) that invokes the API through `Portfolio_API`. Each call therefore traverses browser → Apex → Named Credential → External Client App → Apex REST. The added latency is shown on screen as part of the demonstration.
- **PAPI → SAPI:** remains in-process SOQL. A self-callout per sub-resource would cost eight API requests per `/profile/full` call for no security gain ([ADR-025](025-papi-fan-out-throttling-capacity-planning.md)). One PAPI health check does traverse the Named Credential so the credential is exercised continuously.
- **Rate limiting:** moves from "enforced by MuleSoft API Manager" to on-platform enforcement in Apex by `RateWindowLimiter`, a custom-object counter keyed by a hash of the caller's session id, not by the calling application. See the [ADR-025 amendment (2026-10-21)](025-papi-fan-out-throttling-capacity-planning.md#amendment-2026-10-21).
- **Licensing:** the integration user consumes one Salesforce user licence in the Developer Edition org.
- **Documentation:** the SAS (§5.3, Appendix C) and Technical Guide (§1) sections describing `client_id` / `client_secret` validation against `Portfolio_Config__mdt` must be rewritten to match this decision.
- **Constraints carried forward from ADR-017:** the APIs remain read-only; non-GET methods on data resources return `405 Method Not Allowed`. The only POST endpoints are `/papi/v1/ai/generate` and the token-vending endpoint in ADR-028.

## Amendment (2026-10-20)

**`Integration_Access` is read-only.** The permission set grants read, and only read, on 14 objects: `Account`, `Certification__c`, `Contact`, `Education__c`, `Experience_Highlight__c`, `Experience_Skill__c`, `Experience__c`, `Github_Cache__c`, `Jira_Cache__c`, `Project_Asset__c`, `Project_Skill__c`, `Project__c`, `Skill__c` and `Testimonial__c`. None of its 57 field permissions is editable, and it grants no create, edit, delete, View All or Modify All. Contact field access is limited to the nine fields the API returns: `Career_Objective__c`, `Email`, `GitHub_URL__c`, `Is_Portfolio_Owner__c`, `LinkedIn_URL__c`, `Phone`, `Portfolio_URL__c`, `Title` and `Trailhead_URL__c`. Source: `packages/portfolio-site/main/default/permissionsets/Integration_Access.permissionset-meta.xml`.

Because a vended token works on every REST API as the integration user, this permission set is the security control. It never gains create, edit or delete.

**Run-as profile.** The integration user runs under the `Portfolio API Integration` profile (Salesforce Platform licence). The profile grants API access only and revokes the object permissions the licence adds by default; all data access comes from `Integration_Access`. Its session timeout is 30 minutes (`Portfolio_API_Integration.profileSessionSetting-meta.xml`), which is what makes vended tokens expire ([ADR-028](028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md)).

**Where each construct lives.** The `Portfolio_API_Auth` External Credential (OAuth 2.0, client credentials with client secret, named principal `Portfolio_API_Principal`) and the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential (URL: the My Domain root) are in source under `packages/portfolio-site/main/default/`. The **Portfolio API** External Client App and the integration user were created in Setup and are not in source. The consumer key and secret exist only in the External Client App and the External Credential principal.

## Amendment (2026-10-21)

**Read-only object grants, now 15.** `Integration_Access` also grants read on `Certification_Skill__c` (its only custom fields are master-detail and take no field permission), and no longer grants class access to `SAPIResume`, which was removed. It still grants no create, edit or delete. Source: `Integration_Access.permissionset-meta.xml`.

**A second credential for token vending.** Apex cannot read the client secret of an OAuth External Credential, so evaluator token vending ([ADR-028](028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md)) uses a second pair: the `Portfolio_API_Token_Auth` External Credential (Custom protocol, named principal `Portfolio_API_Token_Principal`, authentication parameters `Client_Id` and `Client_Secret` entered in Setup) and the `Portfolio_API_Token` Named Credential (My Domain root, merge fields allowed in the body, no generated Authorization header). `TokenExchangeService.exchangeToken` posts `grant_type=client_credentials` with `{!$Credential.Portfolio_API_Token_Auth.Client_Id}` and `{!$Credential.Portfolio_API_Token_Auth.Client_Secret}` to `/services/oauth2/token`. The consumer secret therefore lives in two principals, and rotation updates both.

**Access grants as first built** (decision 2026-10-20). Built: `Integration_Access.permissionset-meta.xml` and `Portfolio_Guest.permissionset-meta.xml` under `packages/portfolio-site/main/default/permissionsets/`:

- `Integration_Access` gains class access to the ten new SAPI classes (`SAPIContact`, `SAPIAccount`, `SAPIExperienceHighlight`, `SAPIProjectAsset`, `SAPICertification`, `SAPIEducation`, `SAPIProjectSkill`, `SAPIExperienceSkill`, `SAPICertificationSkill`, `SAPIPortfolioConfig`), `SAPIHealth`, `PAPITestimonialFeed` and `PAPIAiGenerate`, (21 class grants in all), and External Credential principal access to `Portfolio_API_Auth-Portfolio_API_Principal`, so `PAPIHealth` can exercise the credential as the integration user. Object and field grants stay read-only: no create, edit or delete.
- A new `Portfolio_Guest` permission set for the site guest user: class access to `PAPIAuthToken` and `ApiLabController` only, principal access to `Portfolio_API_Auth-Portfolio_API_Principal` and `Portfolio_API_Token_Auth-Portfolio_API_Token_Principal`, read on `UserExternalCredential`, and no portfolio object or field grants at first, because guest reads were added once the components' field needs were known. It has no licence, and it was assigned to the site guest user in an integration scratch org without error. There, before assignment, the guest got 403 on `POST /papi/v1/auth/token`; after it, the token endpoint ran (503, credential not configured in scratch) while `GET /sapi/v1/skills` and `GET /papi/v1/health` stayed 403.
- `Portfolio_Admin` grants read and View All on `API_Access_Request__c` and `API_Rate_Window__c`, with read-only field access on their fields, so an administrator can report on the token audit trail and the rate windows. It grants no create, edit or delete on either object.

# ADR-028: Evaluator Access via Token Vending

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/TokenExchangeService.cls), also [TokenExchangeServiceTest](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/TokenExchangeServiceTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-01). Depends on [ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md). Amended twice on 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

The portfolio's Evidence Matrix invites reviewers to call the APIs and compare live responses against the OpenAPI contracts. Under [ADR-027](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md) every endpoint requires an OAuth 2.0 Bearer token obtained with the External Client App's consumer secret. A single External Client App cannot mint per-person credentials, so an external evaluator with `curl` has no way in unless one of the following is true:

- the secret is published (rejected in ADR-027),
- the evaluator asks me for credentials by email (manual, slow, and invisible to the portfolio),
- or the platform issues them a token on request.

The data behind the APIs is public portfolio content. The assets worth protecting are the consumer secret, the integration user's session, and the Developer Edition org's daily API request quota.

## Decision

Expose one unauthenticated endpoint, `POST /papi/v1/auth/token`, that performs the client-credentials exchange **server-side** and returns a **short-lived access token** to the caller. The consumer secret never leaves the org.

Request: `{ "email": string, "purpose": string }`.
Response: `{ "access_token", "token_type": "Bearer", "instance_url", "docs" }`. (The original response also carried `expires_in`. I dropped it on 2026-10-21, see the second amendment below.)

Behaviour:

1. Validate the email format and reject malformed addresses with `400`. (The original text also rejected disposable addresses. I dropped that on 2026-10-21, see the second amendment below.)
2. Apply the shared rate limiter keyed by email and source IP; reject with `429` and `Retry-After`.
3. Enforce a daily issuance cap (default 50 tokens/day) with `503` once exhausted.
4. Write an `API_Access_Request__c` audit record (email, purpose, timestamp, source IP, correlation ID).
5. Call the org's token endpoint through the `Portfolio_API` Named Credential and return the resulting token.

`PAPIAuthToken` is the **only** REST class the Experience Cloud guest user may execute. It shares a `TokenExchangeService` with the site's API Lab proxy so there is exactly one code path that touches the credential.

## Alternatives Considered

| Option                                        | Rejected because                                                                                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No external access; API Lab on the site only  | Loses the "verify it yourself with curl" evidence hook. The README already promises it.                                            |
| Publish a shared demo secret                  | A published secret is a defect, not a demo (see ADR-027).                                                                          |
| Manual credential requests by email           | Unobservable, unscalable, and demonstrates nothing about the platform.                                                             |
| One External Client App per evaluator         | Manual Setup work per reviewer; cannot be automated from Apex.                                                                     |
| Self-registration as an Experience Cloud user | Heavier than the problem warrants, requires login UX, and still does not give a `curl` user a Bearer token without a browser flow. |

## Rationale

- **The secret is never exposed.** The exchange happens inside the org through the Named Credential. The evaluator only ever sees a token that expires.
- **Least privilege is the real control.** A client-credentials token is valid for any REST API as the integration user, not only the Apex REST endpoints. The binding constraint is therefore the integration user's permission set: read-only on portfolio objects, nothing else. This is deliberately documented as the control so it is never relaxed casually.
- **Exposure is time-bounded.** The integration user runs under a dedicated profile with a 30-minute idle session timeout, so an issued token ends once the shared session goes unused for 30 minutes.
- **There is a kill switch.** Deactivating the External Client App invalidates every outstanding token immediately.
- **The quota is protected.** Each issued token can generate API requests against the Developer Edition limit of 15,000 per day. The issuance cap and rate limiter bound the worst case.
- **It is observable.** Every request leaves an audit row, which doubles as a lightweight signal of who evaluated the portfolio.

## Implications

- **New metadata:** `API_Access_Request__c` custom object (audit only, no guest read access), the `PAPIAuthToken` REST class, and guest execute access on that one class.
- **Spec change:** `/auth/token` is added to `portfolio-papi.yaml` with `security: []`; the generated Markdown is regenerated via `npm run docs:verify`.
- **Site:** the API Lab gains a "Get an API token" action that calls the same endpoint and prints a ready-to-paste `curl` command.
- **README / Evidence Matrix:** the verification method for API design changes from "call the endpoints" to "request a token, then call the endpoints", with the flow documented inline.
- **Operations (Maintenance Guide):** rotation runbook for the consumer secret, the daily cap setting, and the procedure for revoking access (deactivate the app, re-enable after rotation).
- **Risk accepted:** an email address is low friction. For read-only public data this is proportionate; if abuse appears, the cap and the kill switch are the response, not a redesign.

## Amendment (2026-10-21)

Behaviour as built in `PAPIAuthToken.requestToken` and `TokenExchangeService.requestToken`:

1. **Validation (400).** The body must be a JSON object of strings. `email` must be a valid address of at most 254 characters, and `purpose` is required, at most 280 characters. Disposable addresses are not rejected, and the decision no longer asks for it (second amendment below).
2. **Rate limit (429).** 15 requests per minute per email and source IP (`TokenExchangeService.TOKEN_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`, decision 2026-10-20), keyed `papi-token:{SHA-256 hex of lowercase(email)|sourceIp}` through `ApiRateLimiter.checkKey`, on top of the PAPI tier limit applied by `ApiRequestContext.begin`. See the [ADR-025 amendment (2026-10-21)](025-papi-fan-out-throttling-capacity-planning.md#amendment-2026-10-21).
3. **Daily cap (503).** `TokenExchangeService.dailyCap` reads `Portfolio_Config__mdt.Token_Daily_Cap__c` on the `Ryan_Bumstead` record, default 50. The cap counts audit rows with outcome `Issued` created today; once reached, the response is 503 with `Retry-After` set to the seconds until the next midnight in the running user's time zone. A cap of 0 refuses every request.
4. **Audit.** Every attempt, including those `ApiRequestContext` rejects before the service runs (`TokenExchangeService.recordRejected`), writes one `API_Access_Request__c` row with `Email__c`, `Purpose__c`, `Source_IP__c`, `Correlation_Id__c`, `Channel__c` (`REST` or `Aura`) and `Outcome__c` (`Issued`, `Invalid_Request`, `Rate_Limited`, `Cap_Reached`, `Credential_Missing`, `Failed`). When the token callout runs, the row is written after it (contract C2).
5. **Exchange.** Through the `Portfolio_API_Token` Named Credential, not `Portfolio_API` (Apex cannot read the secret of the OAuth credential; see the [ADR-027 amendment (2026-10-21)](027-platform-native-api-authentication.md#amendment-2026-10-21)). A missing or ungranted credential, or `invalid_client_id`, answers 503 "Token issuance is not configured."; any other failure answers 503 "Token issuance is temporarily unavailable."
6. **Response.** `expires_in` was always 1800, the integration profile's session timeout, because the token endpoint returns no expiry. The second amendment below drops it. `instance_url` is the My Domain root returned by the token endpoint, and evaluators call `{instance_url}/services/apexrest/...`. The token request itself goes to the site domain under `/portfoliovforcesite/services/apexrest/`.

The API Lab's `ApiLabController.requestEvaluatorToken` runs the same service, then calls `ApiRequestContext.commitRateCounts()` to write its rate count. An Aura call has no REST request, so the source IP comes from the current session when one exists and is otherwise the literal `unavailable`, which makes that key effectively per email. Each vended token is not its own session, so the session based rate key does not separate evaluators. The second amendment below records what that means.

## Amendment (2026-10-21): a shared token pool, no expiry, no disposable list

**Every evaluator shares one token pool and one rate limit** (my decision, 2026-10-21).

- Two token exchanges in a row return the same access token. The platform hands back the integration user's current session for the same client while that session is valid, instead of opening a new one. So every evaluator who asks for a token in that window gets the same token. This was proven twice in production on 2026-10-21: two exchanges compared equal by hash, and two separately vended tokens landed on the same `RateWindowLimiter` key.
- `RateWindowLimiter` keys SAPI and PAPI requests by a hash of the session id, so all evaluators count against one bucket per tier: SAPI 120, PAPI 15 and `/papi/v1/ai/` 10 requests per minute, shared. One busy evaluator can use up the minute for everyone, and a 429 with `Retry-After` is the answer until the minute ends.
- I accepted this for launch. The data is public, the tiers are small, and the daily cap and the kill switch still bound the worst case. Nothing in the docs or the specs describes a per-evaluator limit.
- The token request itself is still limited per email and source IP (`papi-token` key, item 2 of the 2026-10-21 amendment), because that key does not depend on the session.

**No `expires_in`** (my decision, 2026-10-21). The token endpoint reports no expiry for a client credentials grant, and the token is the integration user's shared session, which ends after 30 minutes without use (the integration profile's idle timeout). A fixed number would describe neither, so the response leaves the field out and the specs and docs say how the session ends instead.

**Disposable addresses.** I dropped "reject disposable addresses" from item 1 of the decision on 2026-10-21. No list of disposable domains is kept, and the audit row plus the daily cap are the controls.

## Note (2026-10-23)

The token request rate (15 a minute per email and source IP) and the default daily cap (50) are now read from the `Token_Requests_Per_Minute` and `Token_Daily_Cap_Default` records of `Portfolio_Setting__mdt`, with those numbers as the code defaults ([ADR-032](032-operational-settings-in-custom-metadata.md)). `Portfolio_Config__mdt.Token_Daily_Cap__c` still wins when set, so a cap of 0 still pauses vending.
