# ADR-029: Schema Visualizer Scope, Discovery and Caching Without Platform Cache

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/SchemaService.cls), also [SchemaServiceTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/SchemaServiceTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-22).

## Context

The SAS promises a data model diagram that never drifts from the deployed org (section 5.1). The Business Architecture page (Pillar A) draws it live. The earlier design in the Technical Guide had two problems:

- It cached the describe result in Platform Cache. The org has no Platform Cache partition, and the project decided against it.
- It drew edges from child relationships. `Account` alone carries hundreds of standard child relationships, so walking them costs CPU and fills the diagram with noise.

The page also needs two schemas: the inert Employer Hub model of the demo (shown by default) and the portfolio's own model. The site guest, who has no read access on the Employer Hub objects, must see the same diagram as an administrator.

## Decision

`SchemaService.getSchemaGraph(scope)` (`public with sharing`, `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`, API 64.0) builds the diagram for one scope, `portfolio` or `employerHub`. Any other scope throws an `AuraHandledException`.

1. **Discovery from the global describe keys only.** One `Schema.getGlobalDescribe()` per call, keys only. An object is a custom object of this org when its name ends in `__c` and has no namespace prefix (exactly one `__`). Names ending in `__mdt`, `__e`, `__b`, `__x`, `__Share`, `__History`, `__Feed` or `__ChangeEvent` are dropped, and so are custom settings (`DescribeSObjectResult.isCustomSetting()`).
2. **Scopes.** An object whose name starts with `EH_` belongs to `employerHub`. Every other custom object belongs to `portfolio`. Each scope adds a standard allowlist: `Account` and `Contact` for the portfolio, and `Account`, `Contact`, `Case`, `Opportunity` and `Contract` for the Employer Hub.
3. **Overrides in Custom Metadata.** `Schema_Visualizer_Object__mdt` rows (`Object_API_Name__c`, `Scope__c`, `Hidden__c`) move an object to a scope or hide it. Four shipped rows hide the internal objects `API_Rate_Window__c`, `API_Access_Request__c`, `Github_Cache__c` and `Jira_Cache__c` (my decision, 2026-10-22).
4. **Describe the filtered list only.** `Schema.describeSObjects(names, SObjectDescribeOptions.DEFERRED)` runs on the objects in scope, never on the whole org.
5. **Edges from reference fields.** An edge is a reference field whose target is in the same scope. It points from the object holding the field to its target. A field with a relationship order (`getRelationshipOrder() != null`) is master-detail, and every other reference is a lookup. Child relationships are not read.
6. **The only cache is the browser's.** `cacheable=true` lets Lightning Data Service cache the answer on the client. There is no Platform Cache and no server cache.
7. **The cost is shown.** The response carries the server CPU time of the call (`cpuMs`), and the page's caption shows it with the object count, for example "9 objects, described in 96 ms of server CPU".

## Rationale

- **It cannot drift.** A new custom object appears on its own in the portfolio scope, and hiding or moving one is a metadata deploy, not a code change.
- **The guest sees the same schema.** Run as the real site guest (`SchemaServiceTest.guestDescribeMatchesAdmin`), the global describe and `describeSObjects` return the same objects as for an administrator, the four `EH_` objects included, though the guest cannot read them. Describe does not filter by object permission, so the guest needs no object grant and no deploy-time snapshot (established 2026-10-22). Exposing names is acceptable because the repository is public.
- **It is cheap.** Uncached in a scratch org, the portfolio scope (14 objects, 21 edges, 10 master-detail) took 141 ms of CPU and the Employer Hub scope (9 objects, 23 edges, 1 master-detail) took 96 ms, against a budget of 1,000 ms per call and the SAS limit of 5,000 ms per request. `SchemaServiceTest.eachScopeStaysUnderTheCpuBudget` asserts the budget.

## Alternatives considered

| Option                                 | Rejected because                                                                                     |
| :------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Platform Cache for the describe result | The org has no partition, and the project decided against Platform Cache.                            |
| Edges from `getChildRelationships()`   | Hundreds of standard child relationships on `Account` cost CPU and draw noise.                       |
| A schema snapshot taken at deploy time | It goes stale, which is what the diagram must not do. The guest describe result made it unnecessary. |
| A hard-coded list of objects           | It drifts the first time an object is added.                                                         |

## Implications

- `SchemaService` reads no records and exposes metadata only. The site guest holds class access to it through `Portfolio_Guest` and nothing else for the diagram.
- The `EH_Demo_Read` permission set (read on the four `EH_` objects) is optional for administrators and is not assigned to the guest.
- `c/schemaVisualizer` draws the result with the shared d3-force engine on desktop and tablet, and shows the object list on phones ([ADR-020 amendment](020-mobile-performance-static-svg-fallback-strategy.md#amendment-2026-10-22-matrix-first-the-graph-on-open-d3-force-as-the-engine)). Technical Guide section 2.4 describes it.
- The class stays on API 64.0. From 67.0 Apex runs in user context by default, which would change the describe.

# ADR-031: Native Contact Form

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/ContactFormController.cls), also [ContactFormControllerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/ContactFormControllerTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-23). I chose a native form on 2026-10-22, and the platform event step was added on 2026-10-23 after a scratch org proof.

## Context

The site had no way to reach me. Email and phone were removed from the site and the API on purpose, and `Portfolio_Config__mdt.Calendly_URL__c` reaches only the API. I asked for a short contact form on the home page that lands in Salesforce as a Lead, so the org's own Lead rules handle it: the assignment rule picks the owner, the auto-response rule thanks the visitor, and a reminder follows if I forget to reply.

The form is public. An auto-response on a public form can be used to send mail to any address someone types in, which spends the org's email allowance and the domain's sending reputation. A single shared rate limit, like the testimonial form's `testimonial-submit` key, would also let a bot lock real visitors out.

## Decision

1. **An LWC and Apex, not Web-to-Lead.** `c-contact-form` sits on the `/contact` page. It asks for first name, last name, email, an optional company and a message, shows a one line privacy note, and thanks the visitor inline ("Thanks, check your inbox") with no redirect. When the address ends in `#contact` the form scrolls into view and focuses its heading, so a footer link needs to know nothing about the page.
2. **The guest checks, a platform event saves.** `ContactFormController` runs as the site guest. It validates the input, then runs `SubmissionGuard`, then publishes one `Contact_Form_Submission__e`. `ContactFormSubmissionTrigger` runs as the Automated Process user and `ContactFormLeadWriter` inserts the Lead in system mode with `Database.DMLOptions`: the default assignment rule, the auto-response only when the event asks for it, the assignment notification email, and duplicates allowed so a returning visitor is never refused. `LeadSource` is "Portfolio Website". The site guest has no Lead permission at all.
3. **Abuse protection before anything is published.** `SubmissionGuard`, shared with the testimonial form, drops a filled honeypot, a submit faster than a person can type and any sender on the `Submission_Block__c` blocklist (an email, a domain or a keyword in the text) silently: the visitor sees the normal thanks, and nothing is stored or sent. Over 20 contact form Leads in 24 hours the visitor is told to try tomorrow or use LinkedIn. The auto-response is asked for only on the first message from an address in 24 hours. The "Block sender" quick action on Lead adds a sender to the blocklist from the desktop or the mobile app and marks the Lead as spam.
4. **The reminder fallback.** `LeadReminderService` stamps two reply reminder times on the Lead, one and two business days after it arrives, counted on the org's default Business Hours. The `Lead_Contact_Form_Reminders` flow sends a custom notification to the owner's desktop and the Salesforce mobile app on arrival, then at each reminder time while the Lead is still "Open - Not Contacted", not spam and not converted.
5. **Nothing is lost.** A Lead insert that fails is retried by the event bus three times. After that the message is kept as a `Contact_Form_Failure__c` row with the reason, and the `Portfolio_Admin` users get a custom notification.
6. **What stays out of source.** The Lead assignment rule and the Lead auto-response rule hold my user and sending address, so they are set up in each org with me signed in, by a browser script kept out of the repository. Both email templates are in source with no address in them.

## Rationale

- **On platform.** The Lead, the standard assignment and auto-response rules, the custom notification and the flow are all ordinary Salesforce features an admin can read and change.
- **The same pattern as the testimonial form.** Server validation, a honeypot, a time check and the blocklist now guard both public forms through one class.
- **No cross domain post and no third party script.** The form posts to the site's own Apex, so the site's content security policy and the "no third party script" rule stay as they are.
- **The same Lead rules as Web-to-Lead.** `DMLOptions` asks for exactly the rules Web-to-Lead would run.
- **Why the platform event.** Proved in a scratch org on 2026-10-23: a Lead inserted in the guest's own context with the auto-response rule active fails with `INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS_ON_CROSS_REFERENCE_ENTITY` on the rule's sending user. With only the assignment rule active the same insert works. The trigger's Automated Process user can send it, and the auto-response reached a test inbox from that context.
- **Why no automatic IP blocking.** The review asked for an automatic block on one source sending from three or more addresses in a day, using a salted hash of the visitor's IP. In a guest request `Auth.SessionManagement.getCurrentSession()` ends the request with "Guest users must never have a session ID created", and an IP the browser sends could be faked. So no server side IP is used. `IP Hash` stays on the blocklist as a type I can add by hand.

## Alternatives considered

| Option                                                                  | Rejected because                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Web-to-Lead                                                             | It posts from the site to a separate Salesforce endpoint, carries the org Id in the page, has no way to run the shared blocklist or the per address auto-response limit before the Lead exists, and redirects the visitor away from the page. It is also an odd fit on an Experience Cloud site that can call its own Apex. |
| A guest Screen Flow                                                     | A flow's Create Records element has no way to set `DMLOptions`, so the assignment and auto-response rules would not run. The blocklist and rate checks would also be flow logic duplicated from the testimonial form's Apex.                                                                                                |
| LWC and Apex inserting the Lead in the guest's own context              | The first version. The auto-response rule fails in that context, as above.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Sending the auto-response from Apex with `Messaging.SingleEmailMessage` | It would bypass the auto-response rule I wanted, and every send would count against the single email allowance. Not tried.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Implications

- The form shows the same thanks whether a message was saved or dropped, so a bot learns nothing. A real visitor whose address is blocked by mistake is not told. I lift a block by clearing its Active box.
- The Lead is saved a moment after the visitor sees the thanks, not in the same request. A visitor never sees a save error from the trigger.
- The reminders count weekends until the org's default Business Hours are set to my working days, because a new org's default hours are 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
- The auto-response did not change the `SingleEmail`, `MassEmail` or `DailyWorkflowEmails` figures that `sf org list limits` reports in the scratch org. Which daily allowance it does count against is not established here.
- The auto-response rule entry has no Reply-To field in Setup, so replies go to the sending address. In production that is the verified organization wide address.
- Cloudflare Turnstile stays the next step if abuse appears. It is out of scope because it brings back a third party script.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): the form has its own page

The form moved from the home page to its own route, `/contact` (page title "Contact | Ryan Bumstead"), with the heading "Get in touch" and a short intro. The home page keeps a one line "Get in touch" prompt, `c-contact-call`, with a link styled as a button to `/contact`. The header gains a Contact item, and the footer's Contact link points at `/contact`. An old `/#contact` address sends the visitor on to `/contact`, replacing the history entry. The form's own behaviour, its guard, the platform event and the Lead rules are unchanged. Each answered submit sends `contact_form_submitted` with only its outcome (Technical Guide §2.16).

## Amendment (2026-10-24): one email to the owner per new Lead

Each new Lead's owner gets one email from `ContactFormLeadWriter` after the insert, rendered from the `Portfolio_Contact_New_Lead` template: the visitor's name, company, email and full message, and a link to the Lead. It goes to the Lead owner's user Id when the owner is an active internal user, or to the `Portfolio_Admin` users while the Lead has no such owner, for example while it stays with the Automated Process user. No address is written in source. The assignment rule's own notification is not sent from the Automated Process context, so the rule entry needs no template and the owner never gets two emails for one message.

- The email is sent to a user Id with `setTargetObjectId`, which the Apex governor limits documentation says does not count toward the daily single email limit.
- A failed send is ignored. The Lead is saved and the in app arrival notice still goes, so there is nothing to undo or retry.
- A Lead rule entry for "Portfolio Website" leads, assigned to me with no template, is optional. With it I own the Lead, so the in app reminders reach me as well.

## Amendment (2026-11-02): Turnstile on the static site

On the static site ([ADR-041](041-headless-static-front-end-on-cloudflare-pages.md)) the contact form and the testimonial form are guarded by Cloudflare Turnstile, checked on the server by the Pages Function before it forwards the submission. The trade this ADR weighed for a third party script changes, because Turnstile comes from the same vendor that hosts the static site, so the host sees no new party. It is still one more script on the page, and it loads only with the form. The honeypot and the elapsed time check stay in `SubmissionGuard`, and the hashed visitor address, made at the edge with a secret salt, now feeds a block rule and a rate limit per address hash. The rule is `SubmissionGuard`'s IP hash block and a per hash limit set by `Form_Rate_Per_Hash_Per_Minute`, three a minute by default. A request that arrives with no trusted hash behaves as it does today.

# ADR-030: Decision Matrix as Custom Metadata

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/DecisionMatrixController.cls), also [DecisionMatrixControllerTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/DecisionMatrixControllerTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-22). Note added 2026-10-22 on whose weights these are.

## Context

The Nonprofit Solutions page (Pillar B) tells the story of an adult literacy nonprofit choosing a platform, in two parts: an unpaid pre-sales cycle of discovery, a demo and this comparison, then a paid build that I led. Its centre is a decision matrix the visitor can reweight. I chose a three-way matrix (my decision, 2026-10-22): NPSP with the Program Management Module, Education Cloud, and Nonprofit Cloud. The client's own decision was two-way, NPSP and PMM against Education Cloud, and it chose NPSP and PMM. That decision is the dated baseline, and Nonprofit Cloud is the option a reviewer would ask about today. The scores and weights are mine to set. I reviewed every score and weight on 2026-10-22, and every placeholder flag is cleared.

> **Note, 2026-10-22.** This record first called the starting weights the client's. No client weighting exists in any source. The starting weights are mine, set from what the client said mattered most, and the reset button now reads "Reset to the starting weights".

The matrix must be source controlled, deploy to production and to CI's scratch orgs with no managed package, use no data storage, and never ship with an empty cell.

## Decision

1. **Three Custom Metadata Types** in the `nonprofit-literacy` package:
   - `Decision_Option__mdt`: `Summary__c`, `Sort_Order__c`. Three records.
   - `Decision_Criterion__mdt`: `Description__c`, `Default_Weight__c` (my starting weight, 0 to 10), `Sort_Order__c`. Ten records.
   - `Decision_Score__mdt`: `Option__c` and `Criterion__c` as metadata relationships, `Score__c` (1 to 5), `Rationale__c`, `Evidence__c`, `Is_Placeholder__c`. Thirty records, one per option and criterion pair.
2. **A placeholder flag.** Every score carries `Is_Placeholder__c` until I review it, and its rationale starts `PLACEHOLDER:`. While any score is flagged the page shows the banner "Scores and weights are provisional placeholders pending the owner's review."
3. **One cacheable read.** `DecisionMatrixController.getMatrix()` (`with sharing`, `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`) returns the options, the criteria, every score and `hasPlaceholders` in one payload. It reads the types with SOQL, because `getAll()` returns only the first 255 characters of a long text field, and maps each score to its option and criterion through the related record Ids it has already read.
4. **Totals in the browser.** `c/decisionMatrix` computes every weighted total, the ranking and the sensitivity line (the single weight change that would first put the runner-up ahead), so moving a weight makes no server call. "Reset to the starting weights" restores each criterion's `Default_Weight__c`.
5. **No holes.** `DecisionMatrixControllerTest.shouldScoreEveryOptionAndCriterionPairExactlyOnce` fails when any option and criterion pair lacks a score or has two.

## Rationale

- Custom Metadata deploys with the code through CI, needs no data load and uses no data storage.
- Metadata relationships make each score name a real option and criterion, so a renamed row cannot leave an orphan.
- The site guest reads the three types through the controller with no custom metadata grant. Run as the real site guest (`DecisionMatrixControllerTest.shouldServeTheSameMatrixToTheSiteGuest`), it gets the same 3 options, 10 criteria and 30 scores as an administrator, cell for cell (established 2026-10-22).
- The placeholder flag keeps my judgement visible. The banner disappears on its own once the last flag is cleared.

## Alternatives considered

| Option                                 | Rejected because                                                                                  |
| :------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A static JSON resource read by the LWC | Simpler and needs no class access, but it hides the metadata pattern the pillar is meant to show. |
| Custom objects with records            | They use data storage and need a data load in every org, including CI's scratch orgs.             |
| A server call for each reweighting     | It costs a call per slider move for arithmetic the browser can do.                                |

## Implications

- The Apex class and both components (`c/decisionMatrix`, `c/pillarBStory`) live in `portfolio-site`, because Jest only runs there. The package holds the types, their 43 records and the `NL_Assets` static resource.
- Changing a score or weight is a metadata deploy. I review the scores and weights, clears each `Is_Placeholder__c` and commits the records. Done 2026-10-22: every score reviewed, every flag cleared, starting weights 2 to 10.
- The cost and effort table on the page is built from public licence facts only, with a source per row (my decision). No client rates or totals appear anywhere.

# ADR-032: Operational Settings in Custom Metadata

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/PortfolioSettings.cls), also [PortfolioSettingsTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/PortfolioSettingsTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-23).

## Context

Operational values sat as constants in Apex and in two components: API page sizes, the three rate tiers, the token rate and the default daily cap, the circuit breaker threshold and open time, the contact and testimonial form limits, the source cache refresh limits, the governance freshness windows, the AI length bounds, the health check timeout and two display counts. Changing any of them meant a code change, a test run and a deploy, even when the change was only a number.

Some values already lived in custom metadata, each in a type of its own (`Cache_Cleanup_Settings__mdt`, `AI_Provider_Config__mdt`, and the token cap on `Portfolio_Config__mdt`). Adding one field per value to those types would spread settings across types that each mean something else, and a new field is a metadata change of its own.

A mistyped value must never break a request. A rate limit of 0 or a page size of 5,000 typed into a record would otherwise reach every caller.

## Decision

1. **One generic type.** `Portfolio_Setting__mdt`, visibility Public, one record per value. `Number_Value__c` (Number 18,4) or `Text_Value__c` (Text 255) holds the value, `Min_Value__c` and `Max_Value__c` hold its safe range, and `Description__c` says in plain words what it controls and what is safe. The label is the setting's plain name.
2. **One accessor.** `PortfolioSettings.getInteger(developerName, fallback)`, `getDecimal(developerName, fallback)` and `getText(developerName, fallback)`. Each caller passes its old constant as the fallback, so the code still states the default.
3. **The range is checked on every read.** A record that is missing, holds no value, or holds a number outside its range returns the fallback. `getInteger` also returns it for a number too large for an Integer, and drops a fraction.
4. **One read per transaction.** `Portfolio_Setting__mdt.getAll()` once, kept in a static map. It runs no SOQL, so a reader adds nothing to a request's query count, including the rate check that runs before any data query.
5. **Behaviour unchanged on the day it ships.** 23 records ship, each with the value the code used before.
6. **Existing settings keep their place.** `Portfolio_Config__mdt.Token_Daily_Cap__c` still wins over `Token_Daily_Cap_Default` when set. `Cache_Cleanup_Settings__mdt` and `AI_Provider_Config__mdt` are not moved.
7. **Contract values stay in code.** Field lengths, enum and key strings, spec names and layout constants (graph geometry, image sizes, label lengths) are part of a contract or a layout, not operations, and stay as constants.

## Alternatives Considered

| Option                                       | Rejected because                                                                                          |
| :------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Keep the constants                           | Every number change is a code change and a full test run.                                                 |
| A field per value on `Portfolio_Config__mdt` | Each new value is a new field, and the config type would mix my details with operational limits.          |
| Hierarchy custom settings                    | Values are data, not metadata, so they do not deploy with the code to production or to CI's scratch orgs. |
| No range check                               | A typo such as a rate of 0 would reach every caller until someone noticed.                                |

## Rationale

- Custom metadata deploys with the code, so CI's scratch orgs and production start with the same values and need no data load.
- `getAll()` runs no SOQL (`PortfolioSettingsTest.recordsLoadOncePerTransaction`), so a setting costs nothing against the query limit.
- The fallback in code means a deleted record, a cleared value or a range mistake degrades to the known default instead of an error.
- The site guest reads a setting through Apex with no permission set (`PortfolioSettingsTest.siteGuestReadsASettingWithNoPermissionSet`).

## Implications

- Every record has a reader, and each reader keeps its constant as the fallback: `ApiRequestContext` (page sizes, rate tiers), `ApiLabController` (the site cover letter's AI tier), `TokenExchangeService`, `PAPIAiGenerate`, `PAPIHealth`, `CircuitBreaker`, `SubmissionGuard`, `SourceCacheRefreshJob`, `GovernanceController`, `DeliveryController` (the roadmap column count) and `ResumeController` (the timeline tab count). The list per record is in the [Technical Guide §1.6](../guides/04-Technical-Guide.md#16-operational-settings-portfolio_setting__mdt).
- A value changed in Setup takes effect on the next transaction. A full mode deploy writes every record in source, so the same value has to be committed to source or a later deploy can put the shipped one back ([Maintenance Guide §3.5](../guides/05-Maintenance-Guide.md#35-changing-an-operational-setting)).
- Two labels do not follow a changed value: the Delivery checklist reads "Org heartbeat today" and "Integration caches under 30 minutes old" from fixed text in `c/smartChecklist`, while `GovernanceController` applies the settings.
- The rate tiers of [ADR-025](025-papi-fan-out-throttling-capacity-planning.md) and the token rate and default cap of [ADR-028](028-evaluator-access-via-token-vending.md) are unchanged as decisions. Only where their numbers are kept has moved.

## Note (2026-10-24)

Content reads follow the same pattern in [ADR-033](033-queries-in-custom-metadata.md): a Public custom metadata type, the code's own value as the fallback, a record that fails a check ignored, and one `getAll()` per transaction. One difference: `Query_Definition__mdt` has long text fields, and `getAll()` returns only their first 255 characters, so a longer field list or filter is read again with one SOQL query. `Portfolio_Setting__mdt` has no long text field, so a setting still costs no query.

# ADR-033: Queries in Custom Metadata

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/QueryDefinitions.cls), also [QueryDefinitionsTest](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/QueryDefinitionsTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-24).

## Context

Every content read was SOQL written into its Apex class. Changing a field list, a filter or a sort order meant a code change, a test run and a deploy, even when the change only narrowed what a page or an API path returns.

I chose whole queries in metadata for every content read, not only the parts of a query that change often. That has a risk the settings in [ADR-032](032-operational-settings-in-custom-metadata.md) do not have. A query decides which records and which fields leave the org, and several of these reads serve the site guest or a public API path. An edit to a record must never be able to return a field the class does not return today, drop a condition such as `Approved__c = true`, or put text from a request into a query.

## Decision

1. **One record per read.** `Query_Definition__mdt`, visibility Public. `Object__c` (Text 80), `Fields__c` (Long Text 4000, a comma list, relationship paths allowed), `Filter__c` (Long Text 4000, a WHERE body that may use only named binds), `Order_By__c` (Text 255), `Row_Limit__c` (Number 6,0), `Access_Mode__c` (`USER_MODE` or `SYSTEM_MODE`), `Active__c` (default true) and `Description__c`. The DeveloperName is `Class_Purpose`, for example `SAPISkill_List`.
2. **The code keeps its own query.** The calling class builds a `QueryDefinitions.QueryDefault`: the object, fields, filter, order, limit and access mode it would run anyway, plus the allowlist of fields the read may ever return and the fields the caller reads. `QueryDefinitions.run`, `runPage` and `count` take the record's name, the bind values and that default.
3. **A record is used only when it is safe.** It must be active, read the same object, ask only for fields in the allowlist and keep every field the caller reads, name only binds the caller supplies, run in an access mode no weaker than the default's (`USER_MODE` stays `USER_MODE`), hold a row limit from 1 to 50000, have balanced brackets outside its quoted literals, and parse. Otherwise the default runs. A record that fails to parse is not tried again in the same transaction.
4. **A record can narrow a read and never widen it.** The record's filter is joined to the default's filter with AND, and the smaller of the two row limits applies. Request values travel only as bind values, so no text from a request is ever added to a query.
5. **Optional filters never change the record's text.** A filter the request may leave out is written as `(IsDeleted = :hasX OR Field = :x)`. The class binds `hasX` to false when the parameter is blank, which matches every row the query can return, and to true when it is set, which leaves only `Field = :x`. SOQL refuses a bind on the left of a comparison, so the test needs a real field, and `IsDeleted` is false on every row a query returns without ALL ROWS. A bind inside INCLUDES matches no row, so the persona filter on experience highlights is four literal INCLUDES clauses, one for each of Admin, Engineer, Architect and Consultant, each with its own switch (`adminOff`, `engineerOff`, `architectOff` and `consultantOff`): `(IsDeleted = :adminOff AND Persona_Tag__c INCLUDES ('Admin'))`. There is no Developer clause, because the API reads Developer as Engineer before it binds the switches.
6. **One load per transaction.** The records are read once with `getAll()` and kept in a static map. `getAll()` returns only the first 255 characters of a long text field, so every record whose field list or filter reaches 255 characters is read again in full, all of them in one SOQL query.
7. **A bad record fails CI.** A field named only in a metadata record is not protected by the compiler or by the platform's delete check. Each class that owns reads implements `QueryDefinitions.Provider` and returns its defaults by record name. `QueryDefinitions.validateAll()` finds every provider, checks every record against its default and runs each record that passes once with sample binds, and a test fails when it returns anything (`SAPIQueryDefinitionsTest.everyDeployedRecordPassesValidation`, `ApiQueryDefinitionsTest.everyApiRecordPassesValidation`, `SiteQueryDefinitionsTest.everyDeployedRecordPassesValidation`).
8. **Behaviour unchanged on the day it ships.** Each record ships equal to its code default, and a test compares them field by field (`everySapiRecordShipsEqualToItsDefault`, `everyApiRecordShipsEqualToItsDefault` and `everySiteRecordShipsEqualToItsDefault` in the three test classes).
9. **Plumbing stays in code.** Reads that are locks, counters or caches used as plumbing, and reads of custom metadata or setup objects, keep their SOQL. A rate window read `FOR UPDATE` (`RateWindowLimiter`) must not be editable as data.

## Alternatives Considered

| Option                                         | Rejected because                                                                                                       |
| :--------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Keep every query in code                       | Every field list or filter change is a code change and a full test run.                                                |
| Only the changeable parts in metadata          | I chose whole queries.                                                                                                 |
| A record replaces the code's query outright    | An edit could drop `Approved__c = true` or add a field the guest must not see, and nothing would catch it.             |
| One record per combination of optional filters | Certifications alone would need 8 records, and the class would pick a record by the request, which is harder to check. |
| Read records with SOQL every time              | Every content read would spend a query on its own definition.                                                          |

## Rationale

- The allowlist, the required fields and the access mode stay in the class, so the class still says what it reads and the most a record can do is return less.
- The default is the fallback for every fault, so a deleted record, a typo or a field later removed from the schema degrades to the known query instead of an error (`QueryDefinitionsTest.fieldOutsideTheAllowlistFallsBack`, `weakerModeFallsBack`, `bracketEscapeCannotWidenTheRead`, `badParseFallsBackAndIsNotRetried`).
- `getAll()` runs no SOQL for records under 255 characters (`QueryDefinitionsTest.shortTextNeedsNoQuery`), and the records load once per transaction (`recordsLoadOncePerTransaction`).
- The rate check still runs before any data query. A rejected request loads no record, because the records are read only when a read runs.

## Implications

- 27 classes read through `QueryDefinitions`, with 69 records. The 13 SAPI list classes have 14 (one list read each, plus `SAPIProject_Detail` for a single project). The Process API and the API Lab options have 27: `PAPIProfile`, `PAPIResume`, `PAPIProjects`, `PAPITestimonialFeed` and `ApiLabOptionsController`. Nine site classes have 28: `ResumeController`, `PortfolioGroundingService`, `ProjectCardController`, `GovernanceController`, `DeliveryController`, `SourceController`, `TestimonialController`, `SkillGraphController` and `PortfolioStatsController`, whose six reads each take an Id and at most one grouping field and are only counted. Each guest facing read keeps its sharing and access mode, and its allowlist is the fields the class returned before.
- A record's field list cannot safely hold a child subquery, because an edit could move a top level field inside it. So the three reads that used one, the profile and resume experiences in `PAPIProfile` and `PAPIResume` and the roles in `ResumeController`, are two reads each: the parents, then their highlights by parent Id in sort order, grouped in code. The rows, order and payload are the same (`ApiQueryDefinitionsTest`, `SiteQueryDefinitionsTest.theSplitRoleReadBuildsTheSameRolesAsOneSubqueryRead`), at the cost of one more SOQL query per request on those paths.
- `PortfolioAgentService` keeps all its reads in code. It serializes nested child lists exactly as they come back, a split read could only rebuild them through a JSON round trip, and no site path or API calls it.
- Plumbing stays coded: the rate window read `FOR UPDATE` (`RateWindowLimiter`), the counters in `SubmissionGuard` and `TokenExchangeService`, `CircuitBreaker`, the cache cleanup batches, `GovernanceEventHandler`, `ContactFormLeadWriter`, `LeadReminderService`, and every read of custom metadata or a setup object. `ApiLabController`, `PAPIHealth`, `FooterController`, `DecisionMatrixController` and `SourceCacheRefreshJob` hold no content read, so they did not change.
- Two records, `SAPIProject_List` and `SAPIExperienceHighlight_List`, have a filter of 255 characters or more, so `/sapi/v1/projects` and `/sapi/v1/experience-highlights` spend one more SOQL query per request. No other record reaches 255 characters.
- The totals for `/sapi/v1/skills`, `/sapi/v1/experience`, `/sapi/v1/projects` and `/sapi/v1/testimonials` ignored the request's filters when this record was first written. `X-Total-Count` on those four paths counted every row the read can return, while the page was filtered. That was kept on purpose so behaviour would not change on the day the reads moved into records, and the amendment of 2026-10-26 below changes it. The count runs through the same record, so a record that narrows the read narrows the total too.
- `contactName` on `/sapi/v1/experience` and `/sapi/v1/projects`, and `projectName` on `/sapi/v1/projects`, are now applied. The spec listed them before and the code ignored them.
- A record changed in Setup takes effect on the next transaction. A full mode deploy writes every record in source, so a change has to be committed to source or a later deploy puts the shipped one back, as with [ADR-032](032-operational-settings-in-custom-metadata.md).
- A new content read adds a `QueryDefault` in its class and a record equal to it, and the class implements `QueryDefinitions.Provider`. `validateAll()` then covers it with no other change.

## Amendment (2026-10-26): the totals follow the filters

`SAPISkill`, `SAPIExperience`, `SAPIProject` and `SAPITestimonial` now pass the request's binds to `QueryDefinitions.count`, as the other nine list classes already did. `X-Total-Count` on those four paths counts the rows that match the request's filters, so it equals the rows the pages add up to. A request with no filter still counts every row the read can return, and a record that narrows the read narrows the total too. The pagination headers, `X-Has-More` included, are unchanged, and the last page keeps the same total as the first. A request the rate limiter rejects still spends no query on a list, so the tests that pin exact query counts before the rate limit check are unchanged. The spec describes the header as the number of records that match the request.

# ADR-039: API v2 and the v1 Sunset

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/ApiVersionTest.cls), also [OpenApiDocument](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/OpenApiDocument.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-29), built and tested. In the integration scratch org `RunLocalTests` passed 1322 of 1322 with 97% org wide coverage, the existing SAPI and PAPI tests among them. A guest call to `/openapi?spec=sapi&version=v2` returned SAPI 2.0.0, `version=v1` returned 1.4.0, and `version=v9` returned 400. Both v1 dates ship blank, so nothing is deprecated or retired in production until I set them after the deploy.

## Context

[ADR-038](038-stable-public-keys-in-the-api.md) gave every record a stable `key` beside its `id` and said a v2 would remove `id` and each reference Id. The v1 SAPI spec also promised to drop the deprecated `accomplishments` HTML field in v2.0.0. [ADR-026](026-header-based-api-versioning-strategy.md) already chose the `X-API-Version` header over a version in the URL, and `ApiRequestContext` already reads it.

I decided that v2 is a breaking contract, selected by header, with keys only. v1 stays for one month so an evaluator can see both and a client has time to move, and then it answers 410.

## Decision

**The API serves two versions from the same URLs. `X-API-Version: v2` returns public keys only. A missing header is still v1, and v1 is deprecated for one month and then answers 410 Gone.**

- **Selection.** `ApiRequestContext.version()` returns `v1` or `v2` and `isV2()` is the shortcut. A missing header means v1. `v1` and `v2` are accepted in any letter case, so `V2` works, and anything else is a 400 "Unsupported X-API-Version". Every response carries `X-API-Version` in lower case with the version served, and `Vary: X-API-Version`. The version and sunset checks run before the rate limiter, so a request refused for an unsupported version or a 410 spends none of the rate limit quota.
- **The v2 shape.** For the record endpoints, `SAPITransformer.toV2` shapes a response body recursively. It drops `id`, drops each `xId` that has an `xKey` beside it, and drops `accomplishments`. `PAPITransformer.toV2` delegates to it, so both APIs shape the same way. The token, health, AI generate, resume generate and portfolio config bodies are not shaped (`UNSHAPED_PATHS`), because they are not lists of records. The v1 bodies are not touched, because v1 never calls `toV2`.
- **The v2 parameters.** The query parameters are `projectKey`, `experienceKey` and `certificationKey`, and each takes a public key only. A Salesforce Id there is a 400 "<parameter> must be a public key." The old `projectId`, `experienceId` or `certificationId` name sent with v2 is a 400 "Use projectKey in v2.", naming the new parameter. The `/projects/{id}` path keeps its name and takes a key in v2, and anything else is a 404. v1 keeps the old names and accepts an Id or a key, as ADR-038 built it.
- **The v1 headers.** Every v1 response carries `Deprecation` (RFC 9745, `@` and unix seconds) once a deprecation date is set, `Sunset` (RFC 8594, an HTTP date) once a sunset date is set, and `Link` with `rel="successor-version"` to `https://ryanbumstead.com/api-lab/reference?version=v2`, plus `rel="deprecation"` and `rel="sunset"` entries when those dates are set. The `Link` header is sent whether or not a date is set.
- **The 410.** From 00:00 UTC on the sunset date, every v1 call except the three below, including a call with no version header, is answered 410 in the existing error envelope with `errorCode` `GONE` and the message "API v1 has been retired. Send X-API-Version: v2. See https://ryanbumstead.com/api-lab/reference?version=v2". v2 never returns it. `GONE` is in the v1 SAPI `Error` enum. The three exceptions are `POST /papi/v1/auth/token`, `/sapi/v1/health` and `/papi/v1/health`. They keep their deprecation headers and are answered normally, so a client can still get a token and check that the API is up.
- **The dates are settings.** Two `Portfolio_Setting__mdt` records, `Api_V1_Deprecation_Date` and `Api_V1_Sunset_Date`, hold a `yyyy-MM-dd` date in **Text Value** and are read as 00:00 UTC. Blank sends no header and never answers 410, and a value that is not a date reads as blank. Both ship blank. I plan to set the sunset to the deploy date plus 30 days.
- **The specs.** `salesforce-sapi-v2.yaml` and `portfolio-papi-v2.yaml` at 2.0.0 sit beside the v1 files at 1.4.0, which are marked deprecated. `scripts/sync-specs.js` makes the YAML and JSON static resources for both, the API Lab catalog (which keeps `v1Params` and `v1Responses`) and the Postman collection, which is built from v2. `npm run specs:check` fails when a copy is stale.
- **The machine readable spec.** `OpenApiDocument` takes `version=v1|v2` beside `spec`, defaults to v2, answers 400 for an unknown version and 503 when the resource is missing. The v2 bodies are the `SAPI_OpenAPI_V2` and `PAPI_OpenAPI_V2` static resources.
- **The API Lab.** `ApiLabController.invokeVersioned(path, params, apiVersion)` sends the version the visitor picked and treats blank as v2. The older `invoke` stays and calls v1. The picker offers "v2" first and "v1 (deprecated)", the Lab sends the picked version's parameter names, and it shows `X-API-Version`, `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` in the response. The reference page opens v2 by default and honours `?version=v1|v2` beside `?spec=`. `ApiLabOptionsController.getOptions()` returns the same public key lists under the `*Id` names for v1 and the `*Key` names for v2.
- **The site's own calls.** The Agentforce cover letter call and the `PAPIHealth` self call send `X-API-Version: v2`, so the sunset cannot reach them.

## Alternatives considered

| Option                                     | Why not                                                                                                                         |
| :----------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A version in the URL path                  | ADR-026 chose the header. A path version would move every URL, spec path and Postman request.                                   |
| Keep v1 with no end date                   | A deprecation with no date does not move anyone. The `Sunset` header says when.                                                 |
| Remove v1 on the day v2 ships              | An evaluator holding a v1 call would break at once, and the Lab could not show the deprecation headers live.                    |
| A hard coded sunset date in Apex           | A date change would be a code change. A setting is a record deploy.                                                             |
| Answer a retired v1 with 404 or a redirect | 410 Gone says the resource existed and is gone for good, and the body names the v2 link.                                        |
| One spec file with both versions           | v1 would stop being documented as a whole. Separate files keep v1 readable for its last month and are deleted after the sunset. |

## Implications

- **A missing header is v1.** After the sunset a call with no `X-API-Version` also gets 410, except on the token and health paths, so a client has to send `v2`.
- **`Vary: X-API-Version` is sent on every response**, because the body differs by version. I added it for any cache in front. It and the `Link` header are appended to a value already set, not replaced. Whether a given cache honours it is not yet checked.
- **Both dates ship blank.** Until I set them, v1 carries only `X-API-Version`, `Vary` and the `Link` header, and nothing answers 410.
- **After the sunset** I delete the v1 spec files, the `V1_SPECS` list in `scripts/sync-specs.js`, the `SAPI_Spec`, `PAPI_Spec`, `SAPI_OpenAPI` and `PAPI_OpenAPI` static resources, the v1 option in the API Lab and API reference pickers, and the v1 mapping in `OpenApiDocument`. The Maintenance Guide lists the steps.
- **ADR-038 is carried out.** Its note that a v2 would remove `id` and each reference Id is what `toV2` does.
- **Not part of this decision.** The site's own LWC components do not read the API responses and are not changed.

## Amendment (2026-10-31)

[ADR-040](040-versionless-api-urls.md) removed the `/v1/` segment from the URLs the API is called at. The old `/v1/` URLs stay as aliases until a date I set, with their own two settings. The behaviour in this ADR is unchanged for every path, old and new: the exceptions are now matched on the versionless path, so each one covers both spellings. The alternatives table above rejected a version in the URL path, and that still holds. The URL now names the resource and the header names the version.

## Amendment (2026-10-31): the v1 dates are set

The dates no longer ship blank. On 2026-10-29 I set `Api_V1_Deprecation_Date` to 2026-10-30 and `Api_V1_Sunset_Date` to 2026-11-29, so v1 responses carry `Deprecation` and `Sunset`, and from 2026-11-29 v1 answers 410 except on the three paths listed above. The "Both dates ship blank" line under Implications describes the state when this ADR was accepted.

# ADR-038: Stable Public Keys in the API

## Status

- **Decision:** Accepted
- **Build:** [Live](../../packages/portfolio-site/main/default/classes/PublicKeyServiceTest.cls), also [SAPIPublicKeyTest](../../packages/integration-api/main/default/classes/SAPIPublicKeyTest.cls)

Accepted (2026-10-28), built and tested. In a scratch org `PublicKeyServiceTest`, `SAPIPublicKeyTest` and `PAPIPublicKeyTest` passed 55 of 55, and every local test, the existing SAPI and PAPI tests among them, passed 1292 of 1292. Rows that existed before the field get their keys when `scripts/backfill-public-keys.apex` runs once in production.

## Context

A reviewer noted that the API returns Salesforce record Ids. It is not a security problem. The API runs as a read only integration user, tokens are scoped, and an Id grants nothing by itself. It is a design smell all the same. A public API should expose keys it controls, not the internal row Ids of the system behind it. An Id ties every client to Salesforce, changes when a record is deleted and recreated in another org, and shows a reader the platform and the object from its first three characters.

I chose an additive change to v1, not a break. Nothing is removed. Removal would be v2.

## Decision

**Every object the API exposes gets a stable `Public_Key__c`. The API returns it beside `id`, accepts it anywhere an Id is accepted, and the specs mark `id` as deprecated.**

- **Field.** `Public_Key__c` on 13 objects. Text(24), External ID, unique, case insensitive, not required at the field level, because rows that existed before the field get their key from the backfill.
- **Format.** An object prefix, an underscore and 10 random characters from `abcdefghijkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789`. The alphabet leaves out `l`, `o`, `0` and `1`, which are easy to misread. A key is 14 characters, for example `prj_8f3k2m9qtz`. It is opaque on purpose. It never encodes a name, so renaming a record never changes it and no personal detail leaks. The 10 characters carry 50 bits, so a collision is rare, and the unique index backs the check.
- **Prefixes.**

| Object                    | Prefix | Object                   | Prefix |
| :------------------------ | :----- | :----------------------- | :----- |
| `Account`                 | `acc`  | `Project_Asset__c`       | `pas`  |
| `Contact`                 | `con`  | `Project_Skill__c`       | `prs`  |
| `Skill__c`                | `skl`  | `Certification__c`       | `crt`  |
| `Experience__c`           | `exp`  | `Certification_Skill__c` | `cks`  |
| `Experience_Highlight__c` | `hlt`  | `Education__c`           | `edu`  |
| `Experience_Skill__c`     | `exs`  | `Testimonial__c`         | `tst`  |
| `Project__c`              | `prj`  |                          |        |

- **Assignment.** `PublicKeyService.assign` fills any blank key before insert. It draws a key, checks the draw against stored rows and the rest of the batch with one query, and draws again for each clash, up to five times, then raises `PublicKeyException`. A key a record arrives with is kept. `PublicKeyService.refuseChange` runs on update and adds an error when an existing key is changed or cleared, with the case compared exactly. Setting a key on a row that had none is allowed, which is how the backfill works. None of the 13 objects had a trigger, so each got one minimal trigger named `<Object>PublicKeyTrigger` that does nothing but call the service.
- **Existing rows.** `scripts/backfill-public-keys.apex` fills blank keys in batches of 200 and says how many rows remain. I run it once against production after the deploy. Writing to production data is mine.
- **API.** Every SAPI and PAPI object that carried `id` also carries `key`. Every reference carries its own pair: `projectKey`, `experienceKey`, `skillKey`, `certificationKey`, `contactKey`, `employerKey` and `issuerKey`. Each query parameter that took an Id (`projectId`, `experienceId`, `certificationId`) and the `/projects/{id}` path segment now take an Id or a key. A value that is a Salesforce Id is used as before. A value shaped like a key is looked up on that object, and a key with no record matches no rows, the way an Id with no record does. Anything else is a `400 BAD_REQUEST` on the three parameters. The path keeps its old behaviour for such a value, a `404`.
- **Query definitions.** The key fields are added to the code defaults and to the matching `Query_Definition__mdt` records together, so each record still ships equal to its default.
- **Specs.** Both specs move to 1.4.0, gain `key` and the reference keys, and mark `id` and each reference Id `deprecated: true` with a description that points at the key.

## Alternatives considered

| Option                                               | Why not                                                                                                                             |
| :--------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Replace `id` with `key` in v1                        | It breaks every client that stores an Id. I chose the additive path.                                                                |
| Use the record Name or a slug                        | A rename would change the key, and names carry personal detail. Names are not unique on every object.                               |
| Use `Auto Number` or a sequence                      | It tells a reader how many records exist and in what order. It is guessable.                                                        |
| Use a UUID                                           | 36 characters is long for a URL, and it carries no hint of the object. The prefix makes a mistyped or misplaced key easy to spot.   |
| Fill the key in a Flow                               | A trigger can check a draw against the stored rows and the batch and redraw in one place, and the same service serves the backfill. |
| Add new `projectKey` style parameters beside the old | Two parameters for one meaning. The existing parameter takes both forms without a change to any client.                             |

## Implications

- **Deprecation, not removal.** `id` and the reference Ids stay in every v1 response and stay accepted. A client should move to `key`. A v2 would remove `id` and `xId` from the responses and the schemas, accept only keys in the parameters, make the field required, and drop the Id branch from `SAPITransformer.resolveReference`.
- **Keys are blank until the backfill runs.** Between the deploy and the backfill, an old row returns `key: null`. The new rows are keyed from their first insert. Run the backfill straight after the deploy.
- **A key is permanent.** Deleting and recreating a record makes a new key. The seed data plans in `data/**` create rows through the import, so the trigger keys them. A reseed after a delete gives new keys.
- **The path `/projects/{id}` is not in the spec.** The Apex serves it and has always done so. It takes a key now. Adding it to the spec is a separate change.
- **One more query per insert transaction.** The collision check reads the stored keys once per object per attempt. A bulk insert of 251 rows costs the same one query.
- **Field access.** `Integration_Access` reads the new fields and `Portfolio_Admin` edits them. `Portfolio_Guest` is not changed in this decision.
- **Not part of this decision.** The site's LWC components do not read the API responses and are not changed.
